units.title: Başlık sorusu
units.description: Fen metinleri: metnin tamamını kapsayan başlığı seç
units.guide:
## Strateji
"Which of the following is the best title for the passage?" sorusunda doğru başlık metnin tamamını kapsar; ne çok dar ne çok geniştir. Yanlış başlıklar çoğu zaman üç tuzaktan birine düşer: yalnızca bir paragraftaki ayrıntıyı anlatır (*dar*), konunun çok ötesine geçer (*geniş*) ya da metindeki sözcükleri kullanıp yanlış bir iddia kurar (*çarpıtma*).

## Nasıl uygulanır
1. Her paragrafa 2–3 kelimelik bir etiket ver: ilk ve son cümleye bak.
2. Etiketleri birleştir ve "konu + yazarın söylediği" biçiminde tek bir cümle kur.
3. Her başlığı bu cümleyle karşılaştır; yalnızca bir paragrafı kapsayanı ele.
4. *only, always, finally, proved* gibi kesin sözcükler taşıyan başlıklara dikkat et; metin çekinceliyse (*may, about*) bu başlıklar genellikle yanlıştır.
5. Kalan iki başlıktan son paragrafla da uyuşanı seç.

## Örnek
*Aerogel is extremely light. It blocks heat and has been used on Mars rovers. However, it is fragile and expensive.*
- "Aerogel on Mars" → dar: yalnızca bir ayrıntı.
- "The Lightest Materials in History" → geniş: metin tarih anlatmıyor.
- "Aerogel: Useful but Still Costly" → üç cümleyi de kapsıyor, **doğru**.

## Sınav ipucu
Başlık sorusunu en sona bırak: diğer soruları çözerken metnin bütününü zaten görmüş olursun. Başlık iki parçalıysa (*X: Y*), iki parçanın da metinde karşılığı olmalı.

exercises.question: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?
options: Why Total Eclipses Are Dangerous to Watch
The Life and Career of Albert Einstein
How Radio Telescopes Replaced Photography
Bending Starlight: The Eclipse That Tested Einstein
The Discovery of Invisible Matter in Distant Galaxies
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Bending Starlight: The Eclipse That Tested Einstein’: metin baştan sona 1919 tutulmasında ışığın sapmasının nasıl ölçüldüğünü anlatıyor. ‘Dangerous’ tutulmanın tehlikesi metinde yok. ‘Career’ çok geniş; metin Einstein’ın hayatını anlatmıyor. ‘Radio’ teleskoplar yalnızca son paragrafta geçen bir ayrıntı. ‘Invisible’ madde de son cümledeki dar bir ayrıntı.
exercises.passage:
In 1919, two teams of British astronomers travelled to distant locations to observe a total eclipse of the Sun, an event in which the Moon briefly blocks its light. Their mission was to test a bold prediction that Albert Einstein had made a few years earlier. According to his general theory of relativity, gravity is not simply a force between objects but a curve in space and time, which means that even light should bend as it passes a massive body.

The test was straightforward in theory but difficult in practice. Stars that lie close to the Sun cannot normally be seen, because its light is far too bright. During an eclipse, however, they become visible for a few minutes, and their positions can be recorded on photographic plates. These images were compared with photographs of the same stars taken months later at night, when the Sun was in a different part of the sky.

The researchers began from a null hypothesis: if gravity had no effect on light, the stars would appear in exactly their usual positions. Instead, a small deflection was measured, roughly equal to the value that Einstein's equations predicted and about twice the value expected from older physics. The results were announced in London later that year and quickly made Einstein famous around the world.

Modern historians have noted that the measurements were far from perfect, since cloud, heat and the limited accuracy of the instruments introduced considerable uncertainty. Nevertheless, later observations with radio telescopes have confirmed the effect with much greater precision. Today the deflection of light by gravity, now called gravitational lensing, is commonly used as a tool to study distant galaxies and to estimate the amount of invisible matter in the universe.

exercises.question: According to the passage, stars close to the Sun could be photographed during the eclipse because ----.
options: the astronomers used radio telescopes instead of cameras
the Moon blocked the bright light of the Sun for a few minutes
gravity made the stars appear much brighter than usual
the Sun had moved to a different part of the sky
the stars were photographed again months later at night
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the Moon blocked the bright light of the Sun for a few minutes’: 1. ve 2. paragraf Ay’ın ışığı kısa süre kapattığını, yıldızların ancak o zaman görünür olduğunu söylüyor. ‘radio’ teleskoplar çok sonraki gözlemlerdir. ‘brighter’ metinde yok; yerçekimi ışığı büker, parlatmaz. ‘moved’ Güneş’in başka yerde olması karşılaştırma fotoğraflarının koşuludur. ‘again’ geceki fotoğraflar karşılaştırma içindir, tutulmanın nedeni değil.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the most suitable title for the passage?
options: The History of Steel Production
Why Nitinol Replaced Surgery in Modern Hospitals
How Atoms Melt at High Temperatures
Cheap Materials for Everyday Products
Metals That Remember: Uses and Limits of Shape-Memory Alloys
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Metals That Remember: Uses and Limits of Shape-Memory Alloys’: metin bu alaşımların nasıl çalıştığını, nerede kullanıldığını ve sakıncalarını anlatıyor. ‘Steel’ yalnızca karşılaştırma için geçiyor. ‘Replaced’ abartı; metin büyük ameliyat ihtiyacının azaldığını söylüyor. ‘Melt’ ters: dönüşüm erimeden gerçekleşiyor. ‘Cheap’ ters: alaşımlar çelikten pahalı.
exercises.passage:
Most metals behave in a predictable way: if you bend a steel wire, it stays bent. A group of materials known as shape-memory alloys, however, can return to their original form when they are heated. The best-known example is nitinol, a mixture of nickel and titanium that was developed at a US naval laboratory in the early 1960s. Its unusual capability was reportedly discovered by accident, when a bent sample recovered its shape after being warmed.

The explanation lies in the arrangement of atoms inside the metal. At lower temperatures, the atoms are organised in a structure which allows the material to change its shape easily. When the temperature rises above a certain point, the atoms move back into a different, more stable pattern, and the object returns to the shape it was given during manufacture. This transformation happens without melting, and it can be repeated many thousands of times.

Because of these properties, shape-memory alloys have found a wide range of applications. In medicine, small tubes called stents are inserted into narrow blood vessels in a compact form and then expand at body temperature, which reduces the need for major surgery. Dental wires made of nitinol apply a gentle, constant force to teeth, so patients need fewer adjustments. Engineers have also used the alloys in aircraft parts, valves and sensors that react to heat without any motor.

The materials are not without disadvantages. They are considerably more expensive than ordinary steel, and repeated cycles of heating and cooling can gradually reduce their performance. Researchers are therefore experimenting with new combinations of metals that could be cheaper and more reliable. If these efforts succeed, the technology may become far more common in everyday products.

exercises.question: According to the passage, stents made of shape-memory alloys ----.
options: are melted before being placed in blood vessels
expand when they reach body temperature
apply a constant force to the teeth
are cheaper than ordinary steel tubes

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘expand when they reach body temperature’: 3. paragraf stentlerin küçük hâlde yerleştirildiğini ve vücut ısısında genişlediğini söylüyor. ‘melted’ metinde erime yok. ‘teeth’ dişlere kuvvet uygulayan diş telleridir. ‘cheaper’ ters; alaşımlar pahalı. ‘motor’ ters; sensörler motorsuz çalışıyor.

nodes.description: Metin 1: Görünmez parçacıkları yerin altında yakalamak. Metin 2: Dünyanın en hafif katı maddesi. ys7 kelimeleri: contradiction, existence, core, mystery, interact, contribute, disturb, oscillation ve 17 kelime daha.

exercises.question: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?
options: How Cosmic Rays Damage Underground Mines
Wolfgang Pauli and the Birth of Atomic Physics
Why Water Is the Purest Substance on Earth
The End of Neutrino Research
Catching Ghostly Particles: The Search for Neutrinos
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Catching Ghostly Particles: The Search for Neutrinos’: metin nötrinoların ne olduğunu, nasıl yakalandığını ve neden önemli olduğunu anlatıyor. ‘Mines’ dar ve yanlış; madenler dedektörün yeridir. ‘Pauli’ yalnızca 1. paragraftaki bir ayrıntı. ‘Purest’ metinde böyle bir iddia yok. ‘End’ ters; son paragraf yeni dedektörlerden söz ediyor.
exercises.passage:
Every second, tens of billions of tiny particles called neutrinos pass through your body, yet you never notice them. Neutrinos are produced in enormous numbers by nuclear reactions in the Sun, and they interact so weakly with ordinary matter that most of them travel straight through the entire Earth. Their existence was first proposed in 1930 by the physicist Wolfgang Pauli, who needed them to explain why some energy seemed to be missing in certain atomic processes.

Detecting such shy particles requires enormous patience and unusual equipment. Because laboratories on the surface are disturbed by cosmic rays, detectors are usually built deep underground, in mines or beneath mountains, where the rock acts as natural protection. One famous Japanese detector, Super-Kamiokande, consists of a huge container holding about fifty thousand tons of extremely pure water, surrounded by thousands of light sensors. On the rare occasions when a neutrino strikes a particle in the water, a faint flash of blue light is produced and recorded.

For decades, such experiments revealed a puzzling contradiction: only about a third of the neutrinos predicted by models of the Sun were actually observed. The mystery was eventually solved when researchers demonstrated that neutrinos change from one type into another during their journey, a phenomenon known as oscillation. This finding, which implied that neutrinos must have a small mass, contributed to Nobel Prizes in 2002 and 2015.

Neutrino research has practical value as well. Because the particles escape from the core of the Sun almost immediately, they offer a direct view of processes that light cannot reveal. Scientists also hope that future detectors will help them understand why the universe contains far more matter than antimatter, which remains one of the major unanswered questions in physics.

exercises.question: According to the passage, neutrino detectors are built deep underground because ----.
options: the rock protects them from disturbance by cosmic rays
neutrinos cannot travel through the surface of the Earth
pure water can only be found in mines
the light of the Sun would destroy the sensors
underground tanks are cheaper to build
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the rock protects them from disturbance by cosmic rays’: 2. paragraf yüzeydeki laboratuvarların kozmik ışınlardan etkilendiğini, kayanın doğal koruma sağladığını söylüyor. ‘surface’ ters; nötrinolar Dünya’nın içinden bile geçiyor. ‘pure’ suyun madenlerde bulunduğu söylenmiyor. ‘destroy’ metinde yok. ‘cheaper’ maliyetten söz edilmiyor.

exercises.passage:
Aerogel is often described as the lightest solid material ever made. It is produced by taking a gel, similar to the kind used to make jelly, and carefully removing the liquid so that only a delicate network of solid remains. Because up to about 99 percent of its volume is air, a block the size of a brick can weigh less than a small bar of chocolate, and some samples look like frozen smoke.

The first aerogels were created around 1931 by the American chemist Samuel Kistler, who reportedly wanted to show that the solid structure of a gel could survive without its liquid. His method, which involved heating the liquid under high pressure, was slow and expensive, and for several decades the material remained little more than a laboratory curiosity.

Interest revived when scientists realised how poorly aerogel conducts heat. Since the tiny holes block the movement of warm air, a thin layer can protect objects from extreme temperatures, and the material has been used to insulate equipment on Mars rovers. NASA's Stardust mission, launched in 1999, also relied on aerogel to capture dust from a comet. Particles travelling at several kilometres per second were gradually slowed down inside the material instead of being destroyed on impact, and they were later returned to Earth for analysis.

Despite these achievements, the substance has important limitations. Traditional aerogels made of silica are fragile and can break into powder when pressed, which makes them difficult to handle. Production also remains costly, although newer, more flexible versions based on plastics or carbon are being developed. Engineers now see potential uses in building insulation, outdoor clothing and the clean-up of oil spills, where the large internal surface of the material can absorb oil. Whether aerogel will ever become cheap enough for everyday use, however, remains uncertain.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Watching Stars Dim: How Distant Planets Are Found’: metnin merkezinde yıldız ışığındaki düşüşü izleyen geçiş yöntemi var. ‘Mars’ metinde geçmiyor; İsviçreli bilim insanları ötegezegen buldu. ‘Cannot’ ters; araştırmacılar yaşam izi arıyor. ‘Last’ Kepler yalnızca bir örnek. ‘Directly’ ters; metin doğrudan görmenin çok zor olduğunu söylüyor.
exercises.passage:
Until the 1990s, astronomers could only guess whether planets existed around stars other than the Sun. The first confirmed discovery around a Sun-like star was announced in 1995 by two Swiss researchers, Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz, who later received the Nobel Prize for their work. Since then, more than five thousand such worlds, known as exoplanets, have been identified, and the number continues to rise.

Exoplanets are extremely difficult to see directly, because they are faint and lie very close to stars that are millions of times brighter. Astronomers therefore rely mainly on indirect methods. The most productive of these is the transit method, whereby a telescope monitors the brightness of a star over a long period. When a planet passes in front of its star, it blocks a small fraction of the light, and the star appears to fade slightly. If this dip is repeated at regular intervals, it is likely to be caused by an orbiting planet rather than by random variability.

The size of the dip indicates the diameter of the planet, while the time between dips reveals the length of its year. NASA's Kepler space telescope, which observed a single region of the sky for about four years, used this approach to find thousands of candidates. Its results suggested that small, rocky planets are far more common than many scientists had assumed.

The method does have limitations. A transit can only be detected if the orbit is lined up with our view from Earth, so most planets are inevitably missed. Measurements must also be confirmed by other techniques to rule out false signals. Nevertheless, by combining several approaches, researchers hope to find planets with conditions comparable to those on Earth and, eventually, to examine their atmospheres for signs of life.

options: Zero Resistance: The Promise and Limits of Superconductors
How Copper Cables Are Made
The Discovery of Liquid Helium
Why Hospital Scanners Are Dangerous
Room-Temperature Superconductors Finally Confirmed
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Zero Resistance: The Promise and Limits of Superconductors’: metin direncin kaybolmasını, kullanım alanlarını ve sıcaklık engelini anlatıyor. ‘Copper’ yalnızca giriş örneği. ‘Helium’ soğutma için kullanılan bir madde, konu değil. ‘Dangerous’ metinde tarayıcıların tehlikesinden söz edilmiyor. ‘Finally’ ters; oda sıcaklığı iddiaları doğrulanmadı.
exercises.passage:
When electricity flows through an ordinary copper cable, some energy is always lost as heat because the moving electrons collide with the atoms of the metal. In 1911, however, the Dutch physicist Heike Kamerlingh Onnes made a surprising observation. After cooling mercury to about minus 269 degrees Celsius, he found that its electrical resistance suddenly disappeared. This phenomenon, which is now called superconductivity, means that a current can circulate in a closed loop for years without any measurable loss.

Superconductors have another remarkable property: they push magnetic fields out of their interior. As a result, a small magnet placed above a cooled superconductor can float in the air, a demonstration that is frequently shown in science classes. The same principle has been applied in experimental high-speed trains, which float above the rails and therefore experience almost no friction.

The greatest barrier to wider use is temperature. Early superconductors only worked when they were cooled with liquid helium, which is rare and expensive. In 1986 a new family of ceramic materials was discovered that remained superconducting at considerably higher temperatures, cold enough to be maintained with cheaper liquid nitrogen. This breakthrough prompted enormous excitement, and its discoverers received a Nobel Prize just a year later.

Today superconducting magnets are essential parts of hospital MRI scanners and of particle accelerators such as the Large Hadron Collider. Engineers would like to use the materials in power lines as well, since they could transmit electricity with minimal waste. Several research groups have claimed to find superconductors that work at room temperature, but none of these claims has so far been verified by independent laboratories. Many physicists therefore remain sceptical, while the search continues.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘This phenomenon, which is now called superconductivity, means that a current can circulate in a closed loop for years without any measurable loss.’
options: means
is now called
can circulate
closed
measurable
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘means’. İskelet: This phenomenon (özne) + means (ana fiil) + that… (nesne cümlesi). ‘is now called’ virgüllerle ayrılan which ara cümlesinin fiilidir. ‘can circulate’ that ile başlayan nesne cümlesinin fiilidir. ‘closed’ loop sözcüğünü niteleyen ortaçtır. ‘measurable’ bir sıfattır.

exercises.question: Cümledeki ‘which’ neyi nitelemektedir? ‘NASA’s Kepler space telescope, which observed a single region of the sky for about four years, used this approach to find thousands of candidates.’

NASA’s Kepler space telescope
the sky
this approach
thousands of candidates
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘NASA’s Kepler space telescope’: virgüllerle ayrılan ara cümle hemen önündeki isme bağlanır; gökyüzünü dört yıl gözleyen teleskoptur. ‘a single region’ ve ‘the sky’ yan cümlenin içindeki nesnelerdir. ‘this approach’ ana fiilin (used) nesnesidir. ‘thousands of candidates’ cümlenin sonunda kalır.

options: Bu düşüş düzenli aralıklarla tekrarlanırsa, kesinlikle yörüngede dönen bir gezegenden kaynaklanır.

Bu düşüş düzenli aralıklarla tekrarlanırsa, büyük olasılıkla yıldızın kendisinden kaynaklanır.
Bu düşüş düzenli aralıklarla tekrarlanırsa, rastgele değişkenlikten çok yörüngede dönen bir gezegenden kaynaklanıyor olması muhtemeldir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘The mystery was eventually solved when researchers demonstrated that neutrinos change from one type into another during their journey.’

Araştırmacılar gizemi çözmek için nötrinoları başka türlere dönüştürmeyi denedi.

Gizem, sonunda araştırmacılar nötrinoların yolculukları sırasında bir türden diğerine dönüştüğünü gösterdiğinde çözüldü.
Gizem, belki bir gün araştırmacılar nötrinoların tür değiştirdiğini gösterirse çözülecek.

Birkaç araştırma grubu oda sıcaklığında çalışan süperiletkenler bulmayı planlıyor.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Whether aerogel will ever become cheap enough for everyday use, however, remains uncertain.’
options: Aerojel günlük kullanım için kesinlikle ucuzlayacak.
Ancak aerojelin günlük kullanım için yeterince ucuz hâle gelip gelmeyeceği belirsizliğini koruyor.
Aerojelin artık günlük kullanımda yeterince ucuz olduğu biliniyor.
Aerojel pahalı olduğu için günlük kullanımda hiç yer almayacak.
Aerojelin ucuzlaması belirsiz değildir, çünkü üretim kolaylaştı.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘…ucuz hâle gelip gelmeyeceği belirsizliğini koruyor’. exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Storms from the Sun: Auroras and the Risks of Space Weather’: metin güneş rüzgârını, kutup ışıklarını ve güneş fırtınalarının risklerini birlikte anlatıyor. ‘Telegraph’ yalnızca 1859 örneğinde geçiyor. ‘Norway’ ışıkların görüldüğü yerlerden biri; dar ve konu dışı. ‘Cooling’ metinde çekirdeğin soğuduğu söylenmiyor. ‘Control’ ters; uydular Güneş’i izliyor, havayı denetlemiyor.
exercises.passage:
The Sun does not only send light and heat towards the Earth. It also releases a constant stream of charged particles, known as the solar wind, which travels through space at several hundred kilometres per second. Most of these particles never reach the ground, because they are pushed aside by the magnetic field of the Earth, an invisible shield that is generated by the motion of liquid iron deep inside the planet.

Near the poles, however, the field lines bend towards the surface, and some particles are able to enter the upper atmosphere. There they collide with atoms of oxygen and nitrogen, which release energy in the form of light. The result is the aurora, the moving curtains of green, red and purple light that are commonly seen in places such as Norway, Canada and Alaska. The colour depends on the type of gas and on the altitude at which the collisions take place.

From time to time the Sun produces much more violent events, including huge explosions on its surface and massive clouds of material thrown into space. When such a cloud strikes the Earth, it can trigger a magnetic storm. In 1859, a powerful storm of this kind caused telegraph systems in Europe and North America to fail, and auroras were reported as far south as the Caribbean. A storm of similar intensity today could damage satellites, interfere with radio communication and disrupt electricity networks over large areas.

For this reason, space weather is now monitored by several government agencies, which use satellites to watch the Sun continuously. Their warnings give power companies and satellite operators a few hours to take protective measures. Forecasting remains imperfect, though, and researchers are still trying to improve their estimation of when and where a storm will arrive.

exercises.question: According to the passage, the colour of an aurora depends on ----.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the type of gas and the altitude of the collisions’: 2. paragrafın son cümlesi bunu açıkça söylüyor. ‘alone’ hız renk için verilmiyor ve ‘alone’ tek nedeni dışlıyor. ‘country’ ülkeler yalnızca görüldüğü yerler. ‘liquid’ demir manyetik alanı üretir, rengi değil. ‘year’ mevsim metinde geçmiyor.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the most suitable title for the passage?

The End of Cement Production
Concrete That Repairs Itself
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Concrete That Repairs Itself’: metin çatlakları kendiliğinden kapatan betonu, yöntemlerini ve sınırlılıklarını anlatıyor. ‘Collapse’ metinde köprülerin çöktüğü söylenmiyor. ‘Tunnels’ yalnızca hasar örneği. ‘Threat’ ters; bakteriler çözümün parçası. ‘Cement’ üretiminin sona erdiği söylenmiyor.
exercises.passage:
Concrete is the most widely used building material in the world, yet it has a well-known weakness: it cracks. Small cracks may seem harmless at first, but they allow water and chemicals to enter the structure, where they can attack the steel bars inside and gradually weaken bridges, tunnels and buildings. Repairing this damage is costly, and inspections of large structures often require roads to be closed for long periods.

One promising solution has been developed by researchers in the Netherlands, who added bacteria to the concrete mixture. The microbes, which belong to species that can survive in extremely dry conditions, are mixed into the concrete together with a source of food. They remain inactive, sometimes for years, until a crack forms and water gets in. The moisture activates the bacteria, which then consume the food and produce limestone, a mineral that gradually fills the gap.

Laboratory experiments have shown that cracks up to roughly a millimetre wide can be sealed in this way within a few weeks. Other teams are testing alternative approaches, such as tiny capsules containing glue that break open when a crack passes through them, or special fibres that help the material close its own gaps.

The technology is not yet widely adopted, mainly because it raises the initial cost of construction. Supporters argue that this extra expense would be recovered over time, since self-healing structures could last longer and need less maintenance. There is also an environmental argument: the production of cement is responsible for a large share of global carbon dioxide emissions, so concrete that endures longer could indirectly reduce pollution. However, long-term data from real buildings are still limited, and engineers want stronger evidence before they rely on the method.

units.title: Çıkarım
units.description: Sağlık metinleri: metinde yazmayanı metinden çıkar
units.guide:
## Strateji
"It can be inferred from the passage that ----" sorusunda doğru şık metinde aynen yazmaz, ama metindeki bilgiden zorunlu olarak çıkar. Çıkarım tahmin değildir: şıkkı destekleyen cümleyi metinde gösterebilmelisin. Yanlış şıklar genellikle metni abartır, metinde olmayan bir bilgi ekler ya da metnin tersini söyler.

## Nasıl uygulanır
1. Soru bir paragraf ya da konu veriyorsa önce o kısmı yeniden oku.
2. Her şık için sor: "Bunu destekleyen cümle hangisi?" Gösteremiyorsan ele.
3. *always, never, all, only, certainly* gibi kesin sözcükler taşıyan şıklara şüpheyle bak; metin *may, suggest, about* diyorsa bunlar çoğu zaman yanlıştır.
4. Doğru şık sık sık metindeki iki bilgiyi birleştirir ya da temkinli bir dil kullanır (*may, not necessarily*).
5. Genel bilgini katma; yalnızca metne dayan.

## Örnek
*Parents were told to avoid peanuts. During the same period, peanut allergy rose sharply.*
- "The advice may have contributed to the rise." → iki cümleyi birleştiriyor, **doğru çıkarım**.
- "Peanuts cause all allergies." → abartı.
- "Parents ignored the advice." → metinde yok.

## Sınav ipucu
Çıkarım sorusunda en "akıllıca" görünen şık değil, metne en yakın duran şık doğrudur. İki şık arasında kaldıysan daha temkinli olanı seç ve onu destekleyen cümlenin altını çiz.

options: Peanuts are dangerous for all babies and should be avoided until school age.

Jewish families in Israel eat more peanuts than any other group.
Allergies to eggs have been cured thanks to the LEAP trial.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Research showed that giving peanut foods early can prevent allergy…’: metin eski tavsiyeden yeni araştırmaya ve değişen yönergelere uzanıyor. ‘dangerous’ eski ve çürütülen tavsiyedir. ‘equally’ ters; İngiltere’de oran yaklaşık on kat yüksek. ‘other’ gruplarla karşılaştırma yapılmıyor. ‘eggs’ için sonuçlar henüz net değil.
exercises.passage:
For many years, parents in several countries were advised to keep peanuts away from young children, especially if the family had a history of allergies. The logic seemed plausible: if a child never encountered a food, the immune system would have no chance to react against it. Yet during the same period, the number of children with peanut allergy rose sharply in many Western countries, which made it evident that the advice was not working.

An important clue came from a comparison between Jewish children living in the United Kingdom and those living in Israel. Researchers noticed that peanut allergy was roughly ten times more common in the British group. One obvious difference was diet: in Israel, peanut snacks are commonly given to babies within their first year, whereas British babies rarely ate them.

To test whether early exposure could build tolerance, a large clinical trial known as LEAP was conducted in London. About six hundred babies who were considered at high risk were randomly divided into two groups. One group regularly ate foods containing peanut from the age of a few months, while the other avoided them completely until the age of five. The results, published in 2015, were striking and prompted a rapid change of advice. Among the children who avoided peanuts, roughly 17 percent developed an allergy, compared with about 3 percent in the group that ate them.

In line with this evidence, medical guidelines in several countries were revised, and parents are now often encouraged to introduce peanut products early, usually in a soft or smooth form that cannot cause choking. Experts stress, however, that babies with severe skin problems or existing allergies should be assessed by a doctor first. Researchers are also investigating whether the same approach could reduce allergies to other foods, such as eggs, although the results so far are less clear.

options: all the babies ate peanut foods from a few months of age

the children were followed only until their first birthday

parents chose which group their babies joined

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the eight-glasses rule is not a reliable guide…’: metin kuralın sağlam bir temeli olmadığını ve ihtiyacın kişiden kişiye değiştiğini savunuyor. ‘plain’ ters; suyun büyük kısmı yiyeceklerden de gelebilir. ‘serious’ ters; ölçülü kahve kayda değer kayıp yaratmıyor. ‘never’ abartı; metin yalnızca aşırı içmenin riskini anlatıyor. ‘hardly’ ters; meyve ve sebzeler çoğunlukla sudur.
exercises.passage:
The advice that everyone should drink eight glasses of water a day is repeated so often that most people take it for granted. Surprisingly, it is difficult to find a clear scientific foundation for this rule. Some historians trace it back to a 1945 recommendation in the United States, which stated that adults need about 2.5 litres of water daily. The same document added that most of this amount is contained in prepared foods, but this second sentence was largely forgotten.

In reality, a considerable share of our water comes from what we eat. Fruit and vegetables such as watermelon, cucumber and oranges consist mostly of water, and even bread and meat contain some, while tea, coffee and milk also count. Coffee was long believed to dry out the body, but studies have found that moderate amounts do not cause any meaningful fluid loss in regular drinkers.

The body is also remarkably good at regulating its own water balance. When fluid levels fall, hormones signal the kidneys to save water, and the brain produces the sensation of thirst, so for most healthy adults drinking when thirsty is sufficient. Needs vary considerably, of course: people who exercise intensively, work in hot climates or have certain medical conditions may require much more.

Too much water can be dangerous as well: in rare cases, athletes who drank huge quantities during long races have developed a condition in which the level of sodium in the blood becomes dangerously low, which can cause confusion, fits and, occasionally, death. None of this means that water is unimportant; a lack of fluid can harm concentration and physical performance. The lesson is rather that a single number cannot capture the needs of every individual.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
options: the life and career of the chemist Arthur Fox
how genetic differences shape the way people taste and why this may matter
why broccoli is the healthiest vegetable
how culture alone decides what people eat
the treatment of nose infections with bitter food
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘how genetic differences shape the way people taste…’: metin genlerin tadı nasıl etkilediğini ve bunun beslenme ve sağlık açısından neden önemli olabileceğini anlatıyor. ‘career’ Fox yalnızca giriş öyküsünde geçiyor. ‘healthiest’ metinde böyle bir iddia yok. ‘alone’ ters; genler de rol oynuyor. ‘treatment’ yanlış; acı yiyecekle tedavi önerilmiyor.
exercises.passage:
Why do some people love broccoli while others find it unbearably bitter? Part of the answer lies in our genes. In 1931 a chemist named Arthur Fox accidentally released a cloud of a chemical called PTC in his laboratory. A colleague complained that the dust tasted bitter, while Fox himself could taste nothing. This chance observation led to one of the earliest studies of inherited differences in perception.

It is now known that the ability to detect PTC depends largely on a gene called TAS2R38, which carries instructions for one of our bitter taste receptors. People who inherit two sensitive versions of the gene tend to experience certain bitter substances intensely, whereas those with two insensitive versions barely notice them. Roughly a quarter of people of European origin are thought to belong to the second group, although the proportion varies between populations.

Such differences may influence everyday food choices. Some studies have reported that highly sensitive tasters eat fewer bitter vegetables, such as cabbage, although the evidence is not entirely consistent, since culture and habit also shape what we eat. Genes have been associated with other preferences as well: many people who dislike fresh coriander say that it tastes like soap, and this reaction has been linked to variation in genes for smell.

Interestingly, bitter receptors are not confined to the tongue. They have also been found in the nose and airways, where they appear to play a role in defending the body against bacteria. Some researchers have suggested that the taste genes of a person might even help predict their vulnerability to certain nose infections. The idea is still under investigation, but it shows that the sense of taste may serve purposes that go far beyond the enjoyment of food.

exercises.question: According to the passage, people with two insensitive versions of TAS2R38 ----.
options: make up about three quarters of Europeans
taste coriander like soap
hardly notice certain bitter substances
cannot smell anything at all
find broccoli unbearably bitter
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘hardly notice certain bitter substances’: 2. paragraf “barely notice them” diyor. ‘quarters’ yanlış; bu grup yaklaşık dörtte bir. ‘soap’ tadı koku genleriyle ilgili ayrı bir örnek. ‘smell’ böyle bir bilgi yok. ‘unbearably’ ters; brokoliyi çok acı bulanlar duyarlı kişilerdir.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Expectations and rituals can produce real effects…’: metin beklentinin ve hap alma ritüelinin belirtiler üzerinde gerçek etki yaratabildiğini anlatıyor. ‘cure’ ters; plasebo tümör küçültmez. ‘lie’ ters; açık plasebolar dürüstçe veriliyor. ‘replaced’ abartı. ‘nocebo’ etkisi yan etkilerin hayalî olduğunu kanıtlamıyor; beklentinin gücünü gösteriyor.
exercises.passage:
In medical research, new drugs are usually compared with a placebo, an inactive pill that looks identical to the real treatment. The purpose is simple: if patients who receive the drug improve more than those who receive the dummy pill, the improvement can reasonably be attributed to the drug itself. Yet these trials have revealed something remarkable. Patients in the placebo group often report genuine relief, particularly from pain, sickness and tiredness.

This placebo effect is not simply imaginary. Brain-imaging studies have shown that when people expect pain relief, the brain releases its own natural painkillers, and activity changes in regions that process pain. Expectations seem to be shaped by many factors, including the colour and size of the pill, its price and the warmth of the doctor. In some experiments, an injection produced stronger effects than a tablet, and expensive pills worked better than cheap ones.

Perhaps the most surprising finding comes from studies of so-called open-label placebos. In these experiments, which were conducted with patients suffering from conditions such as chronic back pain or irritable bowel syndrome, participants were told honestly that they were taking sugar pills with no active ingredient. Many of them nevertheless reported meaningful improvements in their symptoms. Researchers suggest that the ritual of taking a pill may itself trigger a response, even without deception.

The effect also has a darker counterpart, known as the nocebo effect. When patients are warned about possible side effects, some begin to experience them even if they are only taking a placebo. This creates an ethical problem for doctors, who must inform patients honestly while avoiding unnecessary anxiety. It should be noted that placebos cannot shrink tumours or cure infections; their influence is largely limited to symptoms that people feel and report.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Sunlight is the main cause of skin cancer in northern Europe.

Everyone should take very large doses of vitamin D in winter.
Vitamin D is essential, but supplements seem to help mainly people who lack it.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Vitamin D is essential, but supplements seem to help mainly people who lack it’: metin vitaminin önemini, eksikliğin nedenlerini ve takviyelerin sınırlı yararını anlatıyor. ‘Sunlight’ ve cilt kanseri yalnızca bir ayrıntı. ‘prevent’ ters; büyük çalışmalar koruma bulamadı. ‘large’ ters; yüksek doz zehirli olabilir. ‘Rickets’ yalnızca eksikliğin bir sonucu olarak geçiyor.
exercises.passage:
Vitamin D is unusual among nutrients because the body can produce most of what it needs by itself. When ultraviolet rays from the Sun reach the skin, they convert a substance in skin cells into an early form of the vitamin, which is then processed by the liver and kidneys. Its best-known function is to help the gut absorb calcium, a mineral that is essential for strong bones. A severe lack in childhood can lead to rickets, a disease in which the bones become soft and bent.

How much sunlight is enough depends on many circumstances. People living far from the equator receive very little useful ultraviolet radiation in winter, and those with darker skin need longer exposure to make the same amount of the vitamin. Age also matters, since the ability of the skin to produce it declines over a lifetime. Sun cream and clothing, which protect against skin cancer, also reduce production. As a result, low levels are thought to be common in northern Europe during the darker months.

Because low vitamin D has been associated with many conditions, from depression to heart disease, supplements became extremely popular. However, several large randomised trials, in which thousands of adults were given either vitamin D or a placebo for years, found little or no protection against cancer, heart attacks or falls in people who did not have a deficiency. One explanation is that poor health may cause low vitamin D, rather than the other way round; ill people, for instance, often spend less time outdoors.

For this reason, many health authorities now recommend supplements mainly for specific groups, such as babies, older adults and people who rarely go outside. Taking very large doses is not harmless either, since too much vitamin D can raise calcium in the blood to toxic levels.

options: Living alone always makes people feel lonely.
Loneliness can harm physical health, and some societies are starting to respond to it.
Smoking is less dangerous than doctors once believed.
Social prescribing has been proven to cure loneliness.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Loneliness can harm physical health, and some societies are starting to respond to it’: metin yalnızlığın bedensel etkilerini, mekanizmalarını ve hükümetlerin tepkisini anlatıyor. ‘always’ ters; bazıları yalnız yaşar ama yalnızlık hissetmez. ‘Smoking’ yalnızca karşılaştırma için geçiyor. ‘proven’ ters; kanıt sınırlı. ‘first’ yanlış; İngiltere 2018’de, Japonya 2021’de atadı.
exercises.passage:
Loneliness is usually regarded as an emotional problem, but a growing body of research suggests that it also has measurable effects on physical health. In 2010, an influential analysis that combined data from almost 150 studies concluded that people with strong social relationships had a considerably higher chance of survival over the study periods than those who were socially isolated. The authors compared the size of this effect to that of well-established risk factors such as smoking and lack of exercise.

Researchers distinguish between two related ideas. Social isolation is an objective condition, measured by the number of contacts a person has, whereas loneliness is a subjective feeling, the painful sense that relationships are not good enough. The two do not always overlap: some people live alone without feeling lonely, while others feel lonely in the middle of a busy family.

Several mechanisms have been proposed to explain the link. Lonely people may be less likely to exercise, eat well or visit a physician, partly because nobody encourages them to do so. Long-lasting loneliness also appears to keep the body in a state of alert, which is associated with greater vulnerability to infection, higher levels of stress hormones, raised blood pressure and poorer sleep. Over many years, the cumulative effect of these changes could contribute to heart disease and other conditions.

Governments have begun to treat the issue seriously. In 2018 the United Kingdom appointed a minister responsible for loneliness, and Japan followed in 2021. Some doctors now practise social prescribing, an initiative whereby patients are referred to community groups, art classes or volunteering schemes rather than being given medicine. Evidence on how effective such programmes are is still limited, however, and researchers warn that loneliness has many causes, so no single solution is likely to work for everyone.

only affects older people

Some doctors now practise social prescribing, an initiative whereby patients are referred to community groups, art classes or volunteering schemes rather than being given medicine. Evidence on how effective such programmes are is still limited, however, and researchers warn that loneliness has many causes, so no single solution is likely to work for everyone.

exercises.passage:
Loneliness is usually regarded as an emotional problem, but a growing body of research suggests that it also has measurable effects on physical health. In 2010, an influential analysis that combined data from almost 150 studies concluded that people with strong social relationships had a considerably higher chance of survival over the study periods than those who were socially isolated. The authors compared the size of this effect to that of well-established risk factors such as smoking and lack of exercise.

Researchers distinguish between two related ideas. Social isolation is an objective condition, measured by the number of contacts a person has, whereas loneliness is a subjective feeling, the painful sense that relationships are not good enough. The two do not always overlap: some people live alone without feeling lonely, while others feel lonely in the middle of a busy family.

Several mechanisms have been proposed to explain the link. Lonely people may be less likely to exercise, eat well or visit a physician, partly because nobody encourages them to do so. Long-lasting loneliness also appears to keep the body in a state of alert, which is associated with greater vulnerability to infection, higher levels of stress hormones, raised blood pressure and poorer sleep. Over many years, the cumulative effect of these changes could contribute to heart disease and other conditions.

Governments have begun to treat the issue seriously. In 2018 the United Kingdom appointed a minister responsible for loneliness, and Japan followed in 2021. Some doctors now practise social prescribing, an initiative whereby patients are referred to community groups, art classes or volunteering schemes rather than being given medicine. Evidence on how effective such programmes are is still limited, however, and researchers warn that loneliness has many causes, so no single solution is likely to work for everyone.

nodes.title: Cümle çözümleme
nodes.description: Ünitenin metinlerinden uzun cümleler: ana fiil, which ve çeviri

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘In these experiments, which were conducted with patients suffering from conditions such as chronic back pain or irritable bowel syndrome, participants were told honestly that they were taking sugar pills with no active ingredient.’
options: were conducted
suffering
were taking
conducted
were told
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘were told’. İskelet: participants (özne) + were told (ana fiil, edilgen) + that… (nesne cümlesi). Özne uzun ara cümleden sonra geliyor. ‘were conducted’ which ara cümlesinin fiilidir. ‘suffering’ patients sözcüğünü niteleyen -ing biçimidir. ‘were taking’ that cümlesinin fiilidir. ‘conducted’ ara cümledeki fiilin ortacıdır, ana fiil olamaz.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘In 2010, an influential analysis that combined data from almost 150 studies concluded that people with strong social relationships had a considerably higher chance of survival over the study periods than those who were socially isolated.’
options: combined
concluded
had
were socially isolated
influential
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘concluded’. İskelet: an influential analysis (özne) + concluded (ana fiil) + that… (nesne cümlesi). ‘combined’ that ile başlayan ve özneyi niteleyen yan cümlenin fiilidir. ‘had’ nesne cümlesinin fiilidir. ‘were socially isolated’ who ile başlayan yan cümlenin fiilidir. ‘influential’ bir sıfattır.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘However, several large randomised trials, in which thousands of adults were given either vitamin D or a placebo for years, found little or no protection against cancer, heart attacks or falls in people who did not have a deficiency.’
options: randomised
were given
did not have
given
found
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘found’. İskelet: several large randomised trials (özne) + found (ana fiil) + little or no protection (nesne). ‘randomised’ trials sözcüğünü niteleyen sıfattır. ‘were given’ in which ara cümlesinin fiilidir. ‘did not have’ who cümlesinin fiilidir. ‘given’ tek başına çekimli fiil değil, were given yapısının parçasıdır.

exercises.question: Cümledeki ‘which’ neyi nitelemektedir? ‘Some historians trace it back to a 1945 recommendation in the United States, which stated that adults need about 2.5 litres of water daily.’
options: Some historians
the United States
adults
a 1945 recommendation
water
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘a 1945 recommendation’: “bir şeyi belirten” bir belge olabilir; ‘which’ burada in the United States ifadesinin üzerinden atlayarak tavsiyeye bağlanır. ‘Some historians’ who ile nitelenirdi. ‘the United States’ en yakın isim ama bir ülke tavsiye metni gibi “stated” diyemez; sonraki cümle de “The same document” diyor. ‘adults’ ve ‘water’ yan cümlenin içindedir.

exercises.question: Cümledeki ‘which’ neyi nitelemektedir? ‘It is now known that the ability to detect PTC depends largely on a gene called TAS2R38, which carries instructions for one of our bitter taste receptors.’
options: the ability
PTC
a gene called TAS2R38
instructions
bitter taste receptors
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘a gene called TAS2R38’: talimat taşıyan şey gendir; ‘which’ virgülden önceki bu isme bağlanır ve fiil tekildir (carries). ‘the ability’ yeteneğin talimat taşıması anlamsızdır. ‘PTC’ algılanan kimyasal maddedir. ‘instructions’ ve ‘bitter taste receptors’ yan cümlenin içindedir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Experts stress, however, that babies with severe skin problems or existing allergies should be assessed by a doctor first.’
options: Ancak uzmanlar, ciddi cilt sorunları ya da mevcut alerjileri olan bebeklerin önce bir doktor tarafından değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini vurguluyor.
Ancak uzmanlar, ciddi cilt sorunları olan bebeklerin doktora götürülmesine gerek olmadığını vurguluyor.
Uzmanlar, cilt sorunları olan bebeklere asla fıstık verilmemesi gerektiğini vurguluyor.
Doktorlar, ciddi alerjileri olan bebekleri önce uzmanlara gönderdi.
Ancak uzmanlar, hafif cilt sorunları olan tüm bebeklerin evde değerlendirilebileceğini düşünüyor.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘…önce bir doktor tarafından değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini vurguluyor’. İskelet: Experts (özne) + stress (ana fiil) + that babies… should be assessed (edilgen nesne cümlesi). ‘gerek’ olmadığını söyleyen seçenek olumsuzluk ekliyor. ‘fıstık’ metinde olmayan bir yasak ekliyor. ‘gönderdi’ özneyi ve zamanı değiştiriyor. ‘hafif’ severe sözcüğünü tersine çeviriyor.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Coffee was long believed to dry out the body, but studies have found that moderate amounts do not cause any meaningful fluid loss in regular drinkers.’
options: Kahvenin uzun süre vücudu kuruttuğuna inanıldı ve çalışmalar ölçülü miktarların bile ciddi sıvı kaybına yol açtığını buldu.
Kahve vücudu kurutmaz; bu yüzden bu konuda hiçbir çalışma yapılmadı.
Kahvenin uzun süre vücudu kuruttuğuna inanıldı, ancak çalışmalar büyük miktarların hiç sıvı kaybına yol açmadığını buldu.

İskelet: Coffee (özne) + was believed (edilgen) …, but studies (özne) + have found (ana fiil) + that… ‘ciddi’ olumsuzluğu kaldırıyor. ‘yapılmadı’ çalışmaların varlığını inkâr ediyor. ‘büyük’ moderate niceleyicisini değiştiriyor. ‘doğruladı’ hem zamanı hem sonucu ters çeviriyor.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Lonely people may be less likely to exercise, eat well or visit a physician, partly because nobody encourages them to do so.’
options: Yalnız insanların egzersiz yapma, iyi beslenme ya da doktora gitme olasılığı kesinlikle daha düşüktür.
Yalnız insanların egzersiz yapma, iyi beslenme ya da doktora gitme olasılığı, kısmen kimse onları buna teşvik etmediği için daha düşük olabilir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Taking very large doses is not harmless either, since too much vitamin D can raise calcium in the blood to toxic levels.’
options: Çok yüksek dozlar almak da zararsız değildir, çünkü aşırı D vitamini kandaki kalsiyumu zehirli düzeylere çıkarabilir.

Çok yüksek dozlar almak zararsız değildir, çünkü aşırı D vitamini kandaki kalsiyumu zehirli düzeylerin altına düşürür.
Düşük dozlar almak zararlıdır, çünkü D vitamini kandaki kalsiyumu azaltır.
Çok yüksek dozlar her zaman kalsiyumu zehirli düzeye çıkarmıştır.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Lab-grown red blood cells have already replaced human donors.
Blood can now be produced cheaply in large factories.
The discovery of blood groups made transfusion safe, but blood supplies remain a challenge.
Landsteiner opened the first blood bank in 1930.
Type O negative blood is dangerous for most patients.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The discovery of blood groups made transfusion safe, but blood supplies remain a challenge’: metin Landsteiner’in buluşunu, bileşenleri ve gönüllüye bağımlılığı anlatıyor. ‘replaced’ ters; denemeler yeni başladı. ‘cheaply’ ters; üretim çok pahalı. ‘bank’ yanlış; 1930 Nobel ödülünün yılı. ‘dangerous’ ters; bu kan neredeyse herkese verilebilir.
exercises.passage:
Before the twentieth century, attempts to transfer blood from one person to another were extremely risky. Some patients recovered, but many suffered violent reactions and died, and nobody could explain why. The mystery was solved in 1901 by the Austrian doctor Karl Landsteiner, who mixed blood samples from his colleagues and noticed that some combinations formed clumps while others did not. From these observations he identified the main blood groups now known as A, B and O; the fourth group, AB, was described shortly afterwards.

The groups are determined by markers on the surface of red blood cells. The immune system treats unfamiliar markers as foreign, so if a patient receives blood of the wrong type, antibodies attack the donated cells. For this reason, blood must be carefully tested and matched before every transfusion. Type O negative blood, which lacks the main markers, can be given to almost anyone in an emergency, so it is in particularly high demand in hospitals.

The discovery of Landsteiner, which earned him a Nobel Prize in 1930, made safe transfusion possible, and during the First World War doctors began to store blood for later use. Today, donated blood is separated into components, such as red cells, plasma and platelets, so that a single donation can help several patients. These components cannot be manufactured artificially and have a limited lifetime; platelets, for example, can be kept for only about a week.

Consequently, health services depend on a constant flow of volunteers. Yet only a small percentage of eligible people give blood regularly, and supplies often fall during holidays or bad weather. Scientists are experimenting with growing red blood cells from stem cells in the laboratory, and the first small human trials have begun. Producing such cells in large quantities, however, remains far too expensive for routine use.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Horace Wells was the first person to use ether successfully.
Queen Victoria ordered British doctors to use chloroform.
Operations became much faster after anaesthesia was introduced.
Laughing gas is still the most common drug used in surgery.
The introduction of anaesthesia in the 1840s transformed surgery, although it carried risks at first.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The introduction of anaesthesia in the 1840s transformed surgery…’: metin anestezi öncesi cerrahiyi, 1840’lardaki buluşları, sonuçlarını ve ilk dönemdeki riskleri anlatıyor. ‘Wells’ eteri değil gülme gazını denedi; eteri Morton kullandı. ‘ordered’ yanlış; kraliçeye kloroform verildi, bir emir söz konusu değil. ‘faster’ ters; cerrahlar artık acele etmek zorunda kalmadı. ‘common’ metinde böyle bir bilgi yok.
exercises.passage:
Before the middle of the nineteenth century, surgery was a terrifying experience. Patients were held down by assistants while the surgeon worked as fast as possible, and a skilled operator could remove a leg in only a few minutes. Alcohol and opium were sometimes given, but they offered little relief, and many patients died from shock or infection. For this reason, operations were largely confined to the outside of the body and were performed only as a last resort.

The situation changed in the 1840s, when several Americans began to experiment with gases that made people lose consciousness. Nitrous oxide, often called laughing gas, was already popular at public shows, where volunteers breathed it in for entertainment. A dentist named Horace Wells noticed that a man who had injured his leg under its influence felt no pain, and he tried the gas on his own patients. However, a public demonstration in Boston failed, apparently because the patient had not received enough gas.

In 1846, another dentist, William Morton, used ether during an operation at the Massachusetts General Hospital, in which a tumour was removed from the neck of a patient. The patient later said that he had felt no real pain, and news of the event spread rapidly to Europe. Within about a year, chloroform had also been introduced in Britain, and it was later given to Queen Victoria during childbirth, which helped to make anaesthesia socially acceptable.

The discovery had far-reaching consequences. Because surgeons no longer had to hurry, they could perform longer and more complex operations. Yet early anaesthesia was not without risks, since the correct dose was difficult to judge and some patients died. Modern specialists rely on carefully controlled combinations of drugs and constantly monitor breathing, pulse and blood pressure, so serious complications are now rare.

options: the patient had injured his leg

the audience laughed during the show
the tumour was too large to remove
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the patient apparently had not been given enough gas’: 2. paragrafın son cümlesi bunu söylüyor. ‘injured’ bacağını inciten adam Wells’in ilk gözlemindeki kişidir. ‘ether’ Wells’in kullandığı gaz değildi. ‘audience’ seyircinin gülmesi metinde geçmiyor. ‘tumour’ Morton’ın 1846’daki ameliyatıyla ilgilidir.

the news from Boston
the use of chloroform by Queen Victoria during childbirth
the tumour in the neck
the Massachusetts General Hospital

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Because surgeons no longer had to hurry, they could perform longer and more complex operations.’
options: Cerrahlar acele etmek zorunda oldukları için yalnızca kısa ameliyatlar yapabildiler.
Cerrahlar daha uzun ameliyatlar yaptıkları için acele etmeye başladılar.
Cerrahlar artık acele etmedikleri hâlde karmaşık ameliyatlardan kaçındılar.
Cerrahlar artık acele etmek zorunda olmadıkları için daha uzun ve daha karmaşık ameliyatlar yapabildiler.

units.title: Yazarın tutumu
units.description: Yazarın görüşünü gösteren ipuçlarını yakala: olumlu, olumsuz, temkinli
units.guide:
## Strateji
Tutum sorusu (*The author's attitude … is ----*, *The author would most likely agree …*) metnin konusunu değil, yazarın konu hakkındaki **değerlendirmesini** sorar. Akademik yazar görüşünü açıkça bağırmaz; onu birkaç küçük işaretle verir. Bu işaretleri toplarsan tutum kendiliğinden ortaya çıkar.

## Nasıl uygulanır
1. Birinci tekil ifadeleri işaretle: *I believe, in my view, I would argue, I find … hard to accept*.
2. Değer bildiren sıfat ve zarfları bul: *surprisingly weak, worryingly, unfair, sensible*.
3. Kabul + itiraz kalıbını ara: *Admittedly … Nevertheless*, *This is not to say …*, *None of this means …*. Yazarın asıl görüşü itirazdan sonra gelir.
4. Son paragrafta yazarın önerisini oku; tutum çoğu zaman orada özetlenir.
5. Şıklarda ölçüyü kontrol et: tutum "eleştirel ama ılımlı" ise *hostile*, *entirely enthusiastic* gibi uç şıkları ele.

## Örnek
*Tipping is commonly defended as a way of rewarding good service. I find this justification increasingly hard to believe.*
- *commonly defended* → başkalarının görüşü.
- *I find … hard to believe* → yazarın görüşü: olumsuz (*disapproving*).

## Sınav ipucu
Yazarın aktardığı görüş ile kendi görüşünü karıştırma: *Supporters argue …*, *It is often claimed …* başkasının sesidir. *Neutral* ve *indifferent* şıkları, yazar "I" ile konuşuyorsa neredeyse hiç doğru değildir.

exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
options: Open-plan offices should be banned because they are too expensive to run.
Removing walls has saved money but has not delivered the communication it promised.
Workers in open offices send fewer emails than those in closed offices.
Headphones are the best solution to noise in modern offices.
Researchers at Harvard designed the first open-plan office in 2018.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Removing walls has saved money but has not delivered the communication it promised’: yazar açık ofisin ucuz olduğunu kabul ediyor ama iletişimi artırma iddiasının zayıf olduğunu savunuyor. ‘banned’ yanlış, yazar karma bir düzeni öneriyor. ‘fewer emails’ ters, e-postalar arttı. ‘Headphones’ yalnızca bir örnek, çözüm olarak sunulmuyor. ‘designed’ yanlış, Harvard ofisi tasarlamadı, inceledi.
exercises.passage:
Over the past few decades, walls have been removed from offices across the world, and millions of employees now work in large open spaces where desks are arranged in long rows. The arrangement was originally justified on the grounds that it would encourage interaction between colleagues and spark new ideas. Managers also liked a less obvious advantage: open floors are cheaper, because more people can be fitted into the same space, which reduces the burden of rent. In my view, however, the evidence for the main claim is surprisingly weak, and the costs have been taken far too lightly.

The most frequently cited study, which was carried out by researchers at Harvard in 2018, followed employees in two companies before and after they moved into open offices. Contrary to what the designers had predicted, face-to-face conversations fell by about 70 percent, while the number of emails and messages rose. It appears that when people feel they are constantly being watched and heard, they withdraw rather than talk. Many put on headphones, which signal to others that they do not want to be disturbed.

Noise is another problem that is commonly underestimated. Concentration is easily broken by a nearby phone call, and it may take several minutes to return fully to a demanding task. Workers who need quiet for careful thinking, such as writers or engineers, are therefore placed at a clear disadvantage.

None of this means that every office should return to closed doors. Some teams genuinely benefit from sitting together, and a mix of shared areas and quiet rooms seems a reasonable compromise. What I find hard to accept is the assumption that removing walls automatically produces collaboration. Good communication depends on trust and clear goals, not on the absence of furniture.

exercises.question: According to the passage, the study carried out at Harvard found that after the move ----.
options: the number of emails fell by about 70 percent
employees became more productive and creative
managers decided to rebuild the walls
employees talked face to face much less and sent more messages
employees stopped wearing headphones at work
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘employees talked face to face much less and sent more messages’: yüz yüze konuşmalar yaklaşık yüzde 70 azaldı, e-posta ve mesajlar arttı. ‘emails fell’ ters; düşen e-posta değil, yüz yüze konuşmaydı. ‘productive’ metinde yok. ‘rebuild’ metinde geçmiyor. ‘stopped wearing’ ters, çalışanlar kulaklık takmaya başladı.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
options: warn young people about the dangers of changing jobs
describe how pensions worked in the twentieth century
argue that young workers who change jobs often are judged unfairly
explain why companies outsource their departments
advise recruiters on how to read a CV
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘argue that young workers who change jobs often are judged unfairly’: yazar "I believe this criticism is largely unfair" diyerek savunma yapıyor. ‘warn’ ters, yazar iş değiştirmeyi akılcı bir strateji olarak görüyor. ‘pensions’ yalnızca arka plan bilgisi. ‘outsource’ bir ayrıntı, amaç değil. ‘recruiters’ metin işe alımcılara tavsiye vermiyor.
exercises.passage:
Young employees are often criticised for changing jobs too frequently. Older managers sometimes describe them as disloyal or impatient, and a CV which lists four employers in six years is still treated with scepticism by some recruiters, who regard it as an indication of weak commitment. I believe this criticism is largely unfair, and that it rests on a picture of working life which no longer corresponds to reality.

For much of the twentieth century, a worker who joined a large company could reasonably expect to stay there for decades, and in return for loyalty, the employer offered promotion, training and a pension. That arrangement has gradually disappeared. Today, firms restructure, merge and outsource whole departments with little warning, and long-term security is rarely guaranteed, even to staff with excellent records. It seems unreasonable to demand loyalty from employees when it is no longer offered to them.

There are also practical reasons why moving can be a rational strategy. Several surveys have found that people who change employers tend to receive larger pay increases than those who wait for a bonus or a raise from their current firm. A new position may also provide skills, contacts and a wide range of experience that would take years to acquire in one place. In this sense, each move can be seen as an investment in one's own productivity rather than an escape.

Admittedly, frequent moves have costs. Employers lose money when trained staff leave, and a worker who never stays long may fail to develop deep competence or lasting professional relationships. Nevertheless, the solution is not to blame individuals. If companies want people to stay, they should offer what once kept them: fair pay, genuine development and a sense that commitment will be rewarded. Loyalty, after all, is a relationship that has to be earned on both sides.

exercises.question: According to the passage, people who move to a new employer ----.
options: usually lose their pension and promotion
rarely develop any professional skills
tend to receive larger pay increases than those who stay

earn less in the long term than loyal staff
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘tend to receive larger pay increases than those who stay’: anketler iş değiştirenlerin daha büyük zam aldığını gösteriyor. ‘pension’ metinde böyle bir sonuç yok. ‘rarely develop’ abartılı; metin yalnızca derin uzmanlığın gelişmeyebileceğini söylüyor. ‘every recruiter’ yanlış, metin "some recruiters" diyor. ‘earn less’ metinle çelişiyor.

I believe this criticism is largely unfair, and that it rests on a picture of working life which no longer corresponds to reality.

For much of the twentieth century, a worker who joined a large company could reasonably expect to stay there for decades, and in return for loyalty, the employer offered promotion, training and a pension. That arrangement has gradually disappeared. Today, firms restructure, merge and outsource whole departments with little warning, and long-term security is rarely guaranteed, even to staff with excellent records. It seems unreasonable to demand loyalty from employees when it is no longer offered to them.

There are also practical reasons why moving can be a rational strategy. Several surveys have found that people who change employers tend to receive larger pay increases than those who wait for a bonus or a raise from their current firm. A new position may also provide skills, contacts and a wide range of experience that would take years to acquire in one place. In this sense, each move can be seen as an investment in one's own productivity rather than an escape.

Admittedly, frequent moves have costs. Employers lose money when trained staff leave, and a worker who never stays long may fail to develop deep competence or lasting professional relationships. Nevertheless, the solution is not to blame individuals. If companies want people to stay, they should offer what once kept them: fair pay, genuine development and a sense that commitment will be rewarded. Loyalty, after all, is a relationship that has to be earned on both sides.

exercises.passage:
Almost every supermarket, café and airline now invites customers to join a loyalty programme. The offer seems generous: in exchange for showing a card or an app at the till, shoppers accumulate points which can later be swapped for discounts, free coffee or flights. Millions of people are enrolled in several schemes simultaneously, and the cards are usually described as a simple reward for repeat visits. I am, however, far from convinced that the main beneficiary is the customer.

The real value of these programmes lies in the information they collect. Every transaction is recorded, together with the time, the place and the other items in the basket. When this data is combined over months, a remarkably detailed profile of each shopper emerges, which allows companies to predict what people will buy and how much they are willing to pay. Some retailers, notably large supermarket chains, also share such data with partners, although the details are usually buried in long terms and conditions that few people read.

The rewards themselves are often smaller than they appear. In many schemes, a customer must spend a considerable amount before receiving a meaningful discount, and points may expire if they are not used in time. Evidence suggests that the promise of a reward can encourage people to keep buying from one store even when cheaper options are available elsewhere, which is, of course, precisely the intention.

This is not to say that loyalty cards should be banned. For a regular shopper, the savings can be real, and some people are perfectly happy to trade information for lower prices. However, that trade should be made consciously. Shoppers deserve a clear explanation of what is collected and how it is used, and regulators should ensure that such explanations are provided in plain language.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
options: Online Reviews: Useful Evidence, Not a Final Judgement
How to Write a Successful Hotel Review
Why Fake Reviews Have Finally Disappeared
The Rise of Star Ratings in Advertising
Algorithms That Write Reviews for Sellers
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Online Reviews: Useful Evidence, Not a Final Judgement’: yazar yorumların değersiz olmadığını ama kanıt olarak dikkatle okunması gerektiğini savunuyor. ‘Successful Hotel Review’ metin yorum yazmayı öğretmiyor. ‘Disappeared’ ters, sahte yorumlar sürüyor. ‘Advertising’ yorumlar reklamla karşılaştırılıyor, reklamda kullanılmıyor. ‘Algorithms That Write’ ters, algoritmalar sahte yorumları silmek için kullanılıyor.
exercises.passage:
Before booking a hotel or buying a kettle, most of us now check what other customers have written online. Star ratings and short reviews have become one of the most influential sources of consumer information, and studies indicate that a small difference in average rating can noticeably affect a product's sales. It is easy to see why they are trusted: they appear to come from ordinary people who have no reason to lie, and they seem more credible than any advertisement. In my opinion, this trust is only partly justified.

The first difficulty is that a significant share of reviews may not be genuine. Some vendors pay for positive comments or offer free products in exchange for five stars, and fake reviews are sometimes posted in large numbers by organised groups. Platforms remove many of them with the help of algorithms, but the methods used to produce fakes are constantly being improved, and it remains unclear whether most of them are detected.

Even genuine reviews present a distorted picture. People who are either delighted or furious are far more likely to write something than those whose experience was simply acceptable. As a result, ratings tend to cluster at the extremes, while the typical customer stays silent. In addition, a review describes a single experience, which is essentially anecdotal and may tell us little about how the product will perform for someone else.

None of this makes reviews worthless. Read carefully, they can reveal recurring problems, such as a hotel's noisy rooms or a phone's weak battery, which no advertisement would mention. The sensible approach, I would argue, is to treat them as evidence rather than as a final judgement: to look for patterns across many comments, to pay attention to detailed criticism, and to remain sceptical of any product whose praise seems too perfect.

exercises.question: According to the passage, ratings tend to cluster at the extremes because ----.
options: platforms remove all average ratings

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘customers with very strong feelings are more likely to write reviews’: çok memnun ya da çok kızgın olanlar yazıyor, sıradan deneyimi olan sessiz kalıyor. ‘remove all average ratings’ metinde yok. ‘perfect or useless’ ürünlerin kendisiyle ilgili bir iddia yok. ‘one star’ ters, satıcılar beş yıldız için ödüyor. ‘typical customers’ ters, onlar sessiz kalıyor.

exercises.question: The author's main argument in the passage is that ----.
options: cash should remain available even though digital payments have real benefits
digital payments should be banned to protect privacy
Sweden has already abolished notes and coins completely
cash machines are more reliable than banks
tax evasion is the main reason for keeping cash
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘cash should remain available even though digital payments have real benefits’: yazar avantajları kabul ediyor ("I accept these advantages") ama nakdin tamamen terk edilmesine karşı çıkıyor. ‘banned’ ters, yazar kartlara dönüşü reddetmiyor. ‘abolished’ yanlış, İsveç’te hâlâ az da olsa nakit kullanılıyor. ‘cash machines’ bankalarla karşılaştırılmıyor. ‘evasion’ ters, vergi kaçırmanın zorlaşması dijital ödemenin avantajı olarak geçiyor.
exercises.passage:
In several countries, cash is rapidly disappearing from daily life. In Sweden, for example, it is estimated that only around one in ten purchases in shops is now paid for with notes and coins, and many cafés and buses no longer accept them at all. Supporters of a cashless society point to clear benefits: card and phone payments are fast, they reduce the risk of robbery, and they make it harder to hide income from the tax authorities. I accept these advantages, yet I believe that abandoning cash entirely would be a serious mistake.

My main concern is inclusion. A considerable number of people, particularly elderly citizens and those on low incomes, either have no bank account or find digital payments difficult to manage. For them, cash is not an outdated habit but the only reliable means of participating in the economy, and when shops refuse coins, these groups are quietly excluded from ordinary activities such as buying bread or taking a bus.

A second concern is resilience. Electronic systems depend on electricity, networks and a small number of multinational companies, and when they fail, which happens more often than is commonly admitted, payments can halt across a whole region. Cash, by contrast, continues to work in the event of a power cut. It is worth noting that the Swedish authorities, whose country is often presented as a model of the cashless future, have themselves advised households to keep some notes at home for emergencies.

Finally, there is the question of privacy. Every digital transaction leaves a record, whereas cash allows people to make small purchases without being tracked.

Nobody is suggesting that we should return to a world without cards; the point is simply that a choice should be preserved. Governments can achieve this by requiring essential services to accept cash and by ensuring that cash machines remain available outside large cities.

options: banned cafés and buses from accepting coins

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘advised households to keep some cash at home for emergencies’: üçüncü paragraf bunu açıkça söylüyor. ‘banned’ yanlış, kafeler kendi kararıyla nakit almıyor. ‘required all shops’ metinde böyle bir kural yok. ‘closed cash machines’ metin yalnızca makinelerin korunmasını öneriyor. ‘never fail’ ters, sistemler sanıldığından sık çöküyor.

exercises.passage:
In the United States, a restaurant bill is rarely the final price. Customers are expected to add a tip of fifteen to twenty percent, and in recent years tip requests have spread from restaurants to coffee shops, bakeries and even self-service machines, where a screen invites the buyer to choose a percentage. Tipping is commonly defended as a way of rewarding good service. I find this justification increasingly hard to believe.

The most obvious problem is that tipping shifts the burden of paying wages from employers to customers. In many American states, restaurant owners are legally allowed to pay waiters a much lower minimum wage, on the assumption that tips will make up the difference. A worker's income therefore depends less on the quality of the work than on factors which are beyond their control, such as the weather, the mood of the customers or the day of the week.

Moreover, the link between service and tips appears to be weak. Several studies have found that the size of a tip is only slightly affected by how well a customer was actually served. It seems to be more strongly influenced by the size of the bill, by whether the server is friendly in a personal way, and, worryingly, by the appearance of the server, which opens the door to prejudice. A system which is supposed to reward effort ends up rewarding factors that have nothing to do with it.

Supporters warn that abolishing tips would raise menu prices. That is true, but it would also make prices honest. In countries such as Japan, where tipping is uncommon, service is not noticeably worse. A fair wage, included openly in the price, would treat both workers and customers with more fairness and dignity than a social obligation which nobody can quite explain.

exercises.question: According to the passage, the size of a tip ----.
options: is fixed by law in many American states
is always twenty percent of the bill
is largely determined by how quickly the food arrives
depends more on the bill and the server than on the quality of service
is higher in Japan than in the United States
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘depends more on the bill and the server than on the quality of service’: bahşiş hizmetten çok az etkileniyor; hesabın büyüklüğü, garsonun samimiyeti ve görünüşü daha belirleyici. ‘fixed by law’ yanlış, yasa yalnızca düşük asgari ücrete izin veriyor. ‘always’ yanlış, oran yüzde 15–20. ‘quickly’ metinde yok. ‘Japan’ yanlış, Japonya’da bahşiş yaygın değil.
