nodes.title: Cümle çözümleme
nodes.description: Ünitenin metinlerinden uzun cümleler: ana fiil, yan cümle, kalıp ve çeviri

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘When this data is combined over months, a remarkably detailed profile of each shopper emerges, which allows companies to predict what people will buy.’
options: is combined
detailed
emerges
allows
to predict
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘emerges’. İskelet: a remarkably detailed profile of each shopper (özne) + emerges (ana fiil). ‘is combined’ When ile başlayan zaman yan cümlesinin fiilidir. ‘detailed’ profile sözcüğünü niteleyen sıfat-fiildir. ‘allows’ which yan cümlesinin fiilidir. ‘to predict’ mastardır, çekimli fiil değildir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘A system which is supposed to reward effort ends up rewarding factors that have nothing to do with it.’
options: is supposed
reward
ends
rewarding
have
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘ends’ (ends up = sonunda … yapar hale gelir). İskelet: A system (özne) + ends up (ana fiil) + rewarding factors. ‘is supposed’ which yan cümlesinin fiilidir. ‘reward’ mastar (to reward) içindedir. ‘rewarding’ ends up’tan sonra gelen -ing biçimidir. ‘have’ that yan cümlesinin fiilidir.

exercises.question: Cümledeki ‘which’ neyi nitelemektedir? ‘Many put on headphones, which signal to others that they do not want to be disturbed.’
options: headphones
others
employees
messages
open offices
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘headphones’: which virgülden hemen önceki isme bağlanır; başkalarına rahatsız edilmek istemediğini gösteren şey kulaklıklardır. ‘others’ işaretin gönderildiği kişilerdir. ‘employees’ cümlede değil, özne "Many" ile kastedilir. ‘messages’ önceki cümlede geçer. ‘open offices’ cümlede yoktur.

exercises.question: Cümlede that ile başlayan yan cümlenin öznesi ve çekimli fiili hangisidir? ‘It is worth noting that the Swedish authorities, whose country is often presented as a model of the cashless future, have themselves advised households to keep some notes at home.’
options: their country / is presented
households / to keep
It / is worth noting
a model / have advised
the Swedish authorities / have advised
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the Swedish authorities / have advised’: that yan cümlesinin iskeleti budur; whose ile başlayan kısım araya giren yan cümledir. ‘is presented’ whose yan cümlesinin fiilidir. ‘to keep’ mastardır, households nesnedir. ‘It / is worth noting’ ana cümlenin çerçevesidir, that yan cümlesine ait değildir. ‘a model’ yan cümlenin içindedir ve özne olamaz.

exercises.question: Cümledeki ‘on the grounds that’ ifadesinin Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘The arrangement was originally justified on the grounds that it would encourage interaction between colleagues.’
options: -mesine rağmen
-eceği gerekçesiyle
-diği sürece
-mediği takdirde
-eceği yerde
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘-eceği gerekçesiyle’: on the grounds that bir gerekçe bildirir; düzen, iş arkadaşları arasındaki etkileşimi artıracağı gerekçesiyle savunuldu. ‘-mesine rağmen’ zıtlık bildirir. ‘-diği sürece’ koşul ve süre bildirir. ‘-mediği takdirde’ olumsuz koşuldur. ‘-eceği yerde’ beklenenin tersini anlatır.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Concentration is easily broken by a nearby phone call, and it may take several minutes to return fully to a demanding task.’
options: Yakındaki bir telefon görüşmesi konsantrasyonu nadiren bozar ve zorlu bir işe dönmek birkaç saniye sürer.
Konsantrasyon bir telefon görüşmesiyle bozulmaz; zorlu bir işe dönmek birkaç dakika sürmelidir.
Yakındaki bir telefon görüşmesi konsantrasyonu kolayca bozdu ve zorlu işe dönmek birkaç dakika sürdü.
Yakındaki bir telefon görüşmesi konsantrasyonu kolayca bozar ve zorlu bir işe tamamen geri dönmek birkaç dakika sürebilir.
Uzaktaki bir telefon görüşmesi bile konsantrasyonu bozar, bu yüzden zorlu işlerden kaçınılmalıdır.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘…zorlu bir işe tamamen geri dönmek birkaç dakika sürebilir’: edilgen "is broken by" = "… tarafından bozulur", may take = "sürebilir". ‘nadiren’ easily anlamını ters çeviriyor ve ‘saniye’ süreyi değiştiriyor. ‘bozulmaz’ cümleyi olumsuz yapıyor. ‘sürdü’ geniş zamanı geçmiş zamana çeviriyor. ‘Uzaktaki’ nearby anlamını bozuyor ve ‘kaçınılmalıdır’ metinde yok.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘It seems unreasonable to demand loyalty from employees when it is no longer offered to them.’
options: Çalışanlar sadakat talep ettiğinde şirketler bunu artık sunmuyor.
Çalışanlara artık sunulmayan bir sadakati onlardan talep etmek mantıksız görünüyor.
Çalışanlara sadakat sunulduğu sürece onlardan sadakat beklemek mantıklıdır.
Çalışanlardan sadakat talep etmek her zaman mantıksız olmuştur.
Çalışanlara hâlâ sunulan bir sadakati onlardan beklemek mantıklı görünüyor.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Çalışanlara artık sunulmayan bir sadakati onlardan talep etmek mantıksız görünüyor’: It seems unreasonable = mantıksız görünüyor; no longer offered = artık sunulmayan. ‘şirketler’ geçen şık talep edeni çalışanlar yapıyor. ‘sürece’ geçen şık olumsuzluğu kaldırıp anlamı ters çeviriyor. ‘zaman’ geçen şık "her zaman" ekleyip no longer koşulunu siliyor. ‘hâlâ’ no longer anlamının tersidir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Bu, sadakat kartlarının yasaklanması gerektiği anlamına gelmez.’
options: This means that loyalty cards must be banned immediately.
Loyalty cards were banned because of this.
This does not mean that loyalty cards have been banned.
This is not to say that loyalty cards should be banned.
Nobody says that loyalty cards are useful.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘This is not to say that loyalty cards should be banned’: "anlamına gelmez" = is not to say; "yasaklanması gerektiği" = should be banned. ‘immediately’ geçen şık olumsuzluğu kaldırıyor. ‘were’ ile kurulan şık olmuş bir olay anlatıyor. ‘have been banned’ gereklilik yerine olmuş bir yasak anlatıyor. ‘Nobody’ ile başlayan şık başka bir anlam taşıyor.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Bahşişin büyüklüğü, müşteriye ne kadar iyi hizmet edildiğinden yalnızca biraz etkilenir.’
options: The size of a tip is only slightly affected by how well a customer was served.
The size of a tip is strongly affected by how well a customer was served.
How well a customer is served has no effect on the size of a tip.
The size of a tip slightly affects how well a customer will be served.
Customers who are served well always leave larger tips.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The size of a tip is only slightly affected by how well a customer was served’: "yalnızca biraz etkilenir" = is only slightly affected. ‘strongly’ derecesi ters çeviriyor. ‘effect’ geçen şık etkiyi tamamen yok sayıyor. ‘affects’ ile neden ve sonuç yer değiştiriyor. ‘always’ ve ‘larger’ metinde olmayan kesin bir iddia kuruyor.

exercises.question: The author's attitude towards the growth of subscriptions can best be described as ----.
options: enthusiastic
indifferent
hostile
admiring
cautious
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘cautious’: yazar modelin yararlı olabileceğini kabul ediyor ama "deserves more caution" diyor. ‘enthusiastic’ ve ‘admiring’ ters yönde. ‘indifferent’ yanlış, yazar açık görüş bildiriyor. ‘hostile’ aşırı, yazar aboneliklerin ortadan kalkmasını istemiyor.
exercises.passage:
Not long ago, people bought software, music and films once and then owned them. Today, many of these products are offered only as subscriptions, and the same model has been extended to a wide range of goods, from car features and coffee to clothing and even pet food. Companies favour subscriptions because they provide a steady, predictable income, while customers are attracted by low monthly prices, flexibility and the convenience of automatic delivery. Although I do not doubt that the model can be useful, I think its growth deserves more caution than it usually receives.

The central difficulty is that subscriptions are designed to be forgotten. A payment which is taken automatically each month looks like a bargain and attracts little attention, and evidence suggests that consumers commonly underestimate how much they spend on such services, sometimes by a wide margin. Free trials, which turn into paid plans unless they are cancelled in time, rely on precisely this inattention.

Cancelling can also be made deliberately difficult. Some firms allow customers to sign up with a single click but require a phone call, or a sequence of confusing screens, before they can leave, which places the whole burden on the customer. Regulators in the United States and the European Union have begun to respond, and new rules have been proposed which would require cancellation to be as straightforward as registration.

There is a further, less visible cost. When a product is rented rather than owned, the customer's access depends entirely on the vendor, whose prices can be raised, features removed and whole libraries withdrawn with little that the user can do.

None of this implies that subscriptions should disappear, since for a service that is used heavily, they can represent good value. The sensible response is for consumers to audit their monthly commitments regularly, and for the law to guarantee that leaving a service is never harder than joining it.

exercises.question: According to the passage, free trials ----.
options: are only offered by companies in the European Union
must be cancelled by a phone call
turn into paid plans if they are not cancelled in time
are required by law to last a month
allow customers to own the product permanently
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘turn into paid plans if they are not cancelled in time’: "which turn into paid plans unless they are cancelled in time". ‘European Union’ yalnızca düzenleyiciler bağlamında geçiyor. ‘phone call’ bazı firmaların iptal yöntemi, denemelerin kuralı değil. ‘law’ böyle bir süre metinde yok. ‘permanently’ ters, abonelikte sahiplik yok.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
options: explain why university degrees are no longer useful
describe the history of vocational training in Germany
warn students about the risks of weak training programmes
compare youth unemployment rates across Europe
argue that apprenticeships deserve more respect as a route to a career
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘argue that apprenticeships deserve more respect as a route to a career’: yazar ilk paragrafta "apprenticeships deserve far more respect" diyor. ‘no longer useful’ yazar diplomayı küçümsemiyor, iki yolu eşit görüyor. ‘history’ Almanya yalnızca örnek. ‘warn’ zayıf programlar bir ayrıntı. ‘unemployment rates’ tek bir destek bilgisi.
exercises.passage:
In many countries, a university degree is still regarded as the natural route to a successful career, and vocational training is often seen as a second choice for students whose grades are weaker. I believe this attitude is mistaken, and that apprenticeships deserve far more respect than they generally receive.

An apprenticeship combines paid work with structured learning. The apprentice spends most of the week at a company, where skills are acquired under the guidance of experienced colleagues, and the remaining time at a college. Germany and Switzerland, which have long traditions of this kind of training, are often cited as examples: a large proportion of their young people enter the labour market through apprenticeships, and youth unemployment in both countries has generally been lower than the European average, although many other factors are undoubtedly involved.

The advantages for the learner are considerable. Apprentices earn a wage while they train, so they usually finish without the debts which many graduates carry. They also gain practical competence that employers value, and many are offered a permanent position by the firm which trained them. For employers, the arrangement provides a reliable supply of workers whose skills match their actual needs.

Of course, apprenticeships are not suitable for everyone, and a weak programme which offers cheap labour rather than real training is worse than useless. Quality depends on careful regulation, clear standards and genuine cooperation between companies and colleges. These conditions are rarely created quickly, which partly explains why some countries have struggled to copy the German model.

Nevertheless, the main obstacle is cultural rather than practical. As long as parents and teachers present vocational training as a failure, talented students will avoid it. Treating both paths as equally respectable would benefit young people and contribute to the prosperity of the economy as a whole.

exercises.question: According to the passage, one advantage of apprenticeships for learners is that they ----.
options: are guaranteed a permanent job by the firm
earn a wage and usually avoid large debts
spend most of the week at a college
never need to study any theory
receive higher salaries than all graduates
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘earn a wage and usually avoid large debts’: çıraklar eğitim alırken ücret kazanıyor ve mezunların taşıdığı borçlar olmadan bitiriyor. ‘guaranteed’ yanlış, metin "many are offered" diyor. ‘college’ ters, haftanın çoğu şirkette geçiyor. ‘theory’ yanlış, kalan zaman okulda geçiyor. ‘higher salaries’ metinde yok.
exercises.passage:
In many countries, a university degree is still regarded as the natural route to a successful career, and vocational training is often seen as a second choice for students whose grades are weaker. I believe this attitude is mistaken, and that apprenticeships deserve far more respect than they generally receive.

An apprenticeship combines paid work with structured learning. The apprentice spends most of the week at a company, where skills are acquired under the guidance of experienced colleagues, and the remaining time at a college. Germany and Switzerland, which have long traditions of this kind of training, are often cited as examples: a large proportion of their young people enter the labour market through apprenticeships, and youth unemployment in both countries has generally been lower than the European average, although many other factors are undoubtedly involved.

The advantages for the learner are considerable. Apprentices earn a wage while they train, so they usually finish without the debts which many graduates carry. They also gain practical competence that employers value, and many are offered a permanent position by the firm which trained them. For employers, the arrangement provides a reliable supply of workers whose skills match their actual needs.

Of course, apprenticeships are not suitable for everyone, and a weak programme which offers cheap labour rather than real training is worse than useless. Quality depends on careful regulation, clear standards and genuine cooperation between companies and colleges. These conditions are rarely created quickly, which partly explains why some countries have struggled to copy the German model.

Nevertheless, the main obstacle is cultural rather than practical. As long as parents and teachers present vocational training as a failure, talented students will avoid it. Treating both paths as equally respectable would benefit young people and contribute to the prosperity of the economy as a whole.

units.title: Karşılaştırma metinleri
units.description: İki şeyi ya da iki görüşü karşılaştıran metinlerde benzerlik ve farkı yakala
units.guide:
## Strateji
YDS fen metinlerinin çoğu iki şeyi (iki kayaç, iki enerji kaynağı) ya da iki görüşü (eski kuram, yeni kuram) karşılaştırır. Sorular da buna göre gelir: *One difference between X and Y is that ----*, *Unlike X, Y ----*, *Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a difference …?* En sık tuzak, X'in özelliğini Y'ye yapıştıran şıktır.

## Nasıl uygulanır
1. İlk paragrafta karşılaştırılan iki şeyi bul ve kafanda iki sütun aç: X | Y.
2. Karşıtlık işaretlerinde dur: *by contrast, whereas, while, on the other hand, unlike, in contrast to*. İşaretten önceki bilgi bir sütuna, sonraki diğerine gider.
3. Benzerlik işaretlerini de not et: *both, similarly, like, also*.
4. Her özelliğin yanına kısa bir etiket yaz: neden, hız, yer, sıcaklık, maliyet.
5. Şıkta iki şey birlikte geçiyorsa sütunlarını kontrol et; yer değiştirmiş bilgi en sık yanlış şıktır.

## Örnek
*Surface currents are driven mainly by wind. Deep currents, by contrast, are driven by differences in density.*
- X (yüzey) → rüzgâr | Y (derin) → yoğunluk farkı.
- Yanlış şık: "Deep currents are driven by wind." (sütun değişmiş)

## Sınav ipucu
"NOT mentioned" sorusunda her şıkkı metinde tek tek ara ve bulduğunu ele. Metinde "aynıdır" denen bir özellik (*look identical*) fark olarak sunulmuşsa doğru cevap odur.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
options: the reasons why granite is used in modern buildings

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the differences between how igneous and sedimentary rocks are formed and where they are found’: metin iki kayaç grubunun oluşumunu, fosil içeriğini ve bulunduğu yerleri karşılaştırıyor. ‘granite’ yalnızca bir örnek. ‘history’ bilim insanlarının tarihi anlatılmıyor. ‘dangers’ metinde tehlike yok. ‘methods’ fosil çıkarma yöntemi anlatılmıyor.
exercises.passage:
Scientists use a classification which divides rocks into three main groups according to the way in which they were formed. Two of these groups, igneous and sedimentary rocks, offer a useful contrast, since they are produced by almost opposite processes.

Igneous rocks are formed when hot liquid rock, which is known as magma, cools and becomes solid. If the cooling takes place deep underground, it is extremely slow, and large crystals have time to grow; granite is a typical example. When liquid rock reaches the surface and cools rapidly, by contrast, the crystals remain tiny, and a rock with very fine grains is produced. Because they form from a hot liquid, igneous rocks rarely contain fossils.

Sedimentary rocks have a very different origin. They are built up through the gradual accumulation of particles of older rock, sand, mud and the remains of living organisms, which are carried by rivers and wind and deposited in layers, often on the floor of lakes and seas. Over millions of years, the weight of the upper layers presses the lower ones together, and minerals dissolved in water act as a kind of natural glue. Limestone, for example, is formed in this way. Since the process takes place at relatively low temperatures, plants and animals can be preserved, which explains why almost all fossils are found in sedimentary rock.

The two groups also differ in where they are encountered. Igneous rocks make up most of the Earth's crust by volume, yet sedimentary rocks cover roughly three quarters of the land surface as a thin outer layer. For this reason, the rocks which most people see on a walk are likely to be sedimentary, even though igneous rock lies beneath them.

The groups are not completely separate, however. Over long periods, any rock can be broken down, melted or changed into another type, a continuous transformation that scientists call the rock cycle.

exercises.question: According to the passage, one difference between igneous and sedimentary rocks is that ----.
options: igneous rocks form at lower temperatures than sedimentary rocks
sedimentary rocks make up most of the crust by volume

sedimentary rocks often contain fossils, while igneous rocks rarely do
sedimentary rocks cool from magma deep underground
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘sedimentary rocks often contain fossils, while igneous rocks rarely do’: fosillerin neredeyse tamamı tortul kayaçta bulunuyor; magmatik kayaçlar sıcak sıvıdan oluştuğu için nadiren fosil içeriyor. ‘lower temperatures’ ters, düşük sıcaklık tortul kayaçlara ait. ‘volume’ ters, hacimce kabuğun çoğu magmatik. ‘layers of mud’ tortul kayacın özelliği, sütunlar karışmış. ‘magma’ magmatik kayacın özelliği.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
options: Why Wegener's Mechanism Was Finally Proved Correct
The Fossils of Brazil and West Africa
Land Bridges or Moving Continents: A Debate Settled by the Ocean Floor
How Physicists Discovered Pangaea
Underwater Mountains and Their Dangers
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Land Bridges or Moving Continents: A Debate Settled by the Ocean Floor’: metin iki görüşü karşılaştırıyor ve tartışmanın okyanus tabanı haritalarıyla çözüldüğünü anlatıyor. ‘Mechanism’ ters, Wegener’in mekanizması yanlış çıktı. ‘Brazil’ yalnızca bir kanıt örneği. ‘Physicists’ ters, fizikçiler Wegener’in fikrini reddetti. ‘Dangers’ metinde tehlike yok.
exercises.passage:
Until the early twentieth century, most geologists assumed that the continents had always occupied roughly the same positions. Similarities between distant lands, such as identical fossils found in Brazil and West Africa, were explained by ancient land bridges which were thought to have connected the continents before sinking into the ocean. This view seemed plausible because nobody could imagine a force strong enough to move whole continents.

In 1912, the German scientist Alfred Wegener proposed a radically different explanation. He argued that the continents had once formed a single huge landmass, which he later called Pangaea, and that they had slowly drifted apart over millions of years. His evidence came from several fields: the coastlines of South America and Africa fit together remarkably well, rock layers on both sides of the Atlantic match, and fossils of the same land animals and plants appear on continents which are now separated by thousands of kilometres.

The two views differed not only in their conclusions but also in their weaknesses. The land-bridge theory could account for the fossils, yet it could not explain why the rock layers matched or why the bridges had left no trace on the ocean floor. Wegener's theory, on the other hand, explained the evidence well but lacked a credible mechanism. He suggested that the continents moved through the ocean floor like ships, an idea which physicists rejected as impossible. As a result, his proposal was treated with scepticism and dismissed by most experts for several decades.

The debate was finally settled in the 1960s, after detailed mapping of the ocean floor showed that new crust is continuously created along underwater mountain ranges. This discovery led to the theory of plate tectonics, according to which the continents are carried on huge moving plates. Wegener's central claim was thus confirmed, although the mechanism turned out to be different from the one he had imagined.

options: could not explain the similar fossils on distant continents
was rejected by physicists as impossible

was later supported by mapping of the ocean floor

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘could not explain why rock layers on both sides of the Atlantic matched’: kara köprüsü kuramı fosilleri açıklayabiliyordu ama eşleşen kaya katmanlarını açıklayamıyordu. ‘similar fossils’ ters, bunu açıklayabiliyordu. ‘physicists’ fizikçiler Wegener’in mekanizmasını reddetti. ‘mapping’ haritalama Wegener’i destekledi. ‘ships’ Wegener’in önerisi, sütunlar karışmış.

His evidence came from several fields: the coastlines of South America and Africa fit together remarkably well, rock layers on both sides of the Atlantic match, and fossils of the same land animals and plants appear on continents which are now separated by thousands of kilometres.

The two views differed not only in their conclusions but also in their weaknesses. The land-bridge theory could account for the fossils, yet it could not explain why the rock layers matched or why the bridges had left no trace on the ocean floor. Wegener's theory, on the other hand, explained the evidence well but lacked a credible mechanism. He suggested that the continents moved through the ocean floor like ships, an idea which physicists rejected as impossible. exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the causes and behaviour of surface and deep ocean currents’: metin iki akıntı türünü neden, hız ve derinlik açısından karşılaştırıyor. ‘Pacific’ metinde geçmiyor. ‘climates’ yalnızca Gulf Stream örneğinde geçiyor. ‘river water’ metin nehir suyunu karşılaştırmıyor. ‘rivers’ nehirlerin hızı konu değil.
exercises.passage:
The water in the oceans is never still. It is moved by two broad types of current, which differ in their causes, their speed and the depth at which they operate.

Surface currents affect roughly the upper few hundred metres of the ocean and are driven mainly by wind. As steady winds blow across the sea, they drag the surface water along with them, and because of the Earth's rotation the moving water is turned to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere. The result is a pattern of huge circular systems, which are called gyres, in every major ocean basin. Surface currents can reach relatively high velocities; the Gulf Stream, for example, may travel at more than two metres per second in places, and it carries warm water from the tropics towards north-west Europe.

In contrast to surface currents, deep currents are driven by differences in density rather than by wind. Cold water is denser than warm water, and salty water is denser than fresh water. When seawater near the poles is cooled and becomes saltier as sea ice forms, it sinks towards the ocean floor and spreads slowly across the basins. Because this process depends on both temperature and salt, it is often described as thermohaline circulation. Deep currents usually move only a few centimetres per second, and it is estimated that a single portion of water may take several hundred to a thousand years to complete the whole journey.

Although the two systems are distinct, they are closely linked, since water which sinks in one place must eventually rise somewhere else. Together they carry heat, oxygen and nutrients around the planet. For this reason, scientists are concerned that warming and the melting of polar ice, which adds fresh water to the sea, could weaken deep circulation and alter regional climates.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘explain how dissolved salt makes seawater behave differently from fresh water’: metin yoğunluk, donma ve soğuma açısından farkları tuza bağlıyor. ‘warn swimmers’ Ölü Deniz yalnızca bir örnek. ‘removed’ tuz giderme anlatılmıyor. ‘winter roads’ yalnızca aynı ilkenin örneği, karşı çıkılmıyor. ‘identical’ ters; yalnızca bardakta aynı görünürler.
exercises.passage:
Seawater and fresh water look identical in a glass, yet they behave differently in several important ways. The difference comes almost entirely from dissolved salts, mostly sodium chloride, which make up about 3.5 percent of the weight of typical seawater. In river and lake water, the concentration of salts is usually far lower, often less than 0.1 percent.

The first consequence concerns density. Because the dissolved salt adds mass without adding much volume, seawater is slightly denser than fresh water. This is why swimmers float more easily in the sea, and why, where a large river enters the ocean, the lighter fresh water tends to spread out over the salty water below instead of mixing with it at once. In extreme cases such as the Dead Sea, whose water contains almost ten times as much salt as the ocean, a person can lie on the surface without any effort.

Salt also changes the temperature at which water freezes. Fresh water turns to ice at zero degrees Celsius, whereas ordinary seawater does not freeze until it reaches about minus two degrees. The same principle is applied on winter roads, where salt is spread to prevent ice from forming. When sea ice does form, most of the salt is pushed out of the growing crystals, so the ice itself is much less salty than the water around it.

A third difference relates to the way the two waters behave as they cool. Fresh water is densest at about four degrees, so the coldest water stays at the top of a lake and the bottom rarely freezes, which allows fish to survive the winter. In seawater, the density goes on increasing as the temperature falls, and cold surface water simply sinks. These small chemical differences therefore have large effects on climate and on life.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘why two materials made of the same element have very different properties’: elmas ve grafit aynı karbondan oluşur; farkı atomların dizilişi açıklar. ‘taken out of the ground’ madencilik anlatılmıyor. ‘valuable’ ters, değerli olan elmastır. ‘manufactured’ kalem ve pil yalnızca kullanım örneği. ‘most common’ metinde böyle bir iddia yok.
exercises.passage:
Diamond and graphite seem to have almost nothing in common. One is the hardest natural material known and is highly valued; the other is soft, dark and slippery, and is used in the 'lead' of ordinary pencils. Yet both are composed of exactly the same element, carbon. The striking differences between them are explained entirely by the way in which their atoms are arranged.

In diamond, every carbon atom is joined by strong bonds to four neighbouring atoms, which form a rigid three-dimensional network that extends in all directions. Because no part of this network is weaker than the rest, a great deal of energy is required to break it, and as a result diamond is extremely hard. All the electrons are tightly held in these bonds, so diamond does not conduct electricity, and its regular structure allows light to pass through and be split into bright colours.

In graphite, by contrast, each atom is bonded to only three neighbours, and the atoms form flat sheets arranged like a stack of paper. Within each sheet the bonds are very strong, but the attraction between the sheets is weak, which allows them to slide over one another. This is why graphite feels smooth and leaves a mark when it is drawn across paper. Moreover, one electron from each atom is free to move along the sheets, which makes graphite a good conductor of electricity and explains its use in batteries.

Surprisingly, graphite rather than diamond is the more stable form under normal conditions. Diamonds are formed only under the enormous pressure and heat found deep inside the Earth, and in theory they slowly change into graphite at the surface. In practice, however, this conversion is so extremely slow that it would take far longer than a human lifetime to observe.

options: each of its atoms is bonded to four neighbours

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘one electron from each atom can move along the sheets’: metin bunu doğrudan iletkenliğin nedeni olarak veriyor. ‘four neighbours’ elmasın özelliği. ‘weak’ ters, levhalar içindeki bağlar güçlü; zayıf olan levhalar arası çekim. ‘light’ elmasın özelliği. ‘pressure’ elmasın oluşumuyla ilgili.

exercises.passage:
Diamond and graphite seem to have almost nothing in common. One is the hardest natural material known and is highly valued; the other is soft, dark and slippery, and is used in the 'lead' of ordinary pencils. Yet both are composed of exactly the same element, carbon. The striking differences between them are explained entirely by the way in which their atoms are arranged.

In diamond, every carbon atom is joined by strong bonds to four neighbouring atoms, which form a rigid three-dimensional network that extends in all directions. Because no part of this network is weaker than the rest, a great deal of energy is required to break it, and as a result diamond is extremely hard. All the electrons are tightly held in these bonds, so diamond does not conduct electricity, and its regular structure allows light to pass through and be split into bright colours.

In graphite, by contrast, each atom is bonded to only three neighbours, and the atoms form flat sheets arranged like a stack of paper. Within each sheet the bonds are very strong, but the attraction between the sheets is weak, which allows them to slide over one another. This is why graphite feels smooth and leaves a mark when it is drawn across paper. Moreover, one electron from each atom is free to move along the sheets, which makes graphite a good conductor of electricity and explains its use in batteries.

Surprisingly, graphite rather than diamond is the more stable form under normal conditions. Diamonds are formed only under the enormous pressure and heat found deep inside the Earth, and in theory they slowly change into graphite at the surface. In practice, however, this conversion is so extremely slow that it would take far longer than a human lifetime to observe.

exercises.question: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: Fusion has already replaced fission as the main source of nuclear power.
Fission and fusion release nuclear energy in opposite ways, and only fission is used commercially today.
Fission is safer than fusion because it produces no waste.
The Sun produces its energy by splitting heavy atoms.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Fission and fusion release nuclear energy in opposite ways, and only fission is used commercially today’: metin iki süreci karşılaştırıyor ve füzyonun hâlâ deneysel olduğunu söylüyor. ‘replaced’ ters. ‘safer’ yanlış, fisyon uzun ömürlü atık üretir. ‘splitting’ Güneş atomları birleştirir. ‘never’ yanlış, fisyon 1950’lerden beri elektrik üretiyor.
exercises.passage:
Nuclear power stations and the Sun both release energy from the nuclei of atoms, but they do so in opposite ways. Fission splits heavy atoms apart, while fusion joins light atoms together. Comparing the two processes helps to explain why one has been used for electricity since the 1950s and the other remains an experimental technology.

In fission, a heavy nucleus such as uranium is struck by a neutron and breaks into two smaller pieces, releasing a large amount of energy and further neutrons. These neutrons can split other nuclei, which produces a chain reaction that must be carefully controlled inside a reactor. The heat is used to boil water and drive turbines. Fission produces no carbon dioxide during operation, but it generates radioactive waste, some of which remains dangerous for thousands of years and has to be stored safely.

Fusion works in the reverse direction. When very light nuclei, usually forms of hydrogen, are forced together, they combine into helium and release even more energy per kilogram of fuel than fission. This is the reaction that powers the Sun. Its fuel is far more plentiful, and it produces much less long-lived waste. The difficulty is that the nuclei repel each other strongly, so fusion only occurs at temperatures of many millions of degrees, at which matter becomes a gas of charged particles that must be held in place by powerful magnetic fields.

For decades, fusion experiments consumed more energy than they produced. In 2022, researchers at a laboratory in the United States reported that, for the first time, a fusion reaction had released more energy than the lasers had delivered to the fuel, although the facility as a whole still used far more power than it generated. Most experts therefore expect fission to remain the only commercial form of nuclear energy for at least the next few decades.

exercises.question: According to the passage, one advantage of fusion over fission is that fusion ----.
options: takes place at relatively low temperatures
has been used in power stations since the 1950s
does not require any magnetic fields
produces much less long-lived waste
splits uranium into smaller pieces
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘produces much less long-lived waste’: metin füzyonun yakıtının bol olduğunu ve çok daha az uzun ömürlü atık ürettiğini söylüyor. ‘low temperatures’ ters, milyonlarca derece gerekir. ‘1950s’ fisyona ait. ‘magnetic’ ters, güçlü manyetik alan gerekir. ‘uranium’ fisyonun özelliği; sütunlar karışmış.

nodes.title: Cümle çözümleme
nodes.description: Ünitenin metinlerinden uzun cümleler: ana fiil, yan cümle, karşılaştırma yapısı ve çeviri

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘Similarities between distant lands, such as identical fossils found in Brazil and West Africa, were explained by ancient land bridges which were thought to have connected the continents before sinking into the ocean.’
options: found
were thought
were explained
to have connected
sinking
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘were explained’. İskelet: Similarities between distant lands (özne) + were explained (ana fiil, edilgen) + by ancient land bridges. ‘found’ fossils sözcüğünü niteleyen sıfat-fiildir. ‘were thought’ which yan cümlesinin fiilidir. ‘to have connected’ mastardır. ‘sinking’ before’dan sonra gelen -ing biçimidir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘Because the dissolved salt adds mass without adding much volume, seawater is slightly denser than fresh water.’
options: adds
adding
is
dissolved
denser
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘is’. İskelet: seawater (özne) + is (ana fiil) + slightly denser than fresh water. ‘adds’ Because ile başlayan yan cümlenin fiilidir. ‘adding’ without’tan sonra gelen -ing biçimidir. ‘dissolved’ salt sözcüğünü niteleyen sıfat-fiildir. ‘denser’ fiil değil, karşılaştırma sıfatıdır.

exercises.question: Cümledeki ‘which’ neyi nitelemektedir? ‘Since the process takes place at relatively low temperatures, plants and animals can be preserved, which explains why almost all fossils are found in sedimentary rock.’
options: the fact that plants and animals can be preserved
relatively low temperatures
the process
almost all fossils
sedimentary rock
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the fact that plants and animals can be preserved’: virgülden sonra gelen which burada tek bir ismi değil, önceki cümlenin tamamını niteler (Türkçede "bu da"). ‘relatively low temperatures’ yan cümlede bir neden. ‘the process’ Since yan cümlesinin öznesi. ‘almost all fossils’ which cümlesinin içinde. ‘sedimentary rock’ cümlenin sonundaki yer bilgisi.

exercises.question: Cümledeki ‘whose water’ ifadesi neyin suyundan söz eder? ‘In extreme cases such as the Dead Sea, whose water contains almost ten times as much salt as the ocean, a person can lie on the surface without any effort.’
options: the ocean
a person
the surface
extreme cases
the Dead Sea
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the Dead Sea’: whose virgülden hemen önceki isme bağlanır; okyanustan on kat tuzlu olan Ölü Deniz’in suyudur. ‘the ocean’ karşılaştırmanın ikinci öğesidir. ‘a person’ ana cümlenin öznesidir. ‘the surface’ ana cümlede yer bildirir. ‘extreme cases’ genel bir ifadedir, su onlara ait değil.

exercises.question: ‘Surprisingly, graphite rather than diamond is the more stable form under normal conditions.’ cümlesinin anlamı hangisidir?
options: Şaşırtıcı biçimde, normal koşullarda elmas grafite göre daha kararlı bir biçimdir.
Şaşırtıcı biçimde, normal koşullarda daha kararlı olan elmas değil grafittir.
Grafit ve elmas normal koşullarda eşit derecede kararlıdır.
Grafit yalnızca olağanüstü koşullarda kararlıdır.
Elmas, grafitten daha sert olduğu için daha kararlıdır.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘…daha kararlı olan elmas değil grafittir’: A rather than B = B değil A; özne graphite’tır. ‘grafite göre’ geçen şık karşılaştırmayı ters çeviriyor. ‘eşit’ derecesi metinde yok. ‘olağanüstü’ normal conditions ifadesini bozuyor. ‘sert’ geçen şık metinde olmayan bir neden kuruyor ve sonucu ters çeviriyor.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Although the two systems are distinct, they are closely linked, since water which sinks in one place must eventually rise somewhere else.’
options: İki sistem birbirinden ayrı olduğu için hiçbir bağlantıları yoktur.
İki sistem aynı olsa da bir yerde batan su asla yükselmez.
Bir yerde yükselen su başka bir yerde hemen batmak zorunda olduğu için sistemler ayrıdır.
İki sistem birbirinden ayrı olsa da yakından bağlantılıdır, çünkü bir yerde batan su eninde sonunda başka bir yerde yükselmelidir.
İki sistem yakından bağlantılı olsaydı, su bir yerde batıp başka yerde yükselebilirdi.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘…çünkü bir yerde batan su eninde sonunda başka bir yerde yükselmelidir’: although = -se de, since = çünkü, which sinks = batan. ‘hiçbir’ geçen şık zıtlığı neden-sonuca çevirip anlamı tersine çeviriyor. ‘asla’ ve ‘aynı’ anlamı bozuyor. ‘hemen’ geçen şık batma ile yükselmeyi yer değiştiriyor. ‘olsaydı’ gerçek durumu varsayıma çeviriyor.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Most experts therefore expect fission to remain the only commercial form of nuclear energy for at least the next few decades.’
options: Bu nedenle bazı uzmanlar, füzyonun birkaç yıl içinde ticari hale gelmesini bekliyor.
Bu nedenle uzmanların çoğu, fisyonun en az önümüzdeki birkaç on yıl boyunca nükleer enerjinin tek ticari biçimi olarak kalmasını bekliyor.
Uzmanların çoğu, fisyonun önümüzdeki on yıllarda tamamen terk edileceğini düşünüyor.
Uzmanların hiçbiri fisyonun ticari bir enerji biçimi olarak kalmasını beklemiyor.
Bu nedenle uzmanlar, nükleer enerjinin en fazla birkaç on yıl daha kullanılacağını söylüyor.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘…tek ticari biçimi olarak kalmasını bekliyor’: most experts = uzmanların çoğu, at least = en az, remain = kalmak. ‘füzyonun’ geçen şık konuyu ve niceleyiciyi değiştiriyor. ‘terk’ geçen şık remain anlamını tersine çeviriyor. ‘hiçbiri’ olumsuzluk ekliyor. ‘fazla’ at least ifadesini "en fazla"ya çeviriyor.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Yer kabuğunun hacimce büyük bölümünü magmatik kayaçlar oluşturur, ancak kara yüzeyinin yaklaşık dörtte üçünü tortul kayaçlar kaplar.’
options: Sedimentary rocks form most of the crust, while igneous rocks occupy three quarters of the land.
Igneous rocks cover only a quarter of the Earth's surface because they are rare.
Neither igneous nor sedimentary rocks are found on the land surface.
Igneous rocks make up most of the Earth's crust by volume, yet sedimentary rocks cover roughly three quarters of the land surface.
About three quarters of the crust consists of sedimentary layers.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Igneous rocks make up most of the Earth's crust by volume, yet sedimentary rocks cover roughly three quarters of the land surface’: make up = oluşturmak, yet = ancak, roughly = yaklaşık. ‘occupy’ geçen şık iki kayacın yerini değiştiriyor. ‘rare’ ve ‘quarter’ metinde olmayan bir bilgi kuruyor. ‘Neither’ olumsuzluk ekliyor. ‘consists’ geçen şık kabuk ile kara yüzeyini karıştırıyor.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Wegener'in temel iddiası böylece doğrulandı, ancak mekanizmanın onun hayal ettiğinden farklı olduğu ortaya çıktı.’
options: Wegener's central claim was thus confirmed, although the mechanism turned out to be different from the one he had imagined.
Wegener's central claim was rejected because the mechanism he had imagined was wrong.
Wegener confirmed his own claim by imagining a new mechanism.
Both Wegener's claim and his mechanism were finally confirmed.
The mechanism was confirmed, but Wegener's central claim turned out to be false.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Wegener's central claim was thus confirmed, although the mechanism turned out to be different from the one he had imagined’: "ortaya çıktı" = turned out. ‘rejected’ iddianın doğrulanmasını reddedilmeye çeviriyor. ‘imagining’ geçen şık özneyi ve anlamı değiştiriyor. ‘Both’ mekanizmayı da doğrulanmış sayıyor. ‘false’ iddia ile mekanizmanın yerini değiştiriyor.

exercises.question: The passage mainly ----.
options: argues that wind turbines should replace solar panels
describes the history of fossil fuels
explains how solar panels are manufactured
criticises energy planners for ignoring storage
compares the strengths and weaknesses of solar and wind power
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘compares the strengths and weaknesses of solar and wind power’: metin zamanlama, ölçek, arazi kullanımı ve maliyet açısından iki kaynağı karşılaştırıyor. ‘replace’ ters, metin ikisini birleştirmeyi öneriyor. ‘history’ fosil yakıtların tarihi anlatılmıyor. ‘manufactured’ üretim süreci yok. ‘criticises’ planlamacılar eleştirilmiyor, depolamayı onlar öneriyor.
exercises.passage:
Solar panels and wind turbines are now the two fastest-growing sources of electricity in the world, and both produce power without burning fossil fuels. They are frequently mentioned together, but they have quite different strengths and weaknesses, and understanding these differences is essential for planning a reliable energy system.

The most obvious contrast concerns timing. Solar panels generate electricity only during daylight, with a peak around midday and a sharp decline in winter, especially far from the equator. Wind, by contrast, can blow at any hour, and in many northern countries it is stronger in winter and at night. For this reason, the two sources tend to complement each other: when one produces little, the other may produce more, so the fluctuation in their combined output is smaller.

They also differ in scale and flexibility. Solar panels can be installed almost anywhere, from the roof of a single house to huge fields in the desert, and they contain no moving parts, which keeps maintenance costs low. Wind turbines are most efficient when they are very large, and the optimal sites are usually located offshore or on exposed hills, where construction is expensive and sometimes opposed by local residents who object to the noise or the change in the landscape.

In terms of land use, a solar farm covers the ground almost completely, whereas the space between wind turbines can still be used for farming. Each technology, however, has an environmental cost: solar panels require mining for minerals, and turbines may pose a risk to birds and bats.

The cost of both has plummeted over the past decade, and in many regions new solar and wind plants now produce electricity more cheaply than new coal or gas plants. Most energy planners therefore argue that the question is not which one to choose, but how to combine them with storage and modern grids in order to maximise reliability.

exercises.question: According to the passage, solar and wind power tend to complement each other because ----.
options: both work best at midday in summer
wind turbines contain no moving parts
they often produce most of their power at different times
both are cheaper than storage systems
solar farms leave space for farming
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘they often produce most of their power at different times’: güneş gündüz ve yazın, rüzgâr ise birçok kuzey ülkesinde kışın ve gece daha güçlü. ‘midday’ yalnızca güneşe ait. ‘moving parts’ ters, hareketli parçası olmayan güneş panelidir. ‘storage’ metinde böyle bir karşılaştırma yok. ‘farming’ ters, tarım için yer bırakan rüzgârdır.

Wind turbines are most efficient when they are very large, and the optimal sites are usually located offshore or on exposed hills, where construction is expensive and sometimes opposed by local residents who object to the noise or the change in the landscape.

In terms of land use, a solar farm covers the ground almost completely, whereas the space between wind turbines can still be used for farming. Each technology, however, has an environmental cost: solar panels require mining for minerals, and turbines may pose a risk to birds and bats.

The cost of both has plummeted over the past decade, and in many regions new solar and wind plants now produce electricity more cheaply than new coal or gas plants. Most energy planners therefore argue that the question is not which one to choose, but how to combine them with storage and modern grids in order to maximise reliability.

Solar panels and wind turbines are now the two fastest-growing sources of electricity in the world, and both produce power without burning fossil fuels. They are frequently mentioned together, but they have quite different strengths and weaknesses, and understanding these differences is essential for planning a reliable energy system.

The most obvious contrast concerns timing. Solar panels generate electricity only during daylight, with a peak around midday and a sharp decline in winter, especially far from the equator. Wind, by contrast, can blow at any hour, and in many northern countries it is stronger in winter and at night. For this reason, the two sources tend to complement each other: when one produces little, the other may produce more, so the fluctuation in their combined output is smaller.

They also differ in scale and flexibility. Solar panels can be installed almost anywhere, from the roof of a single house to huge fields in the desert, and they contain no moving parts, which keeps maintenance costs low. Wind turbines are most efficient when they are very large, and the optimal sites are usually located offshore or on exposed hills, where construction is expensive and sometimes opposed by local residents who object to the noise or the change in the landscape.

In terms of land use, a solar farm covers the ground almost completely, whereas the space between wind turbines can still be used for farming. Each technology, however, has an environmental cost: solar panels require mining for minerals, and turbines may pose a risk to birds and bats.

The cost of both has plummeted over the past decade, and in many regions new solar and wind plants now produce electricity more cheaply than new coal or gas plants. Most energy planners therefore argue that the question is not which one to choose, but how to combine them with storage and modern grids in order to maximise reliability.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘compare two technologies that could replace petrol and diesel engines’: ilk cümle iki teknolojiyi tanıtıyor, metin verim, şarj ve kullanım alanı açısından karşılaştırıyor. ‘persuade’ metin taraf tutmuyor. ‘exhaust’ yalnızca giriş bilgisi. ‘history’ tarih anlatılmıyor. ‘banned’ metinde böyle bir öneri yok.
exercises.passage:
As countries try to reduce emissions from transport, two technologies are competing to replace petrol and diesel engines: battery electric vehicles and vehicles powered by hydrogen fuel cells. Both use electric motors and produce no exhaust gases on the road, but they store and supply energy in very different ways.

A battery vehicle stores electricity directly in a large battery, which is charged from the grid. The main advantage of this approach is efficiency: roughly 70 to 90 percent of the electricity taken from the grid ends up turning the wheels. Charging, however, can take from about half an hour to many hours, and heavy batteries reduce the load which a vehicle can carry.

A fuel-cell vehicle, by contrast, carries hydrogen gas in a strong tank. Inside the fuel cell, the hydrogen reacts with oxygen from the air to generate electricity, and the only by-product is water. Such a vehicle can be refuelled in a few minutes and can travel long distances, which makes the technology attractive for lorries, buses and ships. Its weakness lies in the chain of conversions that is involved. Electricity must first be used to produce hydrogen, which is then compressed, transported and converted back into electricity, and energy is lost at every stage. As a result, it is estimated that only around 30 to 40 percent of the original energy reaches the wheels. In addition, most hydrogen is still produced from natural gas, which releases carbon dioxide.

At present, batteries clearly dominate the market for private cars, and the number of hydrogen filling stations remains very small. Many analysts believe, however, that hydrogen may still play a role in heavy transport and industry, where long ranges and fast refuelling are more important than efficiency.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘energy is lost at each stage of producing and converting hydrogen’: üretim, sıkıştırma, taşıma ve geri dönüştürmenin her aşamasında enerji kaybolur. ‘water’ yan ürün verimsizliğin nedeni değil. ‘refuelled’ bir avantaj. ‘heavier’ metinde ağır olan bataryalar. ‘long distances’ ters, uzun mesafe gidebilirler.

units.description: Sayı ve yüzde içeren sağlık metinlerini doğru oku
units.guide:
## Strateji

YDS’nin sağlık ve bilim metinleri sık sık sayı, yüzde ve oran içerir. Sorular çoğu zaman rakamın kendisini değil, **neyi ölçtüğünü** sorar: hangi grup, hangi yıl, artış mı azalış mı, kesin bilgi mi tahmin mi. Çeldiriciler metindeki gerçek bir rakamı yanlış bağlamla eşleştirir; rakamı tanıdığın için şıkkı doğru sanırsın.

## Nasıl uygulanır

1. Her rakamın yanına kısa bir not yaz: *kim / ne zaman / neyi ölçüyor*.

2. Oran ile toplamı ayır: *rate* ve *number* farklı şeylerdir; biri düşerken öteki artabilir.

3. Kaçınma ifadelerini işaretle: *about, roughly, nearly, more than, it is estimated that*. Şıkta *exactly, always, certainly* varsa dikkat et.

4. Yön kelimelerini işaretle: *rose, fell, doubled, halved, a quarter*.

5. Şıktaki rakamı metinde bul ve cümlenin tamamını oku.

## Örnek

*About 1.3 billion adults have hypertension, and nearly half of them are unaware of it.* Soru “Kaç kişi durumundan habersiz?” ise cevap *nearly half* olur; *1.3 billion* hastaların toplamıdır. *About* yerine *exactly* diyen bir şık metni aşırı kesinleştirir.

## Sınav ipucu

Rakamı doğru ama bağlamı yanlış şık YDS’nin en sevdiği tuzaktır. Bir şık metindeki sayıyı aynen tekrar ediyorsa, o sayının hangi gruba ve hangi yıla ait olduğunu mutlaka kontrol et.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
In late August 1854, a severe outbreak of cholera struck the Soho district of London, and within about ten days more than 500 people who lived in the area had died. At that time, most physicians believed that the disease was spread by bad air, a view which was rarely questioned. John Snow, a local physician, suspected that contaminated water was the real cause, and he set out to test this idea with a simple but systematic method.

Snow collected the addresses of the victims and marked each death on a map of the district. The deaths formed a dense cluster around a single public water pump on Broad Street. Interestingly, the exceptions supported his argument as well. Workers at a nearby brewery, who were given free beer and rarely drank from the pump, largely escaped the disease, and a workhouse with its own well recorded very few deaths. On the basis of this evidence, the handle of the pump was removed by local officials, although the number of new cases was already declining by then.

Snow also carried out a larger comparison, which he published the following year. Two companies supplied water to the same part of south London, but one of them took its water from a section of the River Thames which was heavily polluted by waste. According to his calculation, the death rate in households served by this company was roughly eight times higher than in those served by its rival.

Snow's work is commonly described as the starting point of modern epidemiology. His conclusions were not widely accepted during his lifetime, and the bacterium that causes cholera was not generally recognised until the 1880s. Nevertheless, his approach of counting cases, mapping them and comparing groups remains central to public health today.
options: The Brewery Workers Who Found a Cure for Cholera
Why Bad Air Spread Disease in Victorian London
How Counting and Mapping Cases Revealed the Cause of Cholera
The Rivalry Between Two Water Companies in London
How the Cholera Bacterium Was Identified in 1854
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘How Counting and Mapping Cases Revealed the Cause of Cholera’: metin Snow’un vakaları sayıp haritalayarak ve grupları karşılaştırarak suyu neden olarak göstermesini anlatır. ‘Brewery’ geçen başlık bir ayrıntıyı abartır, işçiler tedavi bulmadı; ‘Victorian’ geçen başlık Snow’un sorguladığı görüşü doğru sayar; ‘Rivalry’ geçen başlık yalnızca 3. paragrafın bir ayrıntısıdır; ‘Identified’ geçen başlık metinle çelişir, bakteri 1880’lere kadar genel kabul görmedi.

At that time, most physicians believed that the disease was spread by bad air, a view which was rarely questioned. John Snow, a local physician, suspected that contaminated water was the real cause, and he set out to test this idea with a simple but systematic method.

Snow collected the addresses of the victims and marked each death on a map of the district. The deaths formed a dense cluster around a single public water pump on Broad Street. Interestingly, the exceptions supported his argument as well. Workers at a nearby brewery, who were given free beer and rarely drank from the pump, largely escaped the disease, and a workhouse with its own well recorded very few deaths. On the basis of this evidence, the handle of the pump was removed by local officials, although the number of new cases was already declining by then.

Snow also carried out a larger comparison, which he published the following year. Two companies supplied water to the same part of south London, but one of them took its water from a section of the River Thames which was heavily polluted by waste. According to his calculation, the death rate in households served by this company was roughly eight times higher than in those served by its rival.

Snow's work is commonly described as the starting point of modern epidemiology. His conclusions were not widely accepted during his lifetime, and the bacterium that causes cholera was not generally recognised until the 1880s. Nevertheless, his approach of counting cases, mapping them and comparing groups remains central to public health today.

rapidly growing
hardly visible
carefully drawn

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
exercises.passage:
Before a new medicine can be prescribed to patients, it normally passes through a long series of clinical trials, each of which is designed to answer a different question. In the first phase, the drug is given to a small group of perhaps 20 to 100 volunteers, who are often healthy adults. The main aim at this stage is to establish whether it is safe and what dose the body can tolerate. If the results are acceptable, a second phase follows, in which several hundred patients with the target illness receive the treatment, so that researchers can form a preliminary judgment about its effectiveness.

The third phase is usually the largest and most expensive. It may involve hundreds or even thousands of participants, who are randomly assigned either to the new drug or to a comparison treatment, which is sometimes a placebo. In many such trials, neither the patients nor their doctors know who is receiving which treatment until the study ends, an arrangement which reduces the risk of biased results.

The statistics of this process are striking. It is estimated that only about one in ten drugs which enter the first phase is eventually approved for use, and the whole journey frequently takes ten years or more. Failure is most common in the second phase, when a substantial proportion of promising medicines turn out to be less effective than expected or to cause unacceptable harm. Estimates of the total cost of developing a single new drug vary considerably, but many of them exceed one billion dollars.

It could be argued that the system is too slow and costly, particularly for patients with rare or life-threatening conditions. Its supporters reply that these high failure rates are precisely the reason why a careful protocol is needed: in the absence of such testing, a wide range of ineffective or dangerous products would reach the market.
options: argue that clinical trials should be abolished because they are too expensive
describe the side effects of the placebos given in the third phase
compare the cost of medicines in different countries
show that most drugs fail during the first phase of testing
explain how new medicines are tested and why so few of them reach patients
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘explain how new medicines are tested and why so few of them reach patients’: metin evreleri tanıtır ve yaklaşık onda birlik onay oranını açıklar. ‘abolished’ geçen şık yazarın dengeli tutumunu aşırıya taşır; ‘placebos’ geçen şık metinde olmayan bir ayrıntıdır; ‘countries’ geçen şık metinde hiç yoktur; ‘first’ geçen şık yanlıştır, başarısızlık en çok ikinci evrede görülür.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
High blood pressure, or hypertension, is often described as a silent condition, since most people who have it feel no symptoms at all. Yet it is one of the most important risk factors for strokes, coronary heart disease and chronic kidney disease. According to a report published by the World Health Organization in 2023, about 1.3 billion adults between the ages of 30 and 79 are affected, roughly twice as many as in 1990. Much of this increase is attributed to population growth and ageing rather than to a rise in the rate itself.

The figures on diagnosis and treatment are even more worrying. The same report suggests that nearly half of the people with hypertension are unaware of their condition, simply because their blood pressure has never been measured. Among those who have been diagnosed, many do not receive treatment, and only about one in five of all adults with the condition has it under control. The gap is widest in low- and middle-income countries, where regular check-ups at a clinic are less common.

This situation is frustrating for physicians, because the condition is relatively easy to detect and cheap to treat. A reading takes only a few minutes, and effective medicines have been available for decades at a low cost. In addition, changes in lifestyle, such as reducing salt, staying physically active and limiting alcohol, can lower blood pressure considerably.

The WHO has estimated that if the proportion of patients whose blood pressure is controlled rose to about half, roughly 76 million deaths could be prevented between 2023 and 2050. Although such projections involve a degree of statistical uncertainty, they indicate that simple measures, applied on a large scale, could save an enormous number of lives.
options: Hypertension has become less common since 1990 thanks to new medicines.
Most people with high blood pressure experience serious symptoms early.
Hypertension affects a huge number of people, yet it often goes undiagnosed and uncontrolled despite being easy to treat.
Changes in lifestyle are more effective than medicine for every patient.
Hypertension is mainly a problem in high-income countries.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Hypertension affects a huge number of people, yet it often goes undiagnosed and uncontrolled…’: metin hastalığın yaygınlığını, teşhis ve kontrol açığını ve tedavinin ucuzluğunu anlatır. ‘thanks’ geçen şık yanlıştır, sayı 1990’dan beri yaklaşık iki katına çıktı; ‘symptoms’ geçen şık ‘silent condition’ ile çelişir; ‘lifestyle’ geçen şık metinde olmayan bir karşılaştırma yapar; ‘income’ geçen şık tersini söyler, açık en çok düşük ve orta gelirli ülkelerdedir.

exercises.question: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
Salt has been used for thousands of years to flavour and preserve food, but it is widely accepted that in large quantities it is harmful. The sodium which it contains raises blood pressure, and this in turn increases the risk of coronary heart disease and strokes. According to the guidelines of the World Health Organization, adults should consume less than five grams of salt per day, which is roughly one teaspoon. However, it is estimated that the global average is close to eleven grams, more than double the recommended amount.

One reason why intake remains so high is that most salt is not added at the table. In many high-income countries, around three quarters of the salt which people eat is already present in processed foods such as bread, cheese, sauces and ready meals. As a consequence, individual efforts to eat less salt have only a limited effect unless the composition of these products also changes.

The experience of the United Kingdom is often cited in this context. From the early 2000s, food companies were encouraged to reduce the salt in their products gradually, so that consumers would barely notice the difference in taste. At the same time, public campaigns were launched to raise awareness of the problem. Between 2003 and 2011, average salt intake in England is reported to have fallen by about 15 per cent, and this reduction was associated with a decline in average blood pressure.

However, it should be noted that the progress was not permanent, since the programme lost momentum in later years. According to the WHO, excess sodium intake is linked to nearly two million deaths each year worldwide. For this reason, many experts argue that mandatory limits for processed foods would be more effective than voluntary agreements with the industry.
options: Salt as an Ancient Method of Preserving Food
The Health Benefits of Eating More Salt
How Britain Permanently Solved Its Salt Problem
Teaspoons and Tables: Why Home Cooking Causes Disease
Hidden Salt: Why Reducing Intake Depends on Processed Food
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Hidden Salt: Why Reducing Intake Depends on Processed Food’: metin tuzun çoğunun işlenmiş gıdalardan geldiğini ve azaltmanın bunlara bağlı olduğunu anlatır. ‘Ancient’ geçen başlık yalnızca ilk cümleye dayanır; ‘Benefits’ geçen başlık metnin tersini söyler; ‘Permanently’ geçen başlık ilerlemenin kalıcı olmadığı bilgisiyle çelişir; ‘Cooking’ geçen başlık yanlıştır, tuzun çoğu evde ya da sofrada eklenmez.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
exercises.passage:
Road traffic crashes are rarely discussed as a public health problem, yet the numbers suggest that they should be. According to the World Health Organization, about 1.2 million people are killed on the world's roads every year, and between 20 and 50 million more are injured, many of whom are left with a permanent disability. For people aged 5 to 29, road injuries are the leading cause of death, ahead of any single infectious disease.

The burden is distributed very unequally. More than 90 per cent of these deaths occur in low- and middle-income countries, although these countries own only around 60 per cent of the world's vehicles. Over half of those who die are pedestrians, cyclists and motorcyclists, groups whose vulnerability is frequently ignored when roads are planned.

Research has identified a small number of underlying factors that explain much of the risk. Speed is perhaps the most important. It has been calculated that a one per cent increase in average speed leads to roughly a four per cent increase in the risk of a fatal crash. Safety equipment also makes a substantial difference: wearing a seat belt is thought to reduce the risk of death among drivers and front-seat passengers by about half, and a properly fastened helmet greatly lowers the chance of a fatal head injury, notably among motorcyclists.

The positive news is that these measures are well understood and relatively inexpensive. Several countries which have combined lower speed limits, strict enforcement and safer road design have reduced their death rates considerably. The WHO has therefore set the ambitious target of halving road traffic deaths by 2030, although the current trajectory suggests that this goal will be difficult to achieve.
options: the history of seat belts and helmets in rich countries
why pedestrians cause most road crashes
the decline of infectious diseases among young people
the scale of road traffic deaths and the measures that can reduce them
the cost of building safer roads in low-income countries
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the scale of road traffic deaths and the measures that can reduce them’: metin rakamları verir, risk etkenlerini ve çözümleri anlatır. ‘history’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘pedestrians’ geçen şık yanlıştır, yayalar kurbanların bir bölümüdür, kazaların nedeni olarak sunulmaz; ‘decline’ geçen şık konu dışıdır; ‘building’ geçen şık metinde ele alınmaz.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
Tuberculosis, which is caused by a bacterium that usually attacks the lungs, is one of the oldest diseases known to humans. Evidence of it has been found in Egyptian remains that are thousands of years old. Many people assume that it belongs to the past, but the latest figures contradict this view. According to the World Health Organization, about 10.8 million people fell ill with tuberculosis in 2023, and around 1.25 million died, which made it once again the world's leading cause of death from a single infectious agent.

The disease spreads through the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes. Remarkably, it is estimated that about a quarter of the world's population carries the bacterium. However, most of these people are not ill and cannot infect others, since their immune system keeps the infection under control. Only about 5 to 10 per cent of them will develop the active disease during their lifetime, and the risk is considerably higher for people whose immunity is weakened, for instance by HIV, diabetes or malnutrition.

Tuberculosis can be cured in the majority of cases. A standard course of antibiotics lasts about six months, and success rates of close to 90 per cent are reported for patients who complete it. The main difficulty is that the full course must be followed, even after the patient starts to feel better. When treatment is interrupted, resistant forms of the bacterium may emerge, and these are far more expensive and complex to treat.

The distribution of cases is highly uneven: a small number of countries in Asia and Africa account for most of them. Experts argue that the elimination of tuberculosis will depend not only on medicine but also on reducing poverty and overcrowding.
options: Tuberculosis has almost disappeared thanks to modern antibiotics.
Everyone who carries the bacterium will eventually develop the disease.
Tuberculosis was first described by doctors in ancient Egypt.
Resistant forms of tuberculosis are cheaper to treat than ordinary forms.
Tuberculosis remains a major cause of death, although it can be cured when treatment is completed.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Tuberculosis remains a major cause of death, although it can be cured when treatment is completed’. ‘disappeared’ geçen şık ‘the latest figures contradict this view’ ile çelişir; ‘eventually’ geçen şık yanlıştır, taşıyıcıların yalnızca yüzde 5–10’u hastalanır; ‘Egypt’ geçen şık metnin küçük bir ayrıntısını değiştirerek abartır; ‘cheaper’ geçen şık tersini söyler.

were given
drank
were
given
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘escaped’. İskelet: özne ‘Workers at a nearby brewery’ + ana fiil ‘escaped’ + nesne ‘the disease’. ‘were given’ ve ‘drank’ virgüller arasındaki ‘who’ yan cümlesinin fiilleridir; ‘were’ yalnızca o yan cümlenin yardımcı fiilidir; ‘given’ tek başına bir ortaçtır (past participle).

diagnosed
do not receive
have
been
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘do not receive’. İskelet: özne ‘many’ + ana fiil ‘do not receive’ + nesne ‘treatment’; ‘Among those…’ bir edat öbeğidir. ‘have been diagnosed’ ‘who’ yan cümlesinin fiilidir; ‘diagnosed’ bu fiilin ortacıdır; ‘have’ ve ‘been’ yalnızca yardımcı fiillerdir.

have

İskelet: özne ‘Several countries’ + ana fiil ‘have reduced’ + nesne ‘their death rates’. ‘have combined’ ‘which’ yan cümlesinin fiilidir; ‘combined’ bu fiilin ortacıdır; ‘have’ tek başına yardımcı fiildir; ‘to reduce’ cümlede geçmeyen bir mastardır.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
Few public health campaigns have been as successful as the long effort to reduce smoking, although the work is far from finished. According to the World Health Organization, about one in three adults worldwide used tobacco in 2000, whereas by 2022 the proportion had fallen to roughly one in five. Because the world's population grew during this period, the decline in the absolute number of users was much smaller, and it is estimated that about 1.2 billion people still use tobacco today.

The fall has been especially dramatic in some high-income countries. In the United Kingdom, for example, more than a quarter of adults smoked in the late 1990s, compared with about 12 per cent in 2023. Researchers commonly attribute this change to a combination of policies rather than to any single measure. Taxes are thought to be particularly effective: in high-income countries, a ten per cent rise in the price of cigarettes is associated with a fall in consumption of around four per cent, and young people, who usually have less money, appear to respond most strongly. Tobacco is estimated to kill more than eight million people each year, including over a million non-smokers who are harmed through exposure to other people's smoke. exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
Over the past three decades, one of the most remarkable improvements in global health has taken place, largely without attracting much public attention. According to estimates published by the United Nations, the number of children who died before their fifth birthday fell from about 12.8 million in 1990 to roughly 4.9 million in 2022. This decline occurred during a period in which the world's population grew substantially, which makes the achievement even more striking. In 1990, about 93 out of every 1,000 children died before the age of five; by 2022 the figure was close to 37.

This progress is generally attributed to a combination of relatively simple interventions. Oral rehydration salts, which are cheap and easy to use, have saved many children with diarrhoea. Bed nets treated with insecticide reduced deaths from malaria, while wider access to clean water, better nutrition, vitamin supplements and trained health workers also played a role. Maternal education is often mentioned as well, since educated mothers are more likely to seek treatment early.

Despite these gains, the statistics also reveal deep inequalities. More than half of all deaths among children under five now occur in sub-Saharan Africa, where the rate remains many times higher than in Europe. Moreover, a large proportion of the deaths that still occur are caused by conditions which can be prevented or treated, such as pneumonia and other respiratory infections, diarrhoea and complications around birth.

The United Nations has set a target of reducing the rate to 25 or fewer per 1,000 in every country by 2030. At the current pace, however, dozens of countries are expected to miss it, so it could be argued that the remaining gap should not be underestimated.
options: Why Child Mortality Has Risen Since 1990
Malaria: The Only Cause of Child Deaths
The Struggle Against Pneumonia in Europe
Population Growth Ends Global Poverty
Fewer Child Deaths, but an Unfinished Task
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Fewer Child Deaths, but an Unfinished Task’: ölümler büyük ölçüde azaldı ama eşitsizlikler sürüyor ve pek çok ülkenin hedefi kaçırması bekleniyor. ‘Risen’ geçen başlık tersini söyler; ‘Malaria’ geçen başlık birçok nedenden yalnızca birini yanlış biçimde tek neden yapar; ‘Pneumonia’ geçen başlık metinde olmayan bir konuyu işler; ‘Poverty’ geçen başlık metinde yoktur.

units.title: Tanım ve örnek
units.description: Bir kavramı tanımlayıp örnekleyen sosyal bilim metinlerini çöz
units.guide:
## Strateji

Eğitim, dil ve psikoloji metinlerinin çoğu aynı planı izler: önce bir **terim tanımlanır**, sonra **örneklerle** somutlaştırılır, en sonda kanıt ya da eleştiri gelir. Tanımı yakalarsan ana fikir, örnek ve çıkarım sorularının çoğu kendiliğinden çözülür; çünkü her örnek tanımın bir parçasını göstermek için oradadır.

## Nasıl uygulanır

1. Tanım kalıplarını bul: *X is…, X refers to…, the term X describes…, known as, called*.

2. Tanımı tek bir Türkçe cümleyle kenara yaz.

3. Örnek işaretlerini bul: *for example, for instance, such as, consider, imagine*. Her örneğin yanına tanımın hangi parçasını gösterdiğini not et.

4. Karşıt kavramları iki sütuna ayır: *fixed / growth, internal / external, intrinsic / extrinsic*.

5. “Yazar bu örneği neden veriyor?” sorusunda tanıma geri dön.

## Örnek

*A loanword is a word which is borrowed from one language and becomes part of another. Yoghurt and kiosk, for example, came into English from Turkish.* Tanım: başka dilden alınıp yerleşen kelime. Örnek, tanımın “başka dilden alınma” parçasını gösterir; metnin ana fikri yoğurt değil, ödünç kelimedir.

## Sınav ipucu

Başlık ve ana fikir sorusunda yalnızca bir örneği anlatan şıkkı eleme; doğru şık neredeyse her zaman tanımlanan kavramı içerir. Örnek sorusunda da “in order to show…” kalıbının devamı tanımın kendisidir.

nodes.title: Sosyal: zihniyet ve kontrol odağı
nodes.description: Metin 1: Gelişim zihniyeti: tanım, okul örnekleri ve karışık kanıtlar. Metin 2: Kontrol odağı (locus of control): içsel ve dışsal yönelim. ys7 kelimeleri: failure, gradual, online, psychologist, psychology, grade, intelligence, talent ve 11 kelime daha.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
In psychology, the term mindset refers to the beliefs which people hold about whether their basic abilities can change. The idea was popularised by the American psychologist Carol Dweck, who distinguished between two broad types. People with a fixed mindset tend to view intelligence and talent as qualities they are born with, while people with a growth mindset believe that these abilities can be developed through effort, good strategies and help from others.

The difference is most clearly seen in the way people respond to failure. Consider two students who both receive a low grade in a mathematics exam. The first concludes that she is simply not a maths person and gradually stops trying, since further effort seems pointless. The second treats the result as information, asks her teacher which topics she misunderstood and changes the way she studies. According to the theory, the second student is more likely to improve over time, because a difficult experience is interpreted as a stage of learning rather than as a final judgment.

These ideas have been widely adopted in schools, where teachers are often encouraged to praise effort and strategy instead of intelligence.
