exercises.question: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
The concept of locus of control was introduced by the American psychologist Julian Rotter in the 1950s and 1960s. The word locus simply means place, and the term describes where people believe the control over the events of their lives is located. Individuals with an internal locus of control tend to think that outcomes depend mainly on their own actions and decisions, whereas those with an external locus attribute them largely to luck, fate or powerful others.

A simple example illustrates the difference. Imagine that two employees are not promoted after a year of work. The first decides that she needs to improve certain skills and enrols in a course, because she believes that her own behaviour influences what happens to her. The second concludes that the manager is unfair and that nothing can be done, so he makes no changes at all. Similarly, a student who believes that exam results are determined by luck may see little point in revising.

Rotter developed a questionnaire in which respondents were asked to choose between pairs of statements, and versions of this scale have since been used in thousands of studies. In general, an internal orientation has been associated with higher academic achievement, healthier habits and better ways of coping with stress. However, the relationship is not entirely straightforward. In situations which really are beyond a person's control, a strongly internal view may lead to unnecessary self-blame.

It is also worth noting that locus of control is not regarded as a fixed trait. Experiences of success and failure can gradually shift it, and cultural background appears to influence how much control individuals expect to have over their own lives.
options: Luck and Fate in Ancient Philosophy
How Managers Decide Who Gets Promoted
Why an Internal Locus Is Always Better
The Life of Julian Rotter
Who Is in Charge? Understanding Locus of Control

exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
exercises.passage:
Confirmation bias is the tendency to search for, interpret and remember information in a way that supports what we already believe. Psychologists have catalogued dozens of cognitive biases, but this one is often considered among the most powerful, partly because it usually operates without our awareness. In other words, people are rarely conscious that they are ignoring evidence which contradicts their views.

A classic demonstration was devised by the British psychologist Peter Wason in 1960. Participants were told that the sequence 2, 4, 6 followed a certain rule, and they were asked to discover the rule by proposing new sequences of their own. Most of them assumed that the rule was 'numbers increasing by two' and tested only sequences such as 8, 10, 12, which fitted their plausible but narrow idea. In fact, the rule was simply any three increasing numbers, but few participants found it, since they hardly ever tried a sequence that could have proved them wrong.

Anecdotal examples from daily life are easy to find. A person who believes that a certain diet works will notice friends who lost weight and forget those who did not. In a similar way, readers often select news sources whose opinions match their own, so their existing beliefs are reinforced rather than challenged. Even professionals are affected: a doctor who forms an early diagnosis may pay less attention to symptoms that point in a different direction.

Completely eliminating this bias is probably impossible, but its influence can be reduced. Scientists, for example, are trained to design experiments which could disprove their hypotheses, and some decision-makers deliberately ask a colleague to present a counterargument to their preferred option before reaching a final conclusion.
options: the life and career of the psychologist Peter Wason
a mathematical rule for generating number sequences
a common tendency to favour information that supports existing beliefs, with examples
the reasons why doctors usually make accurate diagnoses
a method for removing all bias from scientific research

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
exercises.passage:
Psychologists commonly distinguish between two kinds of motivation. Intrinsic motivation refers to doing something because the activity itself is interesting or satisfying, as when a child reads a novel for pleasure. Extrinsic motivation, by contrast, describes behaviour that is driven by an external outcome, such as a grade, a payment or praise. Both types are part of everyday life, but research suggests that they interact in surprising ways.

In a well-known experiment published in 1973, Mark Lepper and his colleagues observed preschool children who enjoyed drawing. Some of the children were promised a certificate if they produced a drawing, while others received no reward or were given one unexpectedly. When the children were observed again a week or two later, those who had been promised a reward spent noticeably less time drawing of their own volition than the others. This effect, which is known as the overjustification effect, suggests that an expected reward can turn an enjoyable activity into a task that is performed only for the reward.

Such findings contributed to self-determination theory, which was developed by Edward Deci and Richard Ryan. The theory argues that people are more likely to remain motivated when three basic needs are satisfied: a sense of autonomy, a feeling of competence and good relationships with others. A teacher who offers students some choice about what to read, for instance, is supporting their autonomy.

It would be wrong to conclude that rewards are always harmful. For dull or routine tasks, extrinsic incentives can be effective, and unexpected praise for effort rarely reduces interest. The practical lesson is rather that rewards should be used carefully, especially for activities which people already enjoy.
options: prove that all rewards destroy children’s interest in learning
describe the history of preschool education
argue that teachers should never praise students
compare drawing with reading as hobbies
explain two types of motivation and how rewards can influence them

This effect, which is known as the overjustification effect, suggests that an expected reward can turn an enjoyable activity into a task that is performed only for the reward.

Such findings contributed to self-determination theory, which was developed by Edward Deci and Richard Ryan. The theory argues that people are more likely to remain motivated when three basic needs are satisfied: a sense of autonomy, a feeling of competence and good relationships with others. Such findings contributed to self-determination theory, which was developed by Edward Deci and Richard Ryan. The theory argues that people are more likely to remain motivated when three basic needs are satisfied: a sense of autonomy, a feeling of competence and good relationships with others. A teacher who offers students some choice about what to read, for instance, is supporting their autonomy.

It would be wrong to conclude that rewards are always harmful. For dull or routine tasks, extrinsic incentives can be effective, and unexpected praise for effort rarely reduces interest. The practical lesson is rather that rewards should be used carefully, especially for activities which people already enjoy.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
Code-switching is the practice of alternating between two or more languages, or varieties of a language, within a single conversation, and it is extremely common wherever bilingual communities exist. A Turkish-German teenager in Berlin, for example, might say a sentence that begins in German and ends in Turkish, or insert a Turkish word such as 'abla' into an otherwise German sentence because no German word expresses the same relationship.

For much of the twentieth century, code-switching was viewed negatively. Teachers and even some linguists assumed that speakers mixed languages because they did not know either of them properly. Research conducted since the 1970s, however, has largely rejected this interpretation. Studies of bilingual communities, such as Spanish-English speakers in New York, showed that switches are not random but follow grammatical patterns. Speakers rarely switch at points where the grammar of the two languages conflicts, which suggests that skilled code-switching actually requires a high degree of competence in both.

Speakers switch for a wide range of reasons. Sometimes a concept is more easily expressed in one language, while at other times the switch signals a change of topic or tone. A speaker may move into the language of home to show warmth or into a more formal language to sound authoritative. Code-switching can also play a role in expressing identity, since it marks the speaker as a member of a community that is shaped by two cultures.

Nevertheless, attitudes in many schools remain mixed: some educators still discourage it, whereas others now regard it as a resource which can be used to support learning. In some classrooms, students are encouraged to discuss a difficult text in their home language before writing about it in the language of instruction.
options: Code-switching happens only when speakers forget words in one language.
Most linguists still believe that mixing languages shows poor competence.
Turkish-German teenagers in Berlin speak only German at home.
Code-switching, once seen as a weakness, is now widely viewed as a skilled and meaningful practice.
Schools have completely banned code-switching in classrooms.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
A loanword is a word which is borrowed from one language and becomes part of the regular vocabulary of another. Borrowing usually occurs when speakers of different languages come into contact through trade, conquest, religion or technology, and when a new object or idea arrives together with its name. Once a loanword is accepted, it often undergoes adaptation to the sounds and spelling of the new language and is pronounced according to its rules, so that speakers may no longer recognise its foreign origin.

English is a striking example of a borrowing language. After the Norman conquest of 1066, thousands of French words entered the language, particularly in areas such as law, government and food. By some estimates, more than half of modern English vocabulary can be traced to French or Latin, although the most frequent everyday words, such as house, water and bread, remain largely Germanic. English has also taken words from Turkish: yoghurt and kiosk are commonly cited examples, and coffee probably reached English partly through Turkish as well.

Turkish, in turn, contains many loanwords from Arabic, Persian and French. Words such as kitap and kalem came from Arabic, while otobüs, kuaför and asansör were borrowed from French and adapted to Turkish spelling. Dictionaries catalogue the origin of each entry, and these records allow linguists to reconstruct the linguistic history of contact between peoples.

Not everyone welcomes this process. In several countries, official institutions have attempted to replace loanwords with native forms; the Turkish Language Association, which was established in 1932, created new terminology, much of which is now in everyday use. However, it is widely accepted that borrowing does not weaken a language but is a normal sign of its contact with the wider world.
options: Why English Has No Germanic Words
The Turkish Language Association and Its Founders
French Cooking and Its Vocabulary
How to Avoid Using Foreign Words
Borrowed Words: How Languages Take from Each Other
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Borrowed Words: How Languages Take from Each Other’: metin ödünç kelimeyi tanımlar ve İngilizce ile Türkçeden örnekler verir. ‘Germanic’ geçen başlık metinle çelişir; ‘Founders’ geçen başlık metinde olmayan bir konudur; ‘Cooking’ geçen başlık yalnızca bir alanı abartır; ‘Avoid’ geçen başlık dilbilimcilerin görüşüyle çelişir.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
exercises.passage:
The spacing effect is the finding that information is remembered better when study sessions are spread out over time than when they are concentrated in a single block. A student who reviews a list of words for ten minutes on three separate days will usually recall more of them a month later than one who studies the same list for thirty minutes in one evening, even though the total time is identical.

The effect was first described by the German psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus, whose experiments were published in 1885. Using himself as the only participant, he memorised long lists of meaningless syllables and measured how quickly he forgot them. His results produced what is now known as the forgetting curve: much of the new material was lost within the first day, after which forgetting slowed down. He also observed that repeated reviews, especially when they were separated by intervals, made the material considerably more durable.

Since then, the spacing effect has been confirmed in hundreds of studies with children, university students and older adults. It also holds for many types of material, from vocabulary to medical procedures. One explanation is that each review requires the learner to retrieve information which has partly faded, and this effortful recall appears to strengthen memory more than simple rereading does.

Despite this evidence, spacing is rarely used by students on their own initiative. Many prefer cramming, partly because intensive study the night before an exam produces a feeling of mastery that is convincing but short-lived. Flashcard applications, which schedule reviews at increasing intervals such as one, three and seven days, are one practical way of applying the principle without having to plan every session.
options: the life of Hermann Ebbinghaus and his travels
the dangers of using flashcard applications
the finding that spreading study over time improves memory, and why it is underused
why older adults cannot benefit from spaced study
a new theory that rejects the forgetting curve
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the finding that spreading study over time improves memory, and why it is underused’: metin aralıklı tekrar etkisini tanımlar, örnekler ve öğrencilerin neden kullanmadığını açıklar. ‘travels’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘dangers’ geçen şık tersini söyler, uygulamalar pratik bir yol olarak sunulur; ‘older’ geçen şık yaşlı yetişkinlerle yapılan çalışmalarla çelişir; ‘rejects’ geçen şık metinde yoktur.

exercises.question: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
When people who share no common language are brought into regular contact, they often develop a simplified means of communication which is known as a pidgin. A pidgin typically takes most of its vocabulary from one dominant language, while its grammar is greatly reduced: words may have a single fixed form, and tense is often expressed by separate words rather than by endings. It is worth noting that a pidgin has no native speakers, since it is learned by adults for limited purposes such as trade or work.

The situation changes when children grow up in a community where the pidgin is the main shared language. These children acquire it as their first language and, within a generation or two, expand it into a complete system with richer vocabulary and more complex grammar. The resulting language is called a creole. Many creoles emerged in the colonial period, particularly on plantations where enslaved people from different regions were forced to live and work together.

Two examples illustrate the process. Tok Pisin, which developed in the Pacific, began as a pidgin based largely on English vocabulary. It is now spoken by several million people in Papua New Guinea, where it is one of the official languages and is used in the media and in parliament. Haitian Creole, which draws much of its vocabulary from French, is the first language of nearly the entire population of Haiti, which is more than eleven million people.

For a long time, creoles were dismissed as broken versions of European languages. Today, however, linguists regard them as fully developed languages, and some researchers argue that their emergence provides valuable linguistic insight into how human beings construct grammar.
options: Why Creoles Are Broken Forms of European Languages
The Official Languages of the Pacific
Trade Routes of the Colonial Period
How Adults Learn French in Haiti
From Pidgin to Creole: How New Languages Are Born
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘From Pidgin to Creole: How New Languages Are Born’: metin pidgini tanımlar, kreole dönüşümünü anlatır ve örnek verir. ‘Broken’ geçen başlık eski ve reddedilmiş görüşü savunur; ‘Official’ geçen başlık bir ayrıntıyı ana konu yapar; ‘Routes’ geçen başlık metinde yoktur; ‘Adults’ geçen başlık metinle çelişir, Haiti Kreolü ana dildir.

units.title: Problem ve çözüm
units.description: Fen metinlerinde sorunu, nedenini ve önerilen çözümü bul
units.guide:
## Strateji

Fen metinlerinin çoğu bir **problem–çözüm** düzeniyle yazılır: önce bir sorun tanımlanır, sonra nedeni açıklanır, ardından bir ya da birkaç çözüm önerilir ve son paragrafta çoğu zaman çözümün sınırları tartışılır. Bu iskeleti tanırsan, soruyu okuduğunda cevabın metnin hangi bölümünde olduğunu tahmin edebilirsin.

## Nasıl uygulanır

1. İlk paragrafta sorunu bul ve tek cümleyle not et.

2. Nedeni gösteren sinyalleri işaretle: *because, the cause was, the underlying problem is*.

3. Çözümü gösteren sinyalleri işaretle: *one solution, another approach, was adopted, to tackle*.

4. Son paragrafta değerlendirmeye bak: *however, none of these, each of these faces barriers*. Yazarın tutumu genellikle buradadır.

## Örnek

*The Aral Sea shrank because its rivers were used for farming. A dam was built to save the northern part. However, the southern part continues to shrink.* Sorun: göl küçüldü; neden: nehirler tarlalara çevrildi; çözüm: baraj; sınır: güney kısım kurtarılamadı. Soru “yazar bu çözüm hakkında ne düşünüyor?” derse cevap “yararlı ama sınırlı” olur.

## Sınav ipucu

Başlık ve ana fikir sorularında hem sorunu hem çözümü içeren şıkkı ara; yalnızca sorunu ya da tek bir ayrıntıyı veren şık genellikle çeldiricidir. Metin *mitigate, reduce, slow* diyorsa *completely solved, remove every* gibi kesin ifadeler yanlıştır.

exercises.passage:
In 1935, about a hundred cane toads were brought to north-eastern Australia from Hawaii. They were released in sugar plantations, where farmers hoped they would eat the beetles which were damaging the crop. The animals largely ignored the beetles, but they proved remarkably good at survival, and their population is now estimated in the hundreds of millions. Their range has expanded thousands of kilometres towards the west, at times by up to fifty kilometres a year.

The underlying problem is that these invaders carry a highly toxic substance behind their heads. Native predators such as snakes, lizards and the quoll, a small meat-eating mammal, have no evolutionary experience of this toxin, so a single attack on a large toad is often enough to kill them. In some regions quoll numbers fell sharply within a few years of the invaders' arrival, with knock-on effects throughout the food chain.

Complete elimination of the species is no longer considered realistic, so researchers have concentrated on reducing the harm. One proposed solution exploits a simple form of learning. Young quolls are fed small pieces of toad meat that contain a chemical which makes them feel sick but does not kill them. In preliminary trials, animals that had eaten this bait were far less likely to attack the invaders afterwards, and researchers hope the habit may be passed on to their offspring. Another approach involves physical barriers around artificial water points in dry areas, since the invaders lose water rapidly and cannot survive long without it.

None of these measures will halt the invasion entirely. By combining them, however, conservation managers hope to mitigate its impact while native species gradually adapt.

exercises.passage:
About a quarter of the Netherlands lies below sea level, and more than half of the country would be exposed to flooding without protection. For centuries the standard response to this vulnerability was to build dykes higher and stronger. After a disastrous storm in 1953, in which more than 1,800 people died, the government launched the Delta Works, a system of dams and storm barriers that is still regarded as one of the greatest engineering projects of the twentieth century.

In the 1990s, however, two near-floods along the Rhine and the Meuse forced engineers to reconsider this approach. When rivers are confined between ever higher walls, water inevitably rises further during heavy rainfall, and the consequences of a single failure become more severe. Moreover, the land behind the dykes had gradually sunk, so the gap between river and fields kept widening.

The solution that was eventually adopted reversed the old logic. Under a programme known as Room for the River, which was largely completed in the 2010s at a cost of more than two billion euros, dykes were moved further inland, side channels were dug and some low farmland was turned into areas that could be flooded deliberately during periods of extreme flow. In the city of Nijmegen, for example, a second channel, which lowered the water level at peak times by about thirty-five centimetres, was created next to the river Waal.

The programme was not free of controversy. Some farmers and residents had to leave land their families had occupied for generations, and their participation was secured only after long negotiations. Nevertheless, the project is frequently cited as evidence that working with natural processes, rather than against them, can provide more durable protection.

nodes.description: Metin 1: Londra’da sallanan köprü ve sönümleyiciler. Metin 2: Uzay enkazı sorunu ve temizleme denemeleri. ys7 kelimeleri: calculation, feedback, reinforce, prompt, amplitude, modification, oscillation, motion ve 22 kelime daha.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: The Millennium Bridge was closed permanently because it was unsafe.
An unexpected swaying problem on a London bridge was solved without rebuilding it.
Engineers had predicted the swaying of the bridge before it opened.
Pedestrians caused the swaying by walking too quickly across the deck.
Modern footbridges always sway when large crowds cross them.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘An unexpected swaying problem on a London bridge was solved without rebuilding it’: sorun beklenmedikti ve sönümleyicilerle çözüldü. ‘permanently’ geçen şık yanlıştır, köprü 2002’de yeniden açıldı; ‘predicted’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, neden hesaplarda öngörülmemişti; ‘quickly’ geçen şık nedeni yanlış verir, sorun adımların harekete uymasıdır; ‘always’ geçen şık metindeki ‘On most bridges’ bilgisiyle çelişir.
exercises.passage:
When the Millennium Bridge, the first new river crossing in central London for over a century, was opened in June 2000, tens of thousands of people walked across it on the first day. Almost immediately, the deck began to sway from side to side, and many pedestrians had to hold the rails to keep their balance. Two days later the bridge was closed, and it remained closed for almost two years.

Engineers soon identified the cause, which had not been anticipated in the original calculations. When people walk, each step pushes the ground slightly sideways as well as downwards. On most bridges these lateral forces are random and cancel each other out. On this bridge, however, a small initial motion prompted walkers to adjust their steps to the movement in order to stay stable, and once many people did so at the same time, their combined steps reinforced the oscillation. The more the deck moved, the more people fell into step, a feedback loop that increased the amplitude of the swaying.

Rebuilding the structure would have been expensive, so a less drastic solution was chosen. Around ninety dampers, devices which absorb movement in much the same way that shock absorbers do in a car, were fitted beneath the deck. Before the bridge was reopened in 2002, the modification was tested with groups of up to two thousand volunteers, and no significant motion was observed.

The episode had consequences far beyond London. Engineering guidelines in several countries were revised to require designers to check how a footbridge would respond to crowds, and the effect of crowds on lateral stability became a recognised topic of research.

options: work in a similar way to shock absorbers in a car

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘work in a similar way to shock absorbers in a car’: 3. paragraf onları arabadaki amortisörlere benzetir. ‘removed’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘heavier’ geçen şık için bilgi yoktur, sönümleyiciler hareketi emer; ‘installed’ geçen şık yanlıştır, güvertenin altına takıldılar; ‘rebuilding’ geçen şık tersini söyler, yeniden yapım pahalı olacağı için bu çözüm seçildi.

options: describe the career of the scientist who named the Kessler syndrome

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘explain the problem of space debris and the ways it is being tackled’: metin sorunu, nedenini ve iki tür çözümü anlatır. ‘career’ geçen şık yalnızca bir ismi ayrıntı sayar; ‘launched’ geçen şık metinde savunulmaz; ‘compare’ geçen şık yanlıştır, iki ülke yalnızca 2009 çarpışmasında anılır; ‘land’ geçen şık metinde yoktur.
exercises.passage:
More than half a century of space activity has led to a steady accumulation of debris around Earth. Space agencies estimate that over thirty thousand objects larger than about ten centimetres are being tracked, while millions of smaller fragments, which are too small to be followed, also circle the planet. They include dead satellites, used rocket stages and pieces that were produced when objects collided or exploded.

Because these fragments travel at velocities of around seven kilometres per second, even a tiny flake of paint can damage the window of a spacecraft. The greatest concern, however, is a cumulative process known as the Kessler syndrome, after the scientist who described it in 1978. Each collision produces new fragments, which raise the probability of further collisions, so that certain orbits could ultimately become too crowded to use safely. A single collision in 2009, when an inactive Russian satellite hit an American communications satellite, created well over a thousand trackable pieces.

Two kinds of solution are being developed. The first is prevention: new satellites are increasingly required to leave their orbit within a fixed period after their mission ends, usually by using their remaining fuel to fall back and burn up in the atmosphere. The second is active removal. In 2018 and 2019, a small British-led demonstrator called RemoveDEBRIS successfully tested a net and a harpoon on targets that it had released itself, and later missions have been designed to approach and capture real objects.

Experts generally agree that removal alone cannot solve the problem, since it is slow and costly, and legal questions about who owns old objects may hinder it. Stricter rules, better tracking and international cooperation are therefore regarded as equally important for keeping near-Earth space usable.

options: destroyed the International Space Station

was the first test of the RemoveDEBRIS net
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘produced more than a thousand pieces that can be tracked’: ‘well over a thousand trackable pieces’. ‘Station’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘paint’ geçen şık ayrı bir örnektir; ‘inactive’ geçen şık yanlıştır, yalnızca Rus uydusu çalışmıyordu, diğeri Amerikan uydusuydu; ‘test’ geçen şık tarihle çelişir, deneme 2018’de yapıldı.

More than half a century of space activity has led to a steady accumulation of debris around Earth. Space agencies estimate that over thirty thousand objects larger than about ten centimetres are being tracked, while millions of smaller fragments, which are too small to be followed, also circle the planet. They include dead satellites, used rocket stages and pieces that were produced when objects collided or exploded.

Because these fragments travel at velocities of around seven kilometres per second, even a tiny flake of paint can damage the window of a spacecraft. The greatest concern, however, is a cumulative process known as the Kessler syndrome, after the scientist who described it in 1978. Each collision produces new fragments, which raise the probability of further collisions, so that certain orbits could ultimately become too crowded to use safely. A single collision in 2009, when an inactive Russian satellite hit an American communications satellite, created well over a thousand trackable pieces.

Two kinds of solution are being developed. The first is prevention: new satellites are increasingly required to leave their orbit within a fixed period after their mission ends, usually by using their remaining fuel to fall back and burn up in the atmosphere. The second is active removal. In 2018 and 2019, a small British-led demonstrator called RemoveDEBRIS successfully tested a net and a harpoon on targets that it had released itself, and later missions have been designed to approach and capture real objects.

Experts generally agree that removal alone cannot solve the problem, since it is slow and costly, and legal questions about who owns old objects may hinder it. Stricter rules, better tracking and international cooperation are therefore regarded as equally important for keeping near-Earth space usable.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
options: A Deadly Skin Disease of Frogs and How It Might Be Controlled
Why Frogs Need Warm Water to Survive

How Bacteria Cause Heart Disease in Humans
Five Hundred Species Saved by Captivity
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘A Deadly Skin Disease of Frogs and How It Might Be Controlled’: metin Bd mantarını (sorun) ve olası çözümleri anlatır. ‘warm’ geçen şık yalnızca bir çözüm ayrıntısıdır; ‘trade’ geçen şık yayılma nedenlerinden biridir; ‘humans’ geçen şık metinde yoktur, bakteriler kurbağayı korur; ‘saved’ geçen şık sayıyı çarpıtır, beş yüz tür kurtarılmadı, geriledi.
exercises.passage:
Since the 1980s, scientists have recorded alarming declines in frog populations around the world. Much of this loss has been attributed to a fungus known as Bd, which infects the skin of amphibians. Because frogs absorb water and essential minerals through their skin, the infection disturbs the balance of salts in the body, and in severe cases the heart eventually stops. A study published in 2019 estimated that the disease had contributed to the decline of at least five hundred species and to around ninety extinctions, although some researchers regard these figures as approximate.

Several features render the fungus difficult to control. It spreads through water, so it cannot easily be confined to one location, and some species carry it without becoming ill, acting as a reservoir that maintains the infection in an area. The global trade in live animals is also believed to have carried it between continents.

No single solution exists, but several strategies have shown promise. Some threatened species have been rescued by keeping groups in captivity, where they can be bred free of disease until conditions in the wild improve. Researchers have also found that certain bacteria which live naturally on frog skin produce substances that slow the growth of the fungus, and experimental treatments add these protective bacteria to animals before they are released. Since the fungus grows poorly in warm conditions, creating warmer, sunny places in ponds may also help some populations.

Prevention, however, remains the most cost-effective approach. Stricter rules on the movement of amphibians, together with careful cleaning of the equipment used by field workers, may stop the fungus from reaching the few regions that are still free of it.

exercises.question: According to the passage, Bd is difficult to control partly because ----.
options: it cannot survive in water
some species carry it without becoming sick and keep it present in an area
it only infects frogs kept in captivity
it grows best in very warm ponds
it is spread mainly by the clothes of field workers
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘some species carry it without becoming sick and keep it present in an area’: bu türler bir ‘reservoir’ gibi davranır. ‘survive’ geçen şık tersini söyler, mantar suyla yayılır; ‘captivity’ geçen şık yanlıştır, tutsaklık bir çözümdür; ‘warm’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, sıcakta zayıf büyür; ‘clothes’ geçen şık metinde yoktur, yalnızca ekipman temizliği anılır.

options: how the Aral Sea was damaged and how part of it has been restored

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘how the Aral Sea was damaged and how part of it has been restored’: metin sorunu, nedenini, sonuçlarını ve kuzeydeki çözümü anlatır. ‘cotton’ geçen şık yalnızca nedenin bir parçasıdır; ‘refused’ geçen şık tersini söyler, Dünya Bankası destek verdi; ‘farmland’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘always’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, göl su kaybettikçe tuzlandı.
exercises.passage:
In the 1960s, the Aral Sea, on the border between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, was the fourth-largest lake in the world. Over the following decades it lost roughly ninety per cent of its water, in what is often described as one of the worst environmental disasters of the twentieth century. The cause was not natural but the result of human intervention on a vast scale. To expand cotton production in the dry region, Soviet planners diverted the two rivers which fed the lake into a vast network of irrigation channels, many of which leaked badly.

The knock-on effects were severe. As the water retreated, the remaining lake became so salty that most native fish died, and a fishing industry which had once employed tens of thousands of people collapsed. Former harbours were left many kilometres from the shore. Winds picked up salt and dust from the exposed lake bed, which had been contaminated by agricultural chemicals, and carried them across nearby farmland and towns, where residents reported high rates of respiratory illness. In the aftermath, even the local climate changed, with hotter summers and colder winters.

Restoring the entire sea was regarded as unrealistic, so a more modest solution was adopted for the northern part, which lies in Kazakhstan. In 2005, with support from the World Bank, a dam about thirteen kilometres long was completed to separate the small North Aral Sea from the larger southern basin, and the channel of the Syr Darya river was improved. Within months the water level rose faster than expected, the salt content fell, and native fish species returned, allowing commercial fishing to revive.

The southern part, however, has continued to shrink, and much of it is now desert. The contrast between the two basins is frequently cited as evidence that targeted engineering can reverse some environmental damage, provided that sufficient water is available.

exercises.question: According to the passage, after the dam was completed in 2005, ----.
options: the southern basin began to fill with water again
the Syr Darya river stopped reaching the lake
the water level in the northern part rose more quickly than expected
most native fish disappeared from the northern part
the local climate immediately returned to normal
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘the water level in the northern part rose more quickly than expected’: ‘Within months the water level rose faster than expected’. ‘southern’ geçen şık son paragrafla çelişir, güney kısım küçülmeye devam ediyor; ‘stopped’ geçen şık tersini söyler, nehrin yatağı iyileştirildi; ‘disappeared’ geçen şık yanlıştır, yerli balıklar geri döndü; ‘climate’ geçen şık için bilgi yoktur.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Defeating a Deadly Fly with Its Own Males’: metin sorunu (yarada beslenen sinek) ve kısır erkek salma çözümünü anlatır. ‘chemicals’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, kimyasallar yayılmayı durduramadı; ‘Curaçao’ geçen şık yalnızca ilk denemenin yeridir; ‘attack’ geçen şık yanlıştır, sinek tüm sıcakkanlı hayvanlara yumurta bırakır; ‘forever’ geçen şık son paragrafla çelişir, vakalar yeniden görüldü.
exercises.passage:
For much of the twentieth century, livestock farmers in the southern United States faced a pest that could kill a cow within days. The New World screwworm is a fly whose females lay their eggs in open wounds on warm-blooded animals. When the eggs hatch, the young feed on living flesh and enlarge the wound, which in turn attracts more flies. Without treatment an infected animal frequently dies, and the losses to farmers were estimated in the hundreds of millions of dollars a year.

Chemical treatments could protect individual animals but could not halt the spread of the fly across a vast territory. A radically different solution was proposed by two American scientists, Edward Knipling and Raymond Bushland. Knipling had noticed that a female screwworm usually mates only once in her lifetime. If enormous numbers of males which had been made sterile by radiation were released, many females would mate with them and lay eggs that never hatched. Repeated over several generations, the releases would cause the population to collapse.

The idea was first tested in 1954 on Curaçao, a small Caribbean island, where the fly was eliminated within a few months. Encouraged by this result, the authorities built factories capable of producing tens of millions of sterile flies each week, which were dropped from aircraft over infected regions. By the late 1960s the pest had been largely eliminated from the United States, and the programme was gradually extended southwards through Mexico and Central America to Panama, where a permanent barrier of sterile flies is now maintained.

The technique, which leaves no chemical residue and affects only the target species, has since been used against fruit flies and other pests. However, it requires continuous investment, and the recent reappearance of screwworm cases in Central America has demonstrated how quickly progress can be reversed once the barrier weakens.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly about ----.
options: the construction of canals between the Great Lakes and the ocean

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘an invasive fish in the Great Lakes and the long effort to control it’: metin lamprey sorununu ve kontrol programını anlatır. ‘construction’ geçen şık yalnızca istilanın yolunu açıklar; ‘valuable’ geçen şık bir ayrıntıdır; ‘destroyed’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, TFM diğer balıkların çoğuna görece zararsızdır; ‘finally’ geçen şık son paragrafla çelişir, tamamen yok etmek mümkün değil.
exercises.passage:
The Great Lakes of North America hold about a fifth of the world's surface fresh water, and in the first half of the twentieth century they supported a large commercial fishery. That industry was almost destroyed by an invader which had arrived through canals built to connect the lakes with the Atlantic Ocean. The sea lamprey, a long fish that attaches itself to other fish with a round mouth full of teeth and feeds on their blood and bodily fluids, had previously been blocked by Niagara Falls. Once the canals were improved, it spread through all the upper lakes within a few decades.

The ecological consequences were severe. A single lamprey can kill up to about eighteen kilograms of fish during its adult life, and catches of lake trout, the most valuable species, plummeted. In Lake Huron and Lake Michigan, the trout fishery had virtually collapsed by the 1950s.

Finding a solution required a long search. In the 1950s, researchers tested thousands of chemical compounds before identifying one, known as TFM, which is toxic to young lampreys in the streams where they develop but relatively harmless to most other fish at the doses used. Since then, rivers have been treated regularly, and barriers and traps have been installed to block adults from reaching the streams where they breed, thereby limiting reproduction. These cumulative measures have reduced lamprey numbers by about ninety per cent in most parts of the lakes.

The programme is often described as one of the most successful efforts of its kind, yet it cannot simply be stopped. Because complete elimination is not possible, treatment must continue indefinitely, and scientists are now investigating natural chemical signals that might attract lampreys into traps more efficiently.

units.title: Neden–sonuç zinciri
units.description: Sağlık metinlerinde zincirin halkalarını sırayla izle
units.guide:
## Strateji

Sağlık metinleri çoğu zaman bir **neden–sonuç zinciri** anlatır: A, B’ye yol açar; B, C’yi tetikler; C de sonunda bir hastalığa dönüşür. Sorular ya zincirin bir halkasını sorar ya da halkaların sırasını ve yönünü karıştıran çeldiriciler kurar. Zinciri kâğıda dökersen bu tuzakları hemen görürsün.

## Nasıl uygulanır

1. Okurken zinciri oklarla not et: *sigara → hava yollarında iltihap → hava keseciklerinin yıkımı → nefes darlığı → hareketsizlik*.

2. Bağlantı ifadelerini işaretle: *lead to, cause, trigger, contribute to, result in, in turn, as a result*. *which* ile başlayan yan cümleler de çoğu zaman bir sonraki halkayı verir.

3. Yönü kontrol et: “A causes B” ile “B is caused by A” aynıdır, ama “B causes A” ters zincirdir.

4. Kesinlik derecesine bak: *may, appears to, is associated with* kesin bir neden değil, olasılık bildirir.

## Örnek

*Childhood adversity keeps the stress response switched on, which in turn raises inflammation.* Zincir: zor çocukluk → sürekli stres tepkisi → iltihap. “Inflammation causes childhood adversity” diyen şık yönü ters çevirdiği için yanlıştır.

## Sınav ipucu

Metin yalnızca bir ilişkiden söz ediyorsa (*association is not proof of causation*), kesin neden bildiren şıklar (*proves, always causes*) çoğunlukla yanlıştır. Çıkarım sorusunda zincirin bir sonraki halkasını düşün.

options: Childhood adversity always leads to serious illness in adult life.
Difficult childhood experiences may affect adult health through a chain of biological and behavioural effects.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Difficult childhood experiences may affect adult health through a chain of biological and behavioural effects’: metin toksik stres ve davranışlar üzerinden iki halkalı bir zincir anlatır. ‘always’ geçen şık son paragrafla çelişir, zincir kaçınılmaz değildir; ‘nurses’ geçen şık bir önlemi tek neden sayar; ‘happy’ geçen şık tersini söyler; ‘link’ geçen şık çalışmanın bulgusuyla çelişir.
exercises.passage:
In the late 1990s, a large study carried out by an American health insurer and public health researchers asked more than seventeen thousand adults about difficult experiences in their childhood, such as abuse, neglect or growing up with a parent who had a serious drinking problem. The researchers then compared these answers with the participants' current health. The results were striking: the more types of adversity a person had experienced, the higher their risk of heart disease, lung disease, depression and early death decades later.

Researchers have since proposed a chain that might link these early events to adult illness. When a child faces constant threat without the protection of a caring adult, the stress response may be activated so frequently that it becomes, in effect, permanently switched on. This so-called toxic stress is thought to affect the development of brain regions involved in memory, emotion and self-control, and to raise levels of inflammation throughout the body.

A second link is behavioural. Adults who suffered adversity in childhood are more likely to smoke, drink heavily or overeat, which some psychologists interpret as attempts to cope with painful emotions. These habits, in turn, contribute to chronic disease, so that the original harm is reinforced over a lifetime.

It should be noted that the chain is not inevitable. Many people who experienced severe adversity remain healthy, and the presence of at least one stable, supportive relationship appears to protect children from the worst effects. For this reason, programmes which support parents, such as regular home visits by nurses during a child's first years, are increasingly regarded as a long-term investment in health rather than simply a social service.

options: explain how untreated hearing loss might lead to dementia and what this means for health care

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘explain how untreated hearing loss might lead to dementia and what this means for health care’: metin olası zinciri anlatır ve işitme testleri önerir. ‘prove’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, ilişki neden olmanın kanıtı değildir; ‘structure’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘criticise’ geçen şıkta yazarın böyle bir tutumu yoktur; ‘compare’ geçen şık için bilgi yoktur.
exercises.passage:
Hearing loss is so common in later life that many people regard it as an unavoidable inconvenience rather than a medical problem. Roughly one in three people between the ages of sixty-five and seventy-five is thought to have some degree of hearing loss, yet only a minority of those who could benefit from a hearing aid actually use one. In recent years, however, researchers have paid increasing attention to a possible link between untreated hearing loss and dementia.

In 2020, an international commission which reviewed the evidence on dementia prevention identified hearing loss in middle age as the largest single risk factor that could be changed, estimating that it might be responsible for around eight per cent of cases worldwide. Several explanations for this association have been suggested, and together they form a plausible chain. When the ears transmit weaker signals, the brain must devote more effort to understanding speech, which may leave fewer resources for memory and thinking. Over time, reduced input may also contribute to structural changes in the parts of the cortex that process sound.

The social consequences may be equally important. Conversations become tiring and embarrassing, particularly in noisy restaurants or at family gatherings, so people with poor hearing frequently withdraw from them. This withdrawal leads to isolation, which is itself associated with depression and with faster cognitive decline, so the effects of the original impairment become cumulative.

It must be stressed that association is not proof of causation. People who already have early brain changes might simply find it harder to process sound. Nevertheless, a large trial published in 2023 found that, among older adults at higher risk, help with hearing slowed the decline in thinking skills over three years. Such results suggest that hearing tests, which are cheap and quick, should be offered routinely in middle and later life.

options: slowed the decline in thinking skills among older adults at higher risk

caused structural changes in the cortex
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘slowed the decline in thinking skills among older adults at higher risk’: son paragraf bunu açıkça söyler. ‘effect’ geçen şık metinle çelişir; ‘cured’ geçen şık abartılıdır, yalnızca düşüş yavaşladı; ‘expensive’ geçen şık tersini söyler, testler ucuz ve hızlıdır; ‘cortex’ geçen şık 2. paragraftaki olası bir mekanizmayı deneyin sonucu gibi sunar.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
options: Why Young People Fall More Often Than the Elderly
A New Medicine That Cures Osteoporosis
The Dangers of Exercise After Seventy
One Fall, Many Causes: The Chain Behind Injuries in Old Age
How Hip Surgery Became Completely Safe
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘One Fall, Many Causes: The Chain Behind Injuries in Old Age’: metin düşmeyi uzun bir zincirin son halkası olarak anlatır. ‘young’ geçen şık metinle çelişir; ‘medicine’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘dangers’ geçen şık tersini söyler, egzersiz düşmeleri azaltır; ‘surgery’ geçen şık yanlıştır, kalça kırığından sonra birçok hasta bağımsızlığını yitirir.
exercises.passage:
Among older adults, a fall is rarely an isolated accident. More often it is the final link in a chain of changes that develop slowly over many years. From around the age of forty, people gradually lose muscle mass, a process known as sarcopenia, and the loss tends to accelerate after the age of seventy, particularly in people who are physically inactive.

Weaker leg muscles make it harder to recover balance after a trip, and this vulnerability is often aggravated by other factors which accumulate with age, such as poorer eyesight, slower reactions and medicines that cause dizziness. At the same time, bones lose minerals and become more fragile, a condition called osteoporosis that is especially common in women after middle age. As a result, a fall that would merely bruise a younger person may cause a fracture, most seriously of the hip.

The aftermath of a hip fracture illustrates how one event can trigger many others. Surgery is usually required, followed by weeks of reduced mobility, during which further muscle is lost. Many patients never regain their previous level of independence, and a substantial proportion die within a year. Even people who are not injured may develop a fear of falling, which leads them to move less, which in turn weakens their muscles further and makes another fall more likely.

Fortunately, this chain can be broken at several points. Exercise programmes that combine strength and balance training have been shown to reduce the rate of falls by around a quarter. Reviewing medication, treating osteoporosis and removing hazards at home, such as loose carpets and poor lighting, also help. Because the process is cumulative, experts emphasise that prevention should begin well before old age.

exercises.question: According to the passage, the fear of falling ----.
options: only affects people who have broken a hip
makes people exercise more carefully and safely
is the first stage of sarcopenia
disappears after successful surgery
can make another fall more likely by reducing movement
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘can make another fall more likely by reducing movement’: korku daha az hareket, daha zayıf kaslar ve yeni bir düşme demektir. ‘broken’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, yaralanmayanlarda da görülür; ‘carefully’ geçen şık tersini söyler; ‘first’ geçen şık sıralamayı bozar, kas kaybı zincirin başındadır; ‘disappears’ geçen şık için bilgi yoktur.

exercises.passage:
Among older adults, a fall is rarely an isolated accident. More often it is the final link in a chain of changes that develop slowly over many years. From around the age of forty, people gradually lose muscle mass, a process known as sarcopenia, and the loss tends to accelerate after the age of seventy, particularly in people who are physically inactive.

Weaker leg muscles make it harder to recover balance after a trip, and this vulnerability is often aggravated by other factors which accumulate with age, such as poorer eyesight, slower reactions and medicines that cause dizziness. At the same time, bones lose minerals and become more fragile, a condition called osteoporosis that is especially common in women after middle age. As a result, a fall that would merely bruise a younger person may cause a fracture, most seriously of the hip.

The aftermath of a hip fracture illustrates how one event can trigger many others. Surgery is usually required, followed by weeks of reduced mobility, during which further muscle is lost. Many patients never regain their previous level of independence, and a substantial proportion die within a year. Even people who are not injured may develop a fear of falling, which leads them to move less, which in turn weakens their muscles further and makes another fall more likely.

Fortunately, this chain can be broken at several points. Exercise programmes that combine strength and balance training have been shown to reduce the rate of falls by around a quarter. Reviewing medication, treating osteoporosis and removing hazards at home, such as loose carpets and poor lighting, also help. Because the process is cumulative, experts emphasise that prevention should begin well before old age.

exercises.passage:
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, a lung condition usually shortened to COPD, is one of the leading causes of death worldwide, yet many people have never heard of it. In richer countries most cases are attributable to long-term smoking, while in poorer regions smoke from cooking fires burned inside homes, where there is little fresh air, is also a dominant cause.

The disease develops through a chain of damage. Cigarette smoke damages the tubes that carry air into the lungs, which respond by producing more liquid and becoming swollen and red. Over the years, this inflammation narrows the smallest tubes and gradually destroys the walls of the tiny air bags where oxygen passes into the blood. Because these structures cannot be rebuilt, the lungs lose their elasticity, air becomes trapped inside them, and the surface available for exchanging gases shrinks. The result is breathlessness, which at first appears only during exercise but eventually occurs even at rest.

Breathlessness then sets off a second, self-reinforcing cycle, which is often more disabling than the original damage. People who find it hard to breathe naturally avoid physical activity, so their muscles weaken and become less efficient at using oxygen. Weaker muscles make every task more tiring, which leads to even less activity. Many patients become isolated at home, and anxiety and depression are common. Sudden worsening of symptoms, often provoked by chest infections, may require hospital treatment and can accelerate the decline, sometimes with lasting repercussions.

Although the damage cannot be reversed, the chain can be slowed at several points. Stopping smoking is the single most effective step at any stage, and it reduces the rate at which lung function is lost. Vaccination against the flu helps to prevent infections, and supervised exercise programmes, known as lung rehabilitation, have been shown to improve breathlessness and quality of life, even though they do not repair the lungs themselves.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Type 2 diabetes results from a gradual chain of changes that can be interrupted if acted on early’. ‘genetic’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, asıl nedenler yağ ve hareketsizliktir; ‘large’ geçen şık yanlıştır, hem büyük hem küçük damarlar zarar görür; ‘injection’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘symptoms’ geçen şık tersini söyler, hastalık yıllarca sessiz kalabilir.
exercises.passage:
Type 2 diabetes develops through a chain of events that can remain silent for years. It usually begins with insulin resistance, a state in which the cells of the muscles, liver and fat tissue respond poorly to insulin, the hormone that allows sugar to enter cells from the blood. Excess body fat, especially fat stored around the internal organs, and a sedentary lifestyle are the dominant causes, although genetic factors also predispose some people to the condition.

At first, the body compensates by producing more insulin, so blood sugar remains roughly normal. This compensation, however, cannot continue forever. Gradually the cells that produce insulin become exhausted, their output declines, and blood sugar begins to rise. By the time the disease is diagnosed, a considerable proportion of these cells may already have been lost.

The damage caused by high blood sugar is cumulative. Excess sugar harms the lining of blood vessels, both large and small. Damage to the tiny vessels of the eye can lead to blindness, while damage to those of the kidneys may eventually require a transplant. Nerves in the feet are also affected, so minor wounds go unnoticed and become infected, which in severe cases leads to the loss of a limb. Damage to large vessels, meanwhile, roughly doubles the risk of heart attack and stroke.

The encouraging aspect of this chain is that it can be interrupted early, before the damage becomes irreversible. Intensive changes in diet and activity appear to be particularly effective. In a well-known American trial, people with raised blood sugar who were helped to lose about seven per cent of their body weight and to exercise regularly reduced their risk of developing diabetes by more than half. More recently, studies in the United Kingdom have shown that substantial weight loss can return blood sugar to normal levels in many people who have had the disease for only a few years.

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘When One Medicine Leads to Another: The Risks of Polypharmacy’: metin çoklu ilaç kullanımının yarattığı zinciri anlatır. ‘never’ geçen şık abartılıdır, yazar yalnızca gereksiz ilaçların bırakılmasını önerir; ‘stronger’ geçen şık tersini söyler; ‘swollen’ geçen şık bir örneği yanlış aktarır; ‘history’ geçen şık metinde yoktur.
exercises.passage:
Older adults often live with several long-term conditions at once, such as high blood pressure, diabetes and painful joints, and each condition is usually treated with its own medicine. As a result, many people over the age of seventy take five or more different drugs every day, a situation which doctors call polypharmacy. Each prescription may be reasonable on its own, but the combination can set off a chain of unintended effects.

The first link is biological. As people age, the liver and kidneys gradually become less efficient at removing drugs from the body, so a dose that was safe at fifty may accumulate to toxic levels at eighty, particularly in people with reduced kidney function. Some drugs also interact with one another, strengthening or weakening each other's effects in ways that are difficult to predict.

The second link is what researchers describe as a prescribing cascade. A side-effect of one medicine is mistaken for a new illness, and a second drug is prescribed to treat it. For example, certain drugs for blood pressure can cause swelling of the ankles, which may then be treated with another medicine that increases the need to pass water, leading in turn to night-time trips to the toilet, poor sleep and a higher risk of falls. Each step appears logical to the doctor involved, yet the cumulative burden grows, particularly when patients are seen by several specialists who do not communicate with one another.

To break this chain, health services in several countries now encourage regular medication reviews, in which a doctor or pharmacist examines every drug a patient takes and asks whether it is still needed. Studies suggest that the elimination of unnecessary medicines can often be achieved safely, although it requires careful monitoring and the agreement of the patient.

options: the history of the World Health Organization

exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘how chronic work stress develops into burnout and how it can best be addressed’: metin zinciri adım adım anlatır ve son paragrafta çözümleri değerlendirir. ‘history’ geçen şık yalnızca bir tarih bilgisini abartır; ‘drugs’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘doctors’ geçen şık bir örneği ana fikir sayar; ‘longer’ geçen şık tersini söyler, uzun çalışma tükenmeyi derinleştirir.
exercises.passage:
Burnout was first described in the 1970s among staff in helping professions, and in 2019 the World Health Organization included it in its classification of diseases as an occupational phenomenon rather than a medical condition. It is defined as the result of chronic workplace stress that has not been successfully managed, and it is characterised by persistent exhaustion, a growing mental distance from one's job and reduced professional effectiveness.

The chain usually starts with a persistent imbalance between demands and resources. Heavy workloads, unclear expectations and a lack of control over one's tasks keep the body's stress response active for long periods. Initially, employees may attempt to cope by working longer hours, which often means sacrificing sleep, exercise and time with family, the very activities that would normally help them recover. Exhaustion therefore deepens, and concentration and memory begin to suffer.

As performance declines, many workers react by withdrawing emotionally. Doctors and nurses who experience burnout, for example, may begin to treat patients in a more distant manner, a change which has been linked in several studies to more medical errors and lower patient satisfaction. These errors in turn increase stress, so the cycle reinforces itself. For organisations, the knock-on effects include higher absence, more resignations and rising recruitment costs.

Because the roots of burnout lie largely in working conditions, experts argue that solutions focusing only on the individual, such as relaxation courses, are insufficient on their own. Reviews of the evidence suggest that the most effective interventions combine individual support with changes to the organisation of work, such as more reasonable schedules, clearer roles and greater involvement of staff in the decisions that affect them.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
options: Why the Liver Cannot Repair Itself
Fatty Foods and Heart Disease
A Cure for Cirrhosis Has Been Found
How Hepatitis Is Spread
A Silent Chain: How Heavy Drinking Damages the Liver
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘A Silent Chain: How Heavy Drinking Damages the Liver’: metin belirti vermeden ilerleyen zararı aşama aşama anlatır. ‘repair’ geçen şık ilk cümleyle çelişir; ‘foods’ geçen şık metinde yoktur, yağlanma alkolden kaynaklanır; ‘cure’ geçen şık yanlıştır, bırakmak yalnızca ilerlemeyi yavaşlatır; ‘spread’ geçen şık metinde yoktur.
exercises.passage:
The liver is remarkably tolerant of damage: it can rebuild itself after injury and continue to work even when a large part of it is damaged. This capability, however, means that liver disease often produces no symptoms until a late stage, and alcohol-related liver disease is a clear example of how a slow chain of damage can remain hidden for decades.

The first stage is the accumulation of fat. When the liver breaks down alcohol, it produces toxic substances and changes the way fat is processed, so fat builds up within the liver cells. This condition, known as fatty liver, develops in most people who drink heavily and is usually reversible if drinking stops for a few weeks. If heavy drinking continues, however, the toxic by-products provoke inflammation, which damages and kills cells.

Each time damaged tissue is repaired, some of it is replaced by scar tissue, which cannot perform the normal functions of the liver. Over many years this tough, damaged tissue can spread through the organ until its structure is permanently altered, a condition called cirrhosis. A liver in this state can no longer remove toxic substances effectively, and the blocked flow of blood through it raises the pressure in nearby veins, which may burst and bleed. Cirrhosis also substantially raises the risk of liver cancer.

Not every heavy drinker develops cirrhosis; genetic factors, obesity and viral hepatitis are all influential, and they may interact with one another. Nevertheless, the risk rises with the amount and duration of drinking. Because early stages produce few symptoms, doctors increasingly recommend blood tests and scans for heavy drinkers, and they stress that stopping drinking, even after cirrhosis has developed, can slow its progression and improve survival.

units.title: Zamanlı okuma: 12 dakika
units.description: Metin başına 12 dakikada oku ve çöz: tarih, arkeoloji ve kültürel değişim
units.guide:
## Strateji

Gerçek YDS’de okuma parçaları 250–320 kelimelik akademik metinlerdir. Metin başına **12 dakika** ayırırsan dört soruyu acele etmeden çözer, kalan süreyi zor sorulara saklarsın. Sabit bir zaman planı, uzun bir tarih metninde tarihler ve isimler arasında kaybolmanı önler.

## Nasıl uygulanır

1. **1 dk:** soru köklerini oku; çıkarım (*inferred*) ve tutum/amaç (*attitude, purpose*) sorularını işaretle.

2. **5 dk:** metni bir kez, geri dönmeden oku; her paragrafın yanına iki kelimelik not yaz: "keşif", "eski görüş", "itiraz", "yeni kanıt".

3. **5 dk:** soruları çöz; ayrıntı sorusunda notundan doğru paragrafa git, çıkarım sorusunda metnin söylemediğini ya da fazla kesin söyleyen şıkkı ele.

4. **1 dk:** emin olmadığın soruyu işaretle ve geç.

Bu ünitede her metni kronometreyle oku; ilk derste 15, testte 12 dakikanın altını hedefle.

## Örnek

*For several decades, the dominant answer was a story of ecological self-destruction. More recently, this narrative has been challenged.* Notun: "eski görüş → itiraz". Soru yazarın amacını sorarsa cevabı bu geçişte ararsın; metnin başını yeniden okumazsın.

## Sınav ipucu

Tarih metinlerinde yıl ve isim çoktur; hepsini aklında tutmaya çalışma. Soru bir tarihi sorarsa yalnızca o satırı tara. 12 dakika dolunca son soruda en olası şıkkı işaretle ve sonraki metne geç.

exercises.question: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
About 9,000 years ago, several thousand people lived together on the Konya plain in central Anatolia, in a settlement which is now known as Çatalhöyük. It is regarded as one of the earliest large farming communities in the world, and its remains have been studied by archaeologists since the 1960s, when the site was first excavated by the British researcher James Mellaart. Since 2012 it has been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The most striking aspect of Çatalhöyük is its architecture. The houses were built of mud brick and were packed so closely together that there were apparently no streets at all. Instead, people moved across the flat roofs and entered their homes through an opening in the roof, using a wooden ladder. Inside, the walls were often covered with paintings of animals and hunting scenes, and the dead were buried beneath the floors, which suggests that the house was a place of ritual as well as a home.

Perhaps the most debated question concerns equality. In many later civilisations, the existence of an elite is evident from palaces, temples and rich graves, yet no such buildings have been found here. The houses are broadly similar in size, and studies of skeletons indicate that men and women ate similar food and did comparable work. For this reason, some researchers have concluded that the community was organised without a ruling class, although others argue that the evidence is too partial to justify such a generalisation.

What remains clear is that Çatalhöyük offers a rare view of the transformation from hunting to farming, a process which laid the foundation of all later urban life.
options: How the British Discovered Anatolia
Wall Paintings as the First Written Records
Why Mud Brick Replaced Stone in Ancient Cities
The Palaces and Temples of Early Kings
Çatalhöyük: An Early Farming Town and Its Open Questions

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
exercises.passage:
In 1906, archaeologists working near the village of Boğazköy in central Anatolia began to uncover thousands of clay tablets covered in cuneiform, a writing system which had been invented in Mesopotamia. The site turned out to be Hattusa, the capital of the Hittites, a people who dominated much of Anatolia in the second millennium BC. Altogether, around 30,000 tablets and fragments have been recovered there, and they comprise one of the richest archives of the ancient world.

At first, however, the texts could not be read. Although the signs themselves were familiar to scholars, the language behind them remained a mystery until 1915, when the Czech scholar Bedřich Hrozný argued that Hittite was related to languages such as Greek and Latin. His proposition was initially met with scepticism, but it was soon accepted by other experts, and Hittite is now regarded as the oldest recorded language of the Indo-European family.

The content of the archive is remarkably diverse. It includes laws, prayers, descriptions of religious festivals, medical instructions and letters which were exchanged between kings. The best-known document is a peace treaty that was concluded around 1259 BC between the Hittite king Hattusili III and the Egyptian pharaoh Ramesses II after decades of conflict over Syria. A copy of this treaty, which is kept in the Istanbul Archaeology Museums, is often described as one of the earliest surviving peace agreements, and a large replica is displayed at the United Nations in New York.

In recognition of their importance, the Boğazköy tablets were added to the UNESCO Memory of the World Register in 2001. For historians, they provide a rare portrayal of how an ancient state saw itself and its neighbours.
options: describe the discovery, reading and value of the Hattusa tablets
explain how cuneiform writing was invented in Mesopotamia
compare the Hittite and Egyptian armies in battle
argue that Hittite is older than Greek and Latin
criticise UNESCO for ignoring the Boğazköy archive
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘describe the discovery, reading and value of the Hattusa tablets’: metin tabletlerin bulunuşunu, dilin çözülmesini, içeriğini ve önemini sırayla anlatır. ‘invented’ geçen şık yalnızca bir yan bilgiye dayanır; ‘armies’ geçen şık metinde yoktur, yalnızca bir barış antlaşması geçer; ‘argue’ geçen şık metnin amacı değildir; ‘criticise’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, UNESCO tabletleri listesine almıştır.

nodes.title: Sosyal: kahvehane ve patates
nodes.description: Metin 1: Osmanlı kahvehanesi. Metin 2: Patatesin Avrupa’yı değiştirmesi. ys7 kelimeleri: symbol, influential, background, gradual, revive, authority, establishment, merchant ve 24 kelime daha.

exercises.question: Which of the following would be the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
Coffee is so closely associated with Turkish culture today that it is easy to forget it was once a controversial novelty. The drink is thought to have reached Istanbul from Yemen in the middle of the sixteenth century, and according to Ottoman historians, the first coffeehouse in the city was opened around 1554 by two merchants from Damascus and Aleppo. Within a few decades, hundreds of similar establishments had appeared across the capital.

What made the coffeehouse influential was not simply the drink but the new kind of social space which it created. Unlike the mosque or the home, it was a place where men from different backgrounds could meet, play games, listen to storytellers and exchange news. Poets read their work there, and the meddah, a performer who told tales and imitated voices, became a familiar part of the entertainment. In this manner, the coffeehouse gradually became a centre of public opinion.

Precisely for this reason, it was viewed with suspicion by the authorities. Religious scholars debated whether coffee should be permitted, while officials feared that political criticism was being spread in these crowded rooms. In the 1630s, Sultan Murad IV ordered the coffeehouses of Istanbul to be closed, and those who ignored the prohibition could face severe punishment. Nevertheless, such restrictions proved impossible to enforce for long, and the institution soon revived.

The Ottoman model was later imitated in Europe, where coffeehouses opened in Venice, London and Vienna during the seventeenth century and played a similar role in the circulation of news and ideas. In 2013, Turkish coffee culture and tradition was added to the UNESCO list of intangible cultural heritage, which shows how a once suspicious habit became a symbol of hospitality.
options: How Coffee Reached Yemen
Why Murad IV Preferred Tea to Coffee
The Storytellers of Venice and Vienna
Coffee as a Medicine in the Sixteenth Century
The Ottoman Coffeehouse: From Suspicious Novelty to Cultural Symbol
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The Ottoman Coffeehouse: From Suspicious Novelty to Cultural Symbol’: metin kahvehanenin şüpheyle karşılanan bir yenilikten kültürel bir simgeye dönüşmesini anlatır. ‘Reached’ geçen başlık yönü ters kurar, kahve Yemen’den gelmiştir; ‘Preferred’ geçen başlık metinde olmayan bir bilgi verir; ‘Storytellers’ geçen başlık meddahı yanlış şehirlere taşır; ‘Medicine’ geçen başlık metinde yoktur.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
Few foods have had as great an impact on world history as the potato. The plant was first grown in the Andes mountains of South America several thousand years ago, and by the time Spanish explorers arrived in the sixteenth century, hundreds of varieties were being cultivated by indigenous farmers. The Spanish brought the crop back to Europe in the second half of that century, but for a long time it was regarded with suspicion.

Many Europeans initially used the potato as animal food or grew it only as a curiosity in gardens. Some believed that it caused disease, partly because it belongs to the same plant family as several toxic species. Its acceptance was largely the result of deliberate promotion by rulers and scientists. In the eighteenth century, Frederick the Great of Prussia, who saw it as a cheap source of food, encouraged peasants to plant it, while in France the pharmacist Antoine-Augustin Parmentier organised public demonstrations of its value.

Once it was adopted, the potato transformed European agriculture. It produces far more calories per field than wheat, it grows in poor soil and cold climates, and it is rich in vitamin C. A widely cited study by the economists Nathan Nunn and Nancy Qian estimated that the potato may account for about a quarter of the growth in population in the Old World between 1700 and 1900.

However, dependence on a single crop also created vulnerability. When a disease destroyed potato harvests in Ireland in the 1840s, about a million people died and roughly another million left the country, a disaster whose consequences shaped Irish society for generations. The history of the potato therefore illustrates both the benefits and the risks of agricultural transformation.
options: After early distrust, the potato changed European farming and population, but relying on it also carried risks.
The potato failed in Europe because people never trusted it.
Frederick the Great was the first person to grow potatoes outside South America.
Potatoes contain more vitamins than any other food.
The Irish disaster of the 1840s was caused by poor government rather than by crop disease.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘After early distrust, the potato changed European farming and population, but relying on it also carried risks.’: metin şüpheyi, dönüşümü ve tek ürüne bağımlılığın riskini anlatır. ‘never’ geçen şık metinle çelişir; ‘Frederick’ geçen şık metinde olmayan bir ‘ilk’ iddiası kurar; ‘vitamins’ geçen şık abartılı bir genellemedir; ‘government’ geçen şık metinde yoktur, felaketi bir hastalık başlatmıştır.

exercises.question: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
exercises.passage:
When Mount Vesuvius erupted in AD 79, it buried not only Pompeii but also the nearby town of Herculaneum, where a wealthy villa contained a library of papyrus scrolls. The villa was rediscovered in the 1750s, and workers recovered hundreds of scrolls which had been turned to carbon by the intense heat, so that they looked like pieces of burnt wood. It is often described as the only library from classical antiquity that has survived largely intact.

For more than two centuries, scholars struggled to read them. Early attempts to unroll the scrolls by hand often caused them to break into fragments, and many texts were destroyed in the process. Those that could be opened mainly contained works by Philodemus, a Greek philosopher who followed the teachings of Epicurus. Several hundred scrolls, however, remained too fragile to touch.

In recent years, the problem has been approached in a completely different manner. A team led by the computer scientist Brent Seales developed a method whereby the scrolls are scanned with X-rays and the layers are separated digitally, which allows them to be unrolled without any physical contact. In 2023, an international competition called the Vesuvius Challenge offered prize money to anyone who could detect the ink in these scans. Using artificial intelligence, a student identified the first complete word, the Greek word for purple, and a team of three students later revealed whole columns of text about pleasure.

Experts are cautiously optimistic. Some argue that the technique could eventually render the entire library readable and that unknown works of ancient literature may be found among the scrolls. Others note that progress remains slow and that every reading must be checked carefully by specialists before any firm conclusion can be drawn.
options: the causes of the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79
efforts, old and new, to read the burnt scrolls of Herculaneum
the life and teachings of the philosopher Epicurus
the history of papyrus as a writing material
the rules of an international computer science competition
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘efforts, old and new, to read the burnt scrolls of Herculaneum’: metin elle açma denemelerinden yapay zekâya kadar okuma çabalarını anlatır. ‘causes’ geçen şık yalnızca giriş bilgisidir; ‘teachings’ geçen şık tek bir ayrıntıdır; ‘papyrus’ geçen şık metnin konusu değildir; ‘rules’ geçen şık yarışmanın kurallarından söz etmez.
