exercises.question: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
Rapa Nui, also known as Easter Island, is one of the most remote inhabited places on earth, and it is famous for nearly a thousand giant stone statues, called moai, which were carved by its Polynesian inhabitants. When Dutch sailors arrived in 1722, however, they found a small population and an island almost without trees. How could a society capable of such monumental work have ended up in this condition?

For several decades, the dominant answer was a story of ecological self-destruction. According to this view, which was popularised by the geographer Jared Diamond in his 2005 book Collapse, the islanders cut down their forests to move the statues, which led to soil loss, food shortages, warfare and a sharp fall in population. The island was thus portrayed as a warning, and its fate was commonly cited as evidence of what happens when a society uses up its resources.

More recently, this narrative has been challenged on several grounds. Archaeologists have argued that rats, which arrived with the first settlers, ate the seeds of the palm trees and contributed greatly to deforestation. Radiocarbon dating suggests that the island was settled later than once assumed, around AD 1200, which leaves less time for a large population to grow and collapse. A 2024 study of the stone gardens of the island, where crops were grown among rocks to keep the soil damp, estimated that the land could have supported only about 3,000 people, a figure comparable to the numbers that Europeans reported.

If these findings are correct, the real catastrophe came in the aftermath of contact. Diseases introduced by outsiders and slave raids in the 1860s reduced the population to little more than a hundred people by the 1870s. The revised account is therefore less about environmental failure than about the endurance of a community that adapted to a fragile landscape.
options: How the Moai Were Moved Across the Island
Jared Diamond and the Geography of Europe
Why Rats Are Dangerous to Modern Farmers
Rapa Nui: Rethinking the Story of an Ecological Collapse
The Dutch Discovery of the Pacific Ocean
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Rapa Nui: Rethinking the Story of an Ecological Collapse’: metin eski ‘çevresel intihar’ anlatısını ve onu sorgulayan yeni kanıtları anlatır. ‘Moved’ geçen başlık metinde işlenmez; ‘Geography’ geçen başlık Diamond’u yanlış konuya bağlar; ‘Farmers’ geçen başlık fareleri bugüne taşır; ‘Dutch’ geçen başlık tek bir ayrıntıdır.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the last paragraph is to ----.
exercises.passage:
Rapa Nui, also known as Easter Island, is one of the most remote inhabited places on earth, and it is famous for nearly a thousand giant stone statues, called moai, which were carved by its Polynesian inhabitants. When Dutch sailors arrived in 1722, however, they found a small population and an island almost without trees. How could a society capable of such monumental work have ended up in this condition?

For several decades, the dominant answer was a story of ecological self-destruction. According to this view, which was popularised by the geographer Jared Diamond in his 2005 book Collapse, the islanders cut down their forests to move the statues, which led to soil loss, food shortages, warfare and a sharp fall in population. The island was thus portrayed as a warning, and its fate was commonly cited as evidence of what happens when a society uses up its resources.

More recently, this narrative has been challenged on several grounds. Archaeologists have argued that rats, which arrived with the first settlers, ate the seeds of the palm trees and contributed greatly to deforestation. Radiocarbon dating suggests that the island was settled later than once assumed, around AD 1200, which leaves less time for a large population to grow and collapse. A 2024 study of the stone gardens of the island, where crops were grown among rocks to keep the soil damp, estimated that the land could have supported only about 3,000 people, a figure comparable to the numbers that Europeans reported.

If these findings are correct, the real catastrophe came in the aftermath of contact. Diseases introduced by outsiders and slave raids in the 1860s reduced the population to little more than a hundred people by the 1870s. The revised account is therefore less about environmental failure than about the endurance of a community that adapted to a fragile landscape.
options: show that the islanders were responsible for their own decline
present a different interpretation of what happened to the community
describe the methods used to carve the moai
defend the theory popularised by Jared Diamond
list all the diseases that Europeans brought to the island
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘present a different interpretation of what happened to the community’: paragraf hikâyeyi çevresel başarısızlıktan dayanıklılığa çevirir. ‘responsible’ geçen şık eski görüştür; ‘methods’ geçen şık paragrafta yoktur; ‘defend’ geçen şık tersini söyler; ‘list’ geçen şık yanlıştır, paragraf hastalıkları sıralamaz.

exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
Around 1450, in the German city of Mainz, a goldsmith named Johannes Gutenberg developed a printing system which combined movable metal type, a new kind of oil-based ink and a press adapted from those used to make wine. Printing itself was not new, since it had been practised in China and Korea for centuries, but the method of Gutenberg made it possible to produce identical copies quickly and cheaply. By 1500, presses had been established in more than two hundred European towns, and millions of books had been printed.

The consequences were profound, although historians still debate their extent. Before printing, books were copied by hand, which made them expensive and rare, and errors accumulated with every copy. Printed texts, by contrast, were standardised, so scholars in different countries could refer to the same page of the same edition. This uniformity is believed to have accelerated the progression of science, because new findings could be checked, criticised and developed by readers far away.

Printing also transformed religion and politics. When Martin Luther published his criticism of the Church in 1517, his pamphlets were reproduced so rapidly that they spread across Germany within weeks, and the Reformation that followed would be hard to imagine without the press. Governments soon realised that printed material could threaten their authority, and many introduced systems of censorship.

In the Ottoman Empire, the adoption of printing in Turkish took longer. Presses were run by Jewish, Armenian and Greek communities from the late fifteenth century onwards, but the first press printing books in Ottoman Turkish was set up by İbrahim Müteferrika only in 1727. The reasons for this delay are still debated, and simple explanations should be treated with caution.
options: Gutenberg invented printing, which had been unknown anywhere before 1450.
Printing was rejected in the Ottoman Empire because of religious objections.
The printing method of Gutenberg had wide effects on science, religion and politics, although it spread unevenly.
The Reformation began because books became more expensive.
Hand-copied books were more accurate than printed ones.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The printing method of Gutenberg had wide effects on science, religion and politics, although it spread unevenly.’: metin bilimsel, dinî ve siyasi sonuçları ve Osmanlı’daki gecikmeyi anlatır. ‘unknown’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, baskı Çin ve Kore’de biliniyordu; ‘objections’ geçen şık metnin uyardığı basit açıklamalardan biridir; ‘expensive’ geçen şık tersini söyler; ‘accurate’ geçen şık da tersini söyler, el yazmalarında hatalar birikirdi.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
exercises.passage:
When the British archaeologist Arthur Evans excavated the palace of Knossos on Crete at the beginning of the twentieth century, he found thousands of clay tablets marked with an unknown script. He called it Linear B, to distinguish it from an older script, Linear A, which had been found on the same island. Evans was convinced that the tablets recorded a local language unrelated to Greek, and his authority was so great that few scholars dared to contradict him.

The tablets had survived by accident. They were normally made of unbaked clay and would have been reused, but when the palace was destroyed by fire, they were hardened, which preserved them for more than three thousand years. Similar tablets were later discovered on the Greek mainland, at Pylos, which gave researchers a larger corpus to study.

The decipherment was finally achieved in 1952 by Michael Ventris, an architect who had been fascinated by the script since he heard Evans speak as a schoolboy. Building on the systematic work of the American scholar Alice Kober, who had noticed that some words changed their endings, Ventris arranged the signs in a grid according to their probable sounds. When he tested place names from Crete, the results suggested, to his own surprise, that the language was an early form of Greek. His conclusion was soon supported by newly found tablets and by the work of the linguist John Chadwick.

The content of the texts proved less romantic than many had hoped. Rather than poetry or history, they are mainly administrative records: lists of workers, animals, weapons and food. Yet for historians, this ordinary detail is precisely what makes them valuable, since it reveals how a Bronze Age economy was organised. Linear A, meanwhile, has still not been deciphered.
options: argue that Arthur Evans deserves credit for reading Linear B
explain how Linear B was deciphered and what the tablets reveal
describe the architecture of the palace of Knossos
show that the language of Linear A was an early form of Greek
criticise Alice Kober for delaying the work
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘explain how Linear B was deciphered and what the tablets reveal’: metin çözümün nasıl yapıldığını ve tabletlerin içeriğini anlatır. ‘deserves’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, Evans yanılmıştır; ‘architecture’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘Greek’ geçen bu şık Linear A’yı Linear B ile karıştırır, Linear A çözülmemiştir; ‘criticise’ geçen şık tersini söyler, Kober’in çalışması temel olmuştur.

units.title: Karışık zamanlı okuma
units.description: Fen, sağlık ve sosyal metinler art arda: teknoloji, çevre politikası ve kentler; metin başına 12 dakika
units.guide:
## Strateji

Gerçek sınavda okuma parçaları farklı alanlardan art arda gelir: bir teknoloji metninin ardından sağlık, sonra kent politikası. Alan değişince kelimeler de metnin kuruluşu da değişir. Bu ünitede yine metin başına **12 dakika** ayırırsın, ama her metne girerken önce türünü belirlersin: problem–çözüm mü, neden–sonuç mu, eski görüş–yeni kanıt mı? Türü tanıyan okur, cevabın hangi paragrafta olduğunu önceden tahmin eder.

## Nasıl uygulanır

1. **30 sn:** ilk cümleye ve soru köklerine bak; alanı ve metin türünü belirle.

2. **5 dk:** oku ve her paragrafa bir rol ver: "sorun", "çözüm", "sınır", "eleştiri".

3. **6 dk:** soruları çöz; tutum ve çıkarım sorularında temkin kelimelerine (*may, partly, remains controversial*) ve yön değiştiren bağlaçlara (*however, nevertheless*) dikkat et.

4. **30 sn:** belirsiz soruyu işaretle, önceki metni zihninde kapat ve sıradakine geç.

## Örnek

*In the first year, traffic fell by about a fifth. Over the following decade, however, congestion gradually returned.* Roller: "çözüm → sınır". Soru uzun vadeli etkiyi sorarsa cevabı *however*’dan sonra ararsın.

## Sınav ipucu

Tanımadığın bir alan seni yavaşlatabilir; bu normaldir. Teknik terimleri (ozone, telemedicine) anlamaya uğraşma, metnin iskeletine odaklan. Bir metinde 12 dakikayı aşarsan en olası şıkkı işaretle ve geç; kaybettiğin süreyi bir sonraki metinden geri alamazsın.

exercises.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
Heating buildings accounts for a substantial share of the energy used in the world, and most of this heat is still produced by burning gas, oil or coal. In the search for alternatives, many governments are now placing emphasis on a technology which is far from new: the heat pump. The basic principle was described in the nineteenth century, and the same mechanism is found in every household refrigerator.

A heat pump does not generate heat directly. Instead, it moves heat from one place to another. A fluid which boils at a very low temperature circulates through a closed loop; it absorbs thermal energy from the outside air or ground, is compressed so that its temperature rises, and then releases the heat inside the building. Because most of the energy is taken from the environment rather than produced by electricity, a typical heat pump delivers about three units of heat for every unit of electricity it consumes. Its efficiency is therefore several times higher than that of an ordinary electric heater.

A common misconception is that heat pumps cannot work in cold climates. In fact, they are widely used in Norway, Sweden and Finland, where winter temperatures frequently fall far below zero, although their performance declines as the outside air becomes colder.

The main barriers are financial and practical. Installation is expensive, older buildings may need better insulation before a heat pump can operate at an optimal level, and qualified installers are in short supply in many countries. For this reason, several European governments subsidise the purchase of heat pumps. Their environmental benefit also depends on how the electricity is generated: when it comes from clean sources, emissions can be reduced dramatically, whereas the benefit is smaller in a power system that relies heavily on fossil fuels.
options: Heat pumps were invented recently and have not yet been tested in cold countries.
Electric heaters are more efficient than heat pumps in most buildings.
Governments should stop all gas heating immediately.
Heat pumps are an efficient way of heating, but they face some financial and practical obstacles.
Refrigerators use more energy than any other household device.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Heat pumps are an efficient way of heating, but they face some financial and practical obstacles.’: metin ilkeyi, verimliliği ve maliyet, yalıtım, usta eksikliği gibi engelleri anlatır. ‘invented’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, ilke 19. yüzyıldan beri bilinir; ‘heaters’ geçen şık tersini söyler; ‘immediately’ geçen şık metinde olmayan bir öneridir; ‘Refrigerators’ geçen şık yalnızca bir benzetmeyi yanlış genelleştirir.

exercises.question: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
Most people imagine that the internet travels through the air, via satellites or wireless signals. In reality, the vast majority of international data, estimated at more than 95 per cent, is transmitted through cables which lie on the ocean floor. Several hundred of these cables are in operation today, and together they stretch for more than a million kilometres.

The idea itself is old. The first telegraph cable across the Atlantic was laid in 1858, although it failed after only a few weeks. Modern cables, by contrast, contain thin strands of glass called optical fibres, which carry information as pulses of light. In deep water, a cable may be no thicker than a garden hose, while near the shore it is protected by additional layers of steel, because this is where most damage occurs.

Faults are surprisingly common: more than a hundred are reported every year. The majority are caused not by deliberate attacks or natural disasters but by fishing equipment and ship anchors which are dragged across the sea floor. Repairing a cable requires a specialised ship, which lifts the damaged section to the surface, joins in a new piece and lowers it again, a procedure that can take days or even weeks. Fortunately, traffic can usually be sent through other cables, so most users never notice.

Nevertheless, some experts have raised concerns about the vulnerability of this network. Some small island nations depend on a single connection; when the cable of Tonga was damaged by a volcanic eruption in 2022, the country was cut off from the internet for several weeks. In addition, an increasing proportion of new cables is now paid for by a few large technology companies rather than by telephone firms, which raises questions about who should be responsible for protecting a resource on which the global economy depends.
options: Why Satellites Are Replacing Undersea Cables
The Failure of the First Atlantic Telegraph
How Fishing Boats Protect the Ocean Floor
Telephone Companies and Their Profits
The Hidden Cables That Carry the Internet
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The Hidden Cables That Carry the Internet’: metin verinin çoğunu taşıyan deniz altı kablolarını, arızalarını ve kırılganlıklarını anlatır. ‘Satellites’ geçen başlık metinle çelişir; ‘Telegraph’ geçen başlık tek bir ayrıntıdır; ‘Fishing’ geçen başlık tersini söyler, balıkçılık kablolara zarar verir; ‘Profits’ geçen başlık metinde yoktur.

nodes.description: Metin 1: Uzaktan tıbbın artıları ve sınırları. Metin 2: Kurşunlu benzinin uzun vedası. ys7 kelimeleri: session, evident, replacement, marginal, transmit, online, clinic, diagnosis ve 16 kelime daha.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
exercises.passage:
For most of the history of medicine, a consultation required the patient and the physician to be in the same room. Telemedicine, which allows care to be delivered through video calls, phone calls and digital messages, has existed for decades, but it remained a marginal practice until the COVID-19 pandemic. In 2020, when clinics were closed and patients were advised to stay at home, the number of remote consultations rose dramatically in many countries.

The benefits are evident for certain groups of patients. People who live in rural areas, far from a hospital, can avoid long and costly journeys, and those with long-term conditions such as diabetes can be monitored regularly through devices which transmit data on blood sugar or blood pressure to their doctors. Mental health services have also been delivered successfully online, and some studies suggest that patients are just as satisfied with video therapy as with face-to-face sessions.

However, telemedicine has clear limitations. Many diagnoses still depend on a physical examination, and a doctor cannot listen to the lungs of a patient or feel a swollen joint through a screen. There is also a risk that problems are missed when consultations are short and the patient is not seen in person. Furthermore, the technology is not equally accessible: elderly people and those without a reliable internet connection may find it difficult to use, which could widen existing inequalities in health care.

For these reasons, most experts now regard telemedicine not as a replacement for traditional care but as an addition to it. The challenge for health systems is to determine which services can safely be moved online and which should remain in the clinic, where a full examination is possible.
options: argue that hospitals will soon be unnecessary
describe the history of video technology
evaluate the advantages and limitations of telemedicine
warn patients against online therapy
explain how diabetes is treated
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘evaluate the advantages and limitations of telemedicine’: metin önce faydaları, sonra sınırları anlatır ve dengeli bir sonuca varır. ‘unnecessary’ geçen şık son paragrafla çelişir; ‘video’ geçen şık metnin konusu değildir; ‘warn’ geçen şık tersini söyler, çevrim içi terapi başarılı bulunmuştur; ‘diabetes’ geçen şık yalnızca bir örnektir.

exercises.question: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
In the 1920s, engineers at General Motors discovered that adding a lead compound to petrol prevented the knocking noise which damaged car engines. The additive, called tetraethyl lead, was cheap and effective, and within a few decades it was being used in almost every country in the world. Yet even at the time, some scientists warned that lead was a dangerous poison.

Their concerns were later confirmed. Lead released from vehicle exhausts accumulated in the air, soil and dust of cities, and it entered the human body mainly through breathing and swallowing. Because lead affects the developing brain, children were especially vulnerable. Research which was carried out from the 1970s onwards linked exposure to lower intelligence scores, problems with attention and, in adults, heart disease. Evidence of the scale of contamination came partly from the geochemist Clair Patterson, who showed that lead levels in the environment had risen enormously since industrialisation.

The policy response was gradual. The United States began to remove lead from petrol in the 1970s, partly because it damaged new devices that were required to reduce other emissions, and many wealthy countries followed in the 1980s and 1990s. In poorer countries, however, leaded fuel remained in use for much longer. A campaign which was coordinated by the United Nations Environment Programme from 2002 gradually persuaded the remaining governments to stop, and in 2021 Algeria became the last country to end its sale.

According to UN estimates, the elimination of leaded petrol prevents more than a million early deaths every year. Interestingly, some researchers have even suggested that falling lead exposure contributed to the drop in violent crime in several countries, although this hypothesis remains highly controversial.
options: The Long Road to Removing Lead from Petrol
How Lead Improved Engine Performance Safely
Algeria: The First Country to Ban Leaded Fuel
The Proven Link Between Lead and Crime
Why Children Are Immune to Lead
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The Long Road to Removing Lead from Petrol’: metin 1920’lerden 2021’e uzanan yavaş kaldırma sürecini anlatır. ‘Safely’ geçen başlık metinle çelişir, kurşun zehirdir; ‘Algeria’ geçen başlık yanlıştır, Cezayir son ülkedir; ‘Proven’ geçen başlık fazla kesindir, bu hipotez tartışmalıdır; ‘Immune’ geçen başlık tersini söyler, çocuklar özellikle savunmasızdır.

nodes.title: Sosyal: trafik ücreti ve teleferik
nodes.description: Metin 1: Londra’nın trafik sıkışıklığı ücreti. Metin 2: Medellín’in teleferikleri. ys7 kelimeleri: core, influential, circumstance, complicate, gradual, drastic, reversal, planner ve 17 kelime daha.

exercises.question: Which of the following best summarises the passage?
exercises.passage:
Traffic congestion is one of the most persistent problems of large cities, and building more roads rarely solves it, because new space tends to attract new traffic. In February 2003, London opted for a different approach. Under a scheme introduced by the mayor, Ken Livingstone, drivers entering central London on weekdays were required to pay a daily charge of five pounds, which was enforced by cameras that recorded vehicle number plates.

The scheme was highly controversial before it began. Business groups warned of a drastic loss of customers, and many commentators predicted that drivers would simply pay and continue as before. In the first year, however, traffic entering the zone fell by about a fifth, and delays caused by congestion dropped by around 30 per cent. The revenue, which by law had to be spent on transport, was largely invested in the bus network, and the number of bus passengers rose substantially.

The long-term picture is more complicated. Over the following decade, congestion gradually returned to levels close to those before the charge, even though the number of private cars in the zone remained lower. This reversal has been attributed to a wide range of factors, including extensive roadworks, the reallocation of road space to buses, cyclists and pedestrians, and a surge in delivery vans and private hire vehicles, which were partly exempt from the charge.

Despite these mixed results, the London scheme has been influential. Stockholm introduced a permanent charge in 2007 after a trial and a referendum, and New York began charging drivers in parts of Manhattan in 2025. For many planners, the core lesson is that pricing can change behaviour, but only if it is combined with good public transport and revised as circumstances change.
options: The charge reduced traffic at first, but its long-term effect on congestion was weaker, although the idea spread to other cities.
The congestion charge failed completely and was abolished.
Building more roads is the best way to reduce traffic.
Business groups were right that shops would lose customers.
Private hire vehicles were the main reason why the charge was introduced.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The charge reduced traffic at first, but its long-term effect on congestion was weaker, although the idea spread to other cities.’: metin ilk başarıyı, sonraki geri dönüşü ve Stockholm ile New York’a yayılmayı anlatır. ‘abolished’ geçen şık metinde yoktur; ‘Building’ ile başlayan şık metnin ilk cümlesiyle çelişir; ‘shops’ geçen şık metinde desteklenmez; ‘introduced’ geçen şık neden ile sonucu karıştırır.

exercises.question: The main purpose of the passage is to ----.
exercises.passage:
In the early 1990s, Medellín in Colombia was often described as one of the most violent cities in the world. Many of its poorest residents lived in informal neighbourhoods that had been built on steep hillsides around the valley, where roads were narrow and public services were limited. Reaching a job in the city centre could involve a long walk followed by several bus journeys.

In 2004, the city opened the first line of the Metrocable, a system of cable cars which connected these hillside districts directly to the metro network. The technology was borrowed from ski resorts, and it had a crucial advantage: the cable cars could be built above existing houses without the displacement of thousands of residents, which a new road would have required. For many people, journeys which had previously taken more than an hour were reduced to a fraction of that time.

The cable cars were part of a broader strategy, sometimes called social urbanism, whereby the municipal government concentrated public investment in the most marginalised areas. New schools, parks and public buildings of high architectural quality were placed near the stations, with the explicit aim of restoring the dignity and trust of local communities. A study published in 2012 found that violence declined more sharply in neighbourhoods served by the Metrocable than in similar areas elsewhere in the city.

Researchers caution, however, that the causal link is difficult to establish, since many other changes took place in Medellín at the same time, including political reforms and a reduction in organised crime. Some residents have also complained that the benefits were unequally distributed. Nevertheless, the project has inspired similar systems in cities such as La Paz, Caracas and Mexico City.
options: describe the Metrocable and assess claims about its social effects
explain how ski resorts build cable cars
prove that cable cars end violence in any city
criticise the municipal government of Medellín
compare the transport systems of La Paz and Caracas
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘describe the Metrocable and assess claims about its social effects’: metin sistemi tanıtır, şiddetteki düşüşle ilişkisini aktarır ve bu ilişkinin sınırlarını tartışır. ‘resorts’ geçen şık tek bir ayrıntıdır; ‘prove’ geçen şık son paragrafın temkiniyle çelişir; ‘criticise’ geçen şık metnin genel tonuna uymaz; ‘compare’ geçen şık yalnızca son cümlede anılan şehirleri ana konu yapar.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin ana fiili hangisidir? ‘Research which was carried out from the 1970s onwards linked exposure to lower intelligence scores, problems with attention and, in adults, heart disease.’
options: was carried out
linked
carrying
was linked
lowered

boils
closed
circulating
is boiled
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘circulates’. İskelet: özne ‘A fluid’ + ana fiil ‘circulates’ + ‘through a closed loop’. ‘boils’ which yan cümlesinin fiilidir; ‘closed’ ‘loop’ ismini niteleyen bir sıfat-ortaçtır; ‘circulating’ ve ‘is boiled’ cümlede geçmeyen biçimlerdir.

exercises.question: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
exercises.passage:
In 1985, British scientists working in Antarctica published measurements which showed that the ozone layer above the continent was becoming dramatically thinner every spring. The ozone layer, which lies high in the atmosphere, absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun, and its destruction would increase the risk of skin cancer and damage crops and marine life. The main cause was soon identified: chlorofluorocarbons, or CFCs, synthetic chemicals that were widely used in refrigerators, air conditioners and spray cans.

The international response was remarkably fast: in 1987, only two years after the discovery was announced, governments signed the Montreal Protocol, which committed them to reducing the production of CFCs. The agreement was later strengthened several times as the scientific evidence became clearer, and the production of these substances was eventually stopped altogether. In 2009, it became the first treaty in the history of the United Nations to be accepted by every member state.

Several factors explain this success: the threat was easy to understand, and the evidence was difficult to dispute. Alternatives to CFCs were already being developed by industry, so the economic burden of the transition was relatively modest. Moreover, a fund was established to help developing countries cover their costs, which encouraged their participation.

The results are now measurable: according to a 2023 assessment by a panel of UN experts, the ozone layer is on track to recover to its 1980 condition by around 2040 over most of the world, and by around 2066 over Antarctica. Because CFCs are also powerful greenhouse gases, the protocol has slowed climate change as well. Many observers therefore regard it as a model, although they acknowledge that reducing carbon emissions is a far more complex problem.
options: The ozone layer has already fully recovered over Antarctica.
The Montreal Protocol is a rare example of a fast and successful international response to an environmental threat.
CFCs were never a serious problem because they were not widely used.
The Montreal Protocol failed because developing countries refused to join.
Climate change and ozone loss are exactly the same problem.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The Montreal Protocol is a rare example of a fast and successful international response to an environmental threat.’: metin hızlı tepkiyi, başarının nedenlerini ve ölçülebilir sonuçları anlatır. ‘fully’ geçen şık yanlıştır, iyileşme 2066 civarında beklenir; ‘never’ geçen şık metinle çelişir; ‘refused’ geçen şık tersini söyler, her üye devlet anlaşmayı kabul etti; ‘exactly’ geçen şık son cümleyle çelişir.

exercises.question: Which of the following is the best title for the passage?
exercises.passage:
As cities expand, natural ground is replaced by concrete and asphalt, which rain cannot pass through. Water therefore runs quickly into drains, and during heavy storms these systems are easily overwhelmed, which leads to floods in streets and homes. In China, where hundreds of cities have experienced serious flooding in recent decades, the government responded in 2015 by launching a national programme known as the sponge city initiative.

The concept, which is associated with the landscape architect Yu Kongjian, is to make cities behave more like natural landscapes. Rather than sending rainwater away as fast as possible, a sponge city is designed to absorb, store and gradually release it. This is achieved through a wide range of measures, including pavements that let water through, green roofs, artificial wetlands and parks which are allowed to flood for short periods. The stored water can later be used for watering plants or cleaning, and vegetation helps to filter pollutants before the water reaches rivers.

The goals of the programme are ambitious. Initially, the approach was tested in thirty pilot cities, and the authorities have set the target that by 2030, 80 per cent of urban areas should absorb and reuse at least 70 per cent of their rainwater. However, the implementation has been uneven. In July 2021, extreme rainfall in Zhengzhou, one of the pilot cities, caused deadly floods, which prompted questions about the limits of the approach.

Supporters reply that no design can cope with every storm, particularly as climate change makes extreme rainfall more frequent. In their view, sponge city measures should be combined with conventional drainage and early warning systems rather than replace them. Similar ideas are now being tested in cities such as Berlin, Copenhagen and Rotterdam.
options: Why China Has Stopped Building Drains
The Zhengzhou Floods Prove Sponge Cities Are Useless
How Yu Kongjian Designed Berlin
Sponge Cities: A Promising but Imperfect Answer to Urban Flooding
Green Roofs as a Source of Drinking Water
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Sponge Cities: A Promising but Imperfect Answer to Urban Flooding’: metin yaklaşımın amacını, yöntemlerini ve Zhengzhou’da görülen sınırlarını anlatır. ‘Drains’ geçen başlık son paragrafla çelişir, geleneksel drenaj korunmalıdır; ‘Useless’ geçen başlık destekçilerin cevabını yok sayar; ‘Berlin’ geçen başlık iki ayrı bilgiyi birleştirir; ‘Drinking’ geçen başlık metinde yoktur, su temizlik ve sulama için kullanılır.

The stored water can later be used for watering plants or cleaning, and vegetation helps to filter pollutants before the water reaches rivers.

The goals of the programme are ambitious. Initially, the approach was tested in thirty pilot cities, and the authorities have set the target that by 2030, 80 per cent of urban areas should absorb and reuse at least 70 per cent of their rainwater. However, the implementation has been uneven. In July 2021, extreme rainfall in Zhengzhou, one of the pilot cities, caused deadly floods, which prompted questions about the limits of the approach.

Supporters reply that no design can cope with every storm, particularly as climate change makes extreme rainfall more frequent. In their view, sponge city measures should be combined with conventional drainage and early warning systems rather than replace them. Similar ideas are now being tested in cities such as Berlin, Copenhagen and Rotterdam.
options: believe sponge cities can prevent every flood
want to abolish early warning systems
see sponge measures as one part of a wider system of flood protection
blame climate change for the failure of the programme
think the programme should be ended after Zhengzhou
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘see sponge measures as one part of a wider system of flood protection’: destekçilere göre bu önlemler geleneksel drenaj ve erken uyarı sistemleriyle birlikte kullanılmalıdır. ‘prevent’ geçen şık ‘no design can cope with every storm’ ile çelişir; ‘abolish’ geçen şık tersini söyler; ‘blame’ geçen şık metinde yoktur, iklim değişikliği yalnızca yağışın artma nedenidir; ‘ended’ geçen şık destekçilerin görüşüne aykırıdır.

exercises.question: The word ‘uneven’ in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ----.

options: illegal
rapid
inconsistent
expensive
secret
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘inconsistent’: uygulama her yerde aynı başarıyı göstermemiştir; Zhengzhou örneği bunu gösterir. ‘illegal’ ve ‘secret’ bağlamla ilgisizdir; ‘rapid’ bir hız bildirir; ‘expensive’ maliyetle ilgilidir, metin burada maliyetten söz etmez.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘The agreement was later strengthened several times as the scientific evidence became clearer.’
options: Bilimsel kanıtlar netleştikçe anlaşma daha sonra birkaç kez güçlendirildi.
Bilimsel kanıtlar netleştikçe anlaşma daha sonra birkaç kez zayıflatıldı.
Bilimsel kanıtlar belirsizleştikçe anlaşma daha sonra birkaç kez güçlendirildi.
Bilimsel kanıtlar netleşmeden önce anlaşma bir kez güçlendirildi.
Bilimsel kanıtlar netleştikçe anlaşma ileride birkaç kez güçlendirilecek.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Bilimsel kanıtlar netleştikçe anlaşma daha sonra birkaç kez güçlendirildi’. İskelet: özne ‘The agreement’ + edilgen geçmiş zaman ‘was strengthened’ + ‘as …’ (…dikçe). ‘zayıflatıldı’ geçen şık fiili tersine çevirir; ‘belirsizleştikçe’ geçen şık yan cümleyi tersine çevirir; ‘netleşmeden’ geçen şık hem zamanı hem sayıyı değiştirir; ‘güçlendirilecek’ geçen şık geçmişi geleceğe çevirir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Initially, the approach was tested in thirty pilot cities.’
options: Sonunda yaklaşım otuz pilot şehirde denendi.
Başlangıçta yaklaşım yalnızca bir pilot şehirde denendi.
Başlangıçta yaklaşım otuz pilot şehirde denendi.
Başlangıçta yaklaşım otuz pilot şehirde reddedildi.
Başlangıçta otuz pilot şehir yaklaşımı test edecek.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Başlangıçta yaklaşım otuz pilot şehirde denendi’. İskelet: ‘Initially’ + özne ‘the approach’ + edilgen ‘was tested’ + ‘in thirty pilot cities’. ‘Sonunda’ ile başlayan şık zaman zarfını tersine çevirir; ‘yalnızca’ geçen şık sayıyı değiştirir; ‘reddedildi’ geçen şık fiili değiştirir; ‘edecek’ geçen şık edilgen geçmişi etken geleceğe çevirir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Hiçbir tasarım her fırtınayla baş edemez.’
options: Every design can cope with most storms.
No design could cope with the storm in Zhengzhou.
Some designs cannot cope with any storm.
No design can cope with every storm.
No design will ever cause a storm.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘No design can cope with every storm.’: ‘Hiçbir … -emez’ İngilizcede olumlu fiille ‘No design can’ olarak kurulur. ‘storms’ geçen şık niceleyicileri değiştirir; ‘Zhengzhou’ geçen şık genel yargıyı tek bir geçmiş olaya indirger; ‘designs’ geçen şık ‘bazı’ ve ‘hiçbir fırtına’ der; ‘cause’ geçen şık fiili değiştirir.

exercises.question: Bu cümlenin en uygun İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir? ‘Ozon tabakası güneşten gelen zararlı ultraviyole ışınların çoğunu emer.’
options: The ozone layer absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun.
The ozone layer reflects all of the harmful radiation back to the Sun.
The ozone layer absorbed some of the harmless radiation from the Sun.
Ultraviolet radiation from the Sun destroys most of the ozone layer.
The ozone layer will absorb most of the harmful radiation in the future.
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘The ozone layer absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun.’. İskelet: özne ‘The ozone layer’ + geniş zaman ‘absorbs’ + ‘most of the harmful … radiation’. ‘reflects’ geçen şık fiili ve niceleyiciyi değiştirir; ‘harmless’ geçen şık hem zamanı hem anlamı değiştirir; ‘destroys’ geçen şık özne ile nesneyi yer değiştirir; ‘future’ geçen şık geniş zamanı geleceğe çevirir.

exercises.question: Although the London charge reduced traffic in its first year, ----.
options: it was introduced by the mayor in 2003
congestion later returned to levels close to those before the charge
because drivers had to pay five pounds
which was enforced by cameras
so the number of bus passengers rose
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘congestion later returned to levels close to those before the charge’: ‘Although’ ilk başarıya ters düşen bir sonuç ister. ‘mayor’ geçen şık zıtlık kurmayan bir bilgidir; ‘because’ ile başlayan şık ana cümle olamaz; ‘cameras’ geçen şık which ile başladığı için ana cümle olamaz; ‘passengers’ geçen şık ‘so’ ile aynı yönde bir sonuç verir.

exercises.question: ----, the ozone layer is expected to recover over most of the world by around 2040.
options: Thanks to the sharp fall in CFC production
Unless CFCs are banned
Although CFCs were removed from use
Whose production was stopped
Because CFCs are still widely used
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘Thanks to the sharp fall in CFC production’: iyileşmenin nedeni CFC üretimindeki düşüştür. ‘Unless’ ile başlayan şık zaten yasaklanmış maddeler için anlamsız bir koşuldur; ‘Although’ ile başlayan şık nedeni zıtlık gibi sunar; ‘Whose’ ile başlayan şık niteleyecek bir isim bulamaz; ‘widely’ geçen şık iyileşmeyle çelişir.

exercises.question: Sponge cities are designed to absorb and store rainwater ----.
options: so that it can be released gradually and used again
because they are built entirely of concrete
unless it never rains in summer
which caused deadly floods in Zhengzhou
although the stored water can be used for cleaning
exercises.explanation: Doğru cevap ‘so that it can be released gradually and used again’: ‘so that’ tasarımın amacını bildirir ve metinle uyuşur. ‘concrete’ geçen şık metinle çelişir, sorun betonun suyu geçirmemesidir; ‘unless’ ile başlayan şık anlamsız bir koşuldur; ‘deadly’ geçen şıkta which yanlış ismi niteler; ‘cleaning’ geçen şık ‘although’ ile zıtlık kurar, oysa bu bir amaçtır.

exercises.question: Because the sample in the preliminary study was very small, the researchers warned that their findings should not be ---- to the whole population.
options: contradicted
transcribed
generalised
simulated
rotated
exercises.explanation: Küçük bir örneklemden elde edilen bulgular bütün nüfusa ‘generalise’ edilemez (genellenemez); ‘generalise to’ kalıbı tam bu anlamı verir. ‘contradicted’ (çelişmek) ‘to the whole population’ ile anlam kurmaz; ‘transcribed’ (yazıya dökmek) ve ‘simulated’ (benzetimini yapmak) bulgular için uygun değildir; ‘rotated’ (döndürmek) ise fiziksel bir hareket anlatır.

exercises.question: Rising fuel prices are expected to ---- the difficulties of farmers in the region, many of whom are already struggling to cope with a long drought.
options: aggravate
mitigate
verify
portray
resemble
exercises.explanation: Kuraklıkla zaten zor durumda olan çiftçilerin sorunlarını artan yakıt fiyatları ancak ağırlaştırır: ‘aggravate’ (kötüleştirmek). ‘mitigate’ (hafifletmek) anlamca terstir, çünkü fiyat artışı sorunları azaltmaz; ‘verify’ (doğrulamak), ‘portray’ (betimlemek) ve ‘resemble’ (benzemek) ise zorluklarla anlamlı bir ilişki kurmaz.

exercises.question: Although the two reports were prepared by different teams working independently, their conclusions were almost ----, differing only in a few minor details.
options: vague
reciprocal
obscure
drastic
identical
exercises.explanation: ‘differing only in a few minor details’ (yalnızca birkaç küçük ayrıntıda farklı) ifadesi sonuçların neredeyse aynı olduğunu gösterir: ‘identical’. ‘vague’ (belirsiz) ve ‘obscure’ (anlaşılmaz) benzerlik anlatmaz; ‘reciprocal’ (karşılıklı) iki tarafın birbirine yaptığı bir şey içindir; ‘drastic’ (köklü, sert) ise değişiklikler için kullanılır.

exercises.question: The data collected from more than 2,000 households across the country in 2019 ---- that the level of household debt had risen sharply.
options: showing
showed
which showed
to show
having shown
exercises.explanation: Cümlenin öznesi ‘The data’ dır; ‘collected from … in 2019’ onu niteleyen bir sıfat-fiil grubudur, bu yüzden boşluğa çekimli bir ana fiil gerekir: ‘showed’. ‘showing’ ve ‘having shown’ çekimsiz fiilimsilerdir; ‘which showed’ cümleyi ana fiilsiz bir yan cümleye çevirir; ‘to show’ da tek başına yüklem olamaz.

exercises.question: Since the new safety protocol ---- in 2021, the number of infections reported in the hospital has fallen by almost a third.
options: has been introduced
is introduced
had introduced
was introduced
introduces
exercises.explanation: ‘Since’ ile başlayan zaman bağlacı geçmişteki başlangıç anını gösterir ve belirli bir yıl (‘in 2021’) içerir; bu yüzden edilgen geçmiş zaman ‘was introduced’ gelir. ‘has been introduced’ belirli bir geçmiş tarihle kullanılmaz; ‘is introduced’ ve ‘introduces’ şimdiki zamandır; ‘had introduced’ ise etken çatıdır ve protokol kendini uygulamaya koyamaz.

exercises.question: Had the engineers checked their calculations more carefully, the bridge ---- so soon after it was opened to traffic.
options: would not have collapsed
will not collapse
did not collapse
would not collapse
had not collapsed
exercises.explanation: ‘Had the engineers checked’ devrik üçüncü tip koşul cümlesidir (If the engineers had checked); geçmişte gerçekleşmemiş bir koşulun sonucu ‘would not have collapsed’ ile verilir. ‘will not collapse’ birinci tip, ‘would not collapse’ ikinci tip koşula aittir; ‘did not collapse’ ve ‘had not collapsed’ ise koşul cümlesinin sonuç kısmında kullanılmaz.

exercises.question: ---- the lack of reliable data, the committee decided to postpone its decision until a more systematic study had been completed.
options: Although
Despite
Owing to
Unless
As long as
exercises.explanation: Güvenilir veri eksikliği kararın ertelenmesinin nedenidir; isim öbeği alan neden bildiren ‘Owing to’ gerekir. ‘Despite’ zıtlık kurar ve anlamı bozar; ‘Although’, ‘Unless’ ve ‘As long as’ ise bağlaçtır, ardından tam bir yan cümle ister, isim öbeği almaz.

exercises.question: Historians are still debating ---- the ancient city was abandoned so suddenly in the third century.
options: which
what
whom
whose
why
exercises.explanation: Boşluktan sonra eksiksiz bir cümle (the ancient city was abandoned) gelir; tartışılan şey terk edilmenin nedenidir, bu yüzden isim cümleciği ‘why’ ile kurulur. ‘what’ ve ‘which’ cümlede eksik bir öğe ister; ‘whom’ nesne konumundaki bir kişi, ‘whose’ ise ardından bir isim gerektirir.

exercises.passage: In 1887, a Polish eye doctor named Ludwik Zamenhof published a short book introducing a new language, which he hoped would (1)---- people from different nations to communicate on equal terms. He signed the book as "Doktoro Esperanto", meaning "one who hopes", and the name was soon given to the language itself. Esperanto was designed to be easy to learn: its grammar has no irregular verbs, and all nouns end in the same letter. (2)----, because most of its vocabulary was taken from European languages, it was far less easy for speakers in Asia or Africa. The language attracted many supporters in the early twentieth century, but its growth was (3)---- by two world wars and, in some countries, by governments that viewed its speakers with suspicion. Today, estimates of the number of speakers range from tens of thousands to a few million, although such figures are very difficult to (4)----. Critics argue that Esperanto has failed, since English has become the international language instead. Its supporters, (5)----, point out that it is still used at conferences and online more than a century after its creation.

enable
insist
suggest

options: Therefore

exercises.question: (5) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?

for example
on the other hand
in other words

exercises.question: Although the results of the pilot study were promising, ----.
options: since the sample included more than ten thousand patients from several countries
the drug was therefore approved for use in all hospitals without delay
because the findings had already been confirmed by independent laboratories
the researchers stressed that a larger trial was needed before any firm conclusions could be drawn
which is why the team decided to publish them as quickly as possible
exercises.explanation: ‘Although’ zıtlık ister: sonuçlar umut verici olsa da araştırmacılar kesin sonuç için daha büyük bir deneme gerektiğini vurguladı (‘the researchers stressed that a larger trial was needed …’). ‘since’ ve ‘because’ ile başlayan seçenekler ana cümle olmadığından cümleyi tamamlamaz; ‘approved … therefore’ ve ‘publish … quickly’ içeren seçenekler umut verici sonuçlarla zıtlık kurmaz, aksine onları destekler.

exercises.question: ----, the company would not have been able to survive the financial crisis of 2008.
options: Unless it reduces its overhead costs significantly
Had it not received a large loan from the government
Even though its profits rose steadily throughout the decade
As long as the economy continues to grow
Since its main rivals have been forced to close
exercises.explanation: Ana cümle ‘would not have been able’ ile üçüncü tip koşulun sonucunu verir; koşul kısmı da devrik geçmiş yapıdadır: ‘Had it not received a large loan from the government’. ‘Unless … reduces’ ve ‘As long as … continues’ şimdiki/gelecek zamana ait koşullardır; ‘profits rose’ zıtlık kurar ama gerçek dışı sonucu açıklamaz; ‘rivals have been forced’ ise zaman uyumunu bozar.

exercises.question: The new interface is so complicated that ----.
options: many older users have given up trying to use it
it has been praised for its simplicity by most reviewers
the designers made it as simple as they possibly could
whereas the previous version required more training
which explains why it is popular with beginners
exercises.explanation: ‘so … that’ yapısı bir sonucu bekler: arayüz çok karmaşık olduğu için yaşlı kullanıcıların çoğu kullanmaktan vazgeçmiştir (‘many older users have given up trying to use it’). ‘simplicity’ ve ‘simple’ içeren seçenekler karmaşıklıkla çelişir; ‘whereas’ ve ‘which explains’ ile başlayan seçenekler ‘that’ sonrasında gereken tam cümleyi kurmaz, ‘popular with beginners’ ise anlamca da terstir.

exercises.question: Not only did the long drought reduce crop yields in the region, ----.
options: so farmers were able to export more grain than usual
although rainfall was much higher than in previous years
but the harvest was also the best in a decade
because of which the government will cut taxes next year
but it also led to a sharp rise in food prices
exercises.explanation: ‘Not only … but (it) also’ kalıbı aynı yönde ikinci bir sonuç ekler: kuraklık hem verimi düşürdü hem de gıda fiyatlarını artırdı (‘but it also led to a sharp rise in food prices’). ‘harvest was also the best’ kalıba uysa da verimin düştüğü bilgisiyle çelişir; ‘export more grain’ ve ‘rainfall was much higher’ kuraklıkla uyuşmaz; ‘because of which’ ise ‘not only’ kalıbını tamamlamaz.

exercises.question: Most scientists remain cautious about the new findings, ----.
options: because the experiment has already been repeated successfully in dozens of laboratories
so that the results can be published more quickly
given that the experiment has not yet been replicated by an independent team
unless they were confirmed by other researchers long ago
which have already been accepted by every expert in the field

exercises.passage: In the 1920s, a series of experiments was carried out at the Hawthorne Works, a large electrical factory near Chicago. The original aim was straightforward: managers wanted to know whether brighter lighting would make workers more productive. According to the most widely repeated account, productivity rose when the lights were turned up, but it also rose when they were turned down, and it fell only when the light became so dim that workers could hardly see. Later studies in the same factory, which examined rest breaks and working hours, appeared to produce similar results. The researchers concluded that the changes in output were caused not by the physical conditions themselves but by the attention that the workers were receiving. Decades later, the term "Hawthorne effect" was introduced to describe the tendency of people to change their behaviour simply because they know they are being observed. The idea has since become a standard warning in research methods courses, and it is often used to explain why participants in a study may perform better than they would in ordinary circumstances. In recent years, however, scepticism about the original experiments has grown. Critics, who have examined the original records closely, have pointed out that the samples were extremely small, that the procedures were not systematic, and that other factors, such as the economic insecurity of the period, may have influenced the workers. When two economists re-examined the surviving data in 2011, they found that the pattern was far less clear than the famous story suggested. None of this means that being observed has no influence on behaviour; rather, it indicates that the effect is probably more modest and more variable than textbooks once implied. Ironically, a concept that is used to warn researchers about weak evidence may itself rest on rather weak evidence.
exercises.question: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
options: a well-known research concept and the growing doubts about the experiments on which it is based
the effects of lighting on the health of factory workers in the 1920s
the history of the electrical industry in the United States
the reasons why economists have rejected research methods courses
how managers can raise productivity by reducing working hours
exercises.explanation: Metin ‘Hawthorne etkisi’ kavramını, nasıl ortaya çıktığını ve dayandığı deneylere yönelik artan kuşkuları anlatır: ‘a well-known research concept and the growing doubts about the experiments on which it is based’. Aydınlatmanın sağlığa etkisi (‘health’) incelenmez, deneyler verimlilikle ilgilidir; elektrik sanayisinin tarihi (‘industry’) yalnızca arka plandır; iktisatçılar dersleri reddetmez (‘rejected’), verileri yeniden inceler; çalışma saatlerini azaltma (‘reducing’) ise bir yönetim önerisi olarak sunulmaz.

exercises.passage: Construction of the bell tower in Pisa began in 1173, but the building had reached only its third storey when it started to lean. The cause was the ground beneath it: the tower stands on soft layers of clay and sand, which compressed more on the south side than on the north. Work was interrupted for almost a century, largely because of wars, and engineers now believe that this long pause allowed the soil to become firmer, which may have prevented an early collapse. When building resumed, the upper floors were deliberately constructed with one side slightly taller than the other in an attempt to correct the tilt, which is why the tower is in fact slightly curved. Over the following centuries, the lean continued to increase gradually. By 1990, the top of the tower was more than four metres away from where it would be if the structure were perfectly vertical, and the authorities closed it to visitors because of fears about its stability. An international committee of engineers was then appointed to find a solution that would reduce the tilt without destroying the character of the monument. After several proposals had been rejected, the committee chose a remarkably simple method. Small amounts of soil were carefully removed from beneath the north side, so that this side would settle slightly and pull the tower back towards the vertical. The process was monitored continuously by instruments, and by 2001 the lean had been reduced by about forty centimetres. The tower was then reopened to the public, and measurements suggest that it has continued to straighten very slightly since then. Engineers expect it to remain stable for at least two centuries, although nobody intends to make it stand completely straight, since its famous lean is the main reason why millions of tourists visit it each year.
exercises.question: Which of the following could be the best title for the passage?
options: Why Medieval Builders Preferred Soft Ground

exercises.explanation: Metin kulenin neden eğildiğini ve mühendislerin eğimi tamamen düzeltmeden onu nasıl güvenli hâle getirdiğini anlatır: ‘How the Leaning Tower of Pisa Was Saved Without Being Straightened’. Ortaçağ ustalarının yumuşak zemini tercih ettiği (‘Preferred’) söylenmez; savaşlar şehri yıkmamış (‘Destroyed’), yalnızca inşaatı durdurmuştur; kimse kuleyi tamamen dikleştirmek (‘Perfectly Vertical’) istemez; turizmin azaldığı (‘Decline’) değil, eğimin turist çektiği belirtilir.

Most of our participants live in rural areas.
exercises.explanation: Görüşmeci sürenin zaman içindeki değişimi izlemek için gerekli olduğunu anladığını söyler; bunu açıklayan yanıt aynı çocukları büyürken izleyen boylamsal çalışma bilgisidir: ‘It's a longitudinal study, so we need to follow the same children as they grow older.’ Verilerin çoğunun toplandığı (‘finished’) uzun süreyi açıklamaz; bütçe onayı (‘budget’) ve katılımcıların kırsalda yaşaması (‘rural’) süreyle ilgili değildir; ‘a few weeks’ ise sürenin gerekli olduğu sonucuyla çelişir.

exercises.question:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

Hardly had the new policy been announced when critics began to question whether it could be put into practice.
options: Critics questioned the new policy for a long time before it was finally announced.
Few critics believed that the new policy would ever be announced.
Although the new policy was put into practice quickly, critics did not question it.
As soon as the new policy was announced, critics started to ask whether it could actually be implemented.
Critics had hardly any doubts about whether the new policy could be put into practice.
exercises.explanation: ‘Hardly had … when’ bir olayın hemen ardından ötekinin geldiğini anlatır: politika açıklanır açıklanmaz eleştirmenler uygulanabilirliğini sorguladı (‘As soon as the new policy was announced, critics started to ask …’). ‘before it was finally announced’ sıralamayı tersine çevirir; ‘would ever be announced’ açıklanma olasılığına kuşkuyu konu eder; ‘did not question’ ve ‘hardly any doubts’ ise sorgulamayı ortadan kaldırarak anlamı tersine çevirir.

exercises.question:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

The more data the researchers collected, the less certain they became about their original hypothesis.
options: The researchers collected less data because they were already certain about their hypothesis.
Collecting more data made the researchers more confident that their hypothesis was correct.
As the researchers gathered more data, their doubts about their original hypothesis increased.
The researchers changed their hypothesis before they began to collect any data.
Although the researchers collected a great deal of data, their hypothesis remained unchanged.
exercises.explanation: ‘The more …, the less …’ yapısı veri arttıkça hipoteze duyulan güvenin azaldığını anlatır: ‘As the researchers gathered more data, their doubts about their original hypothesis increased.’ ‘already certain’ nedensellik ilişkisini değiştirir; ‘more confident’ anlamı tersine çevirir; ‘before they began’ zaman sırasını bozar; ‘remained unchanged’ ise artan kuşkudan söz etmez.

exercises.passage: The Dead Sea, which lies between Jordan, Israel and the West Bank, has been shrinking for decades, and its surface is now falling by about a metre each year. ---- As a result, far less fresh water reaches the lake, while evaporation in the hot, dry climate continues as before. The retreating water has also left behind thousands of sinkholes, which have damaged roads and farmland along the shore.
exercises.question: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: The water is so salty that swimmers can float easily on its surface.
This is mainly because the River Jordan, its main source, is heavily used upstream for farming and drinking water.
Tourists have visited the area to bathe in its waters since ancient times.
Mud from the lake is sold all over the world as a beauty product.
Several plans to build new hotels near the shore have recently been approved.
exercises.explanation: Boşluktan sonraki ‘As a result, far less fresh water reaches the lake’ cümlesi bir neden bekler; Ürdün Nehri’nin sularının yukarıda tarım ve içme suyu için kullanılması bu nedeni verir: ‘This is mainly because the River Jordan, its main source, is heavily used upstream …’. Tuzluluk ve yüzme (‘swimmers’), turistler (‘ancient times’), çamur satışı (‘beauty product’) ve otel planları (‘hotels’) gölün küçülmesini ve tatlı su azalmasını açıklamaz.

exercises.passage: The QWERTY keyboard layout, named after the first six letters on its top row, was developed for typewriters in the 1870s. A popular explanation is that the letters were arranged so that the metal bars of early machines would not strike each other and get stuck. ---- Nevertheless, once millions of people had learned to type on QWERTY, changing the layout became almost impossible, and it survived the move from typewriters to computers.
exercises.question: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Over the following century, several alternative layouts were designed that were claimed to make typing faster and less tiring.
Modern computers can be connected to more than one keyboard at the same time.
Most typists in the nineteenth century were young women working in offices.
The metal bars of these early machines were usually made by hand.
Many people today type on their phones with only two thumbs.
exercises.explanation: Boşluktan sonraki ‘Nevertheless’ bir zıtlık bekler: daha hızlı alternatif düzenler tasarlanmış, buna rağmen QWERTY değiştirilememiştir: ‘Over the following century, several alternative layouts were designed …’. Birden çok klavye bağlama (‘connected’), daktilocuların kimliği (‘young women’), metal çubukların el yapımı olması (‘made by hand’) ve telefonda iki başparmakla yazma (‘thumbs’) ‘Nevertheless’ ile kurulan zıtlığı hazırlamaz.

exercises.passage: (I) Mangrove forests grow along tropical coastlines, where their dense roots trap mud and hold the shore in place. (II) During storms, these roots reduce the height and energy of waves before they reach the land behind them. (III) Studies carried out after the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami suggested that villages sheltered by healthy mangroves often suffered less damage than exposed ones. (IV) For this reason, a growing number of governments now regard planting mangroves as a cheaper alternative to building concrete sea walls. (V) Mangrove wood is hard and resistant to decay, so it has long been used to build houses and boats.
exercises.question: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
exercises.explanation: Paragraf mangrovların kıyıları dalgalara ve fırtınalara karşı nasıl koruduğunu anlatır. ‘V’ numaralı cümle de mangrovlardan söz eder ama koruma işlevinden ayrılıp odunun ev ve tekne yapımında kullanılmasına geçer. ‘I’ köklerin kıyıyı tuttuğunu, ‘II’ dalgaları zayıflattığını, ‘III’ tsunami sonrası kanıtı verir; ‘IV’ ise ‘For this reason’ ile bu koruma işlevinden çıkan sonucu bildirir.

exercises.passage: (I) Sign languages are not simply visual versions of spoken languages; they have their own grammar and vocabulary. (II) British Sign Language and American Sign Language, for example, are so different that their users cannot easily understand each other, even though English is spoken in both countries. (III) In many sign languages, the position of the hands in space and the expression on the face carry grammatical information, such as whether a sentence is a question. (IV) Learning a sign language as an adult can take several years, and good courses are often expensive. (V) Features like these show that sign languages are complete and independent linguistic systems.
exercises.question: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
exercises.explanation: Paragraf işaret dillerinin kendine özgü dil bilgisi olan bağımsız diller olduğunu savunur. ‘IV’ numaralı cümle yine işaret dilleriyle ilgilidir ama dilin yapısından ayrılıp yetişkinlerin onu öğrenmesinin süresine ve maliyetine geçer; (V) numaralı cümledeki ‘Features like these’ de (II) ve (III) numaralı cümlelerdeki özelliklere bağlanır. ‘I’ savı ortaya koyar, ‘II’ ve ‘III’ örnek verir, ‘V’ sonuca bağlar.

exercises.passage: (I) The Voynich manuscript, a fifteenth-century book of about 240 pages, is written in a script that no one has ever been able to read. (II) The manuscript is now kept in a library at Yale University, where researchers can examine it on request. (III) Over the past century, professional code-breakers, linguists and, more recently, computer scientists have all tried to decipher its text. (IV) Their efforts have been hindered by the fact that the text does not closely resemble any known language or writing system. (V) As a result of these repeated failures, some scholars have suggested that the text may contain no real meaning at all.
exercises.question: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
exercises.explanation: Paragraf Voynich elyazmasının neden çözülemediğini anlatır. ‘II’ numaralı cümle aynı elyazmasından söz eder ama okunamama sorunundan ayrılıp elyazmasının bugün nerede saklandığına geçer; (V) numaralı cümledeki ‘these repeated failures’ ise (III) ve (IV) numaralı cümlelerdeki başarısız çabalara bağlanır. ‘I’ konuyu tanıtır, ‘III’ çabaları, ‘IV’ güçlüğün nedenini anlatır, ‘V’ sonucu verir.

exercises.passage: (I) When the Galaxy Zoo project was launched in 2007, many astronomers doubted whether members of the public could classify images of galaxies accurately. (II) To deal with this concern, each image was shown to many different volunteers, and only the classifications on which most of them agreed were accepted. (III) The website became so popular that its servers struggled to cope with the number of visitors in the first few days. (IV) When these classifications were compared with those made by professional astronomers, the level of agreement turned out to be remarkably high. (V) This evidence of reliability encouraged researchers in other fields to design similar projects, from transcribing old ship records to counting animals in camera photographs.
exercises.question: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
exercises.explanation: Paragraf gönüllülerin yaptığı sınıflandırmaların güvenilirliğinin nasıl sağlandığını ve kanıtlandığını anlatır. ‘III’ numaralı cümle aynı projeyle ilgilidir ama güvenilirlikten ayrılıp sitenin popülerliğine ve sunucu sorunlarına geçer; (IV) numaralı cümledeki ‘these classifications’ de (II) numaralı cümledeki kabul edilen sınıflandırmalara bağlanır. ‘I’ kuşkuyu ortaya koyar, ‘II’ alınan önlemi, ‘IV’ sonucu anlatır, ‘V’ ise bunun etkisini bildirir.
